# Boilerplate

> Boilerplate pairs a Python development environment, one tool for each job, with templates that build on one another to stamp out projects. It takes care of the parts around writing code (a working toolchain and a configured project), so you start at the work.

Boilerplate pairs a Python development environment, one tool for each job, with templates that build on one another to stamp out projects. Each pick is the most modern and lightweight option for its job. These pages describe the tool at its current version. The status page maps what is implemented; the design section describes the target state, not what exists.

# Get started

# Boilerplate

**Boilerplate pairs a Python development environment, one tool for each job, with templates that build on one another to stamp out projects.** Use its templates as they are, or put your own standards on top of one instead of forking it. It renders each template with [Copier](https://copier.readthedocs.io/), a tool for project templates, and you don't need to know Copier to use it.

Boilerplate takes care of the setup chores around writing code, the kind developers call yak shaving: a working toolchain and a configured project. You start at the work.

Each pick is the most modern and lightweight option for its job: uv for installing Python and managing dependencies, Ruff for linting and formatting, Pyright in strict mode for type checking, pytest for testing and VS Code as the editor. The templates configure them in `pyproject.toml` and `.vscode/`, so the editor and the command line format code the same way.

**Less yak. More stack.**

New project, dependencies installed, pytest passing.

The [Quickstart](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/quickstart/index.md) shows the same steps in text.

## Why choose Boilerplate?

- **Instant productivity**

  ______________________________________________________________________

  Scaffold fully configured projects with one command.

- **Locked dependencies**

  ______________________________________________________________________

  `uv.lock` pins the environment, so every machine resolves the same.

- **Toolchain**

  ______________________________________________________________________

  `uv`, `ruff`, and `pytest` arrive preconfigured and ready to go, plus a strict `pyright` configuration checked live via Pylance.

- **Cross-platform**

  ______________________________________________________________________

  Windows 11 installs are automated; Linux/WSL2 and macOS follow the same steps manually.

- **Minimal configuration**

  ______________________________________________________________________

  Defaults from the first render, so there is less setup before you write code.

- **[Template composition](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/templates-hub/composition/index.md)**

  ______________________________________________________________________

  Layer templates with `extends` — one command, one merged question set, deterministic precedence when layers overlap.

Planned

`boilerplate update` — a three-way merge that consumes the lock `boilerplate new` writes to move a generated project to a newer template version — is planned. See the [roadmap](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/roadmap/index.md) for sequencing, the [update model design](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/adr-007-update-model/index.md) for the approach, and [Implementation Status](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/status/index.md) for what exists today.

## Mini quickstart

```powershell
# Install (-ExecutionPolicy Bypass is per-process only)
powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -Command "irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/TheRealBillSiegler/boilerplate/v0.4.0/scripts/install.ps1 | iex"
# Scaffold
boilerplate new project my-first-project
```

With [Git](https://git-scm.com/) and [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/getting-started/installation/) installed:

```bash
uv tool install git+https://github.com/TheRealBillSiegler/boilerplate.git@v0.4.0
boilerplate new project my-first-project
```

Then run `uv run pytest` inside `my-first-project`. The [Quickstart](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/quickstart/index.md) walks every step with expected output, and [Installation](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/install/#setup-options) covers manual setup.

# Why Boilerplate?

Boilerplate takes care of the parts around writing code — a working toolchain and a configured project — so a new Python project starts on one golden path and you start at the work. A golden path is the supported, opinionated way to build one kind of project.

Boilerplate is an ethos made executable: engineering judgment — which tools, how they're configured, how a project is laid out — encoded as software that runs, so a new project inherits the discipline instead of being advised toward it. It is two things at once: a particular Python development environment, and the scaffolder that stamps out projects configured for it.

## Yak shaving

You need one package for the task at hand. That package needs a newer Python. The newer Python needs a PATH fix before it will even run. Three side quests deep, and the actual work hasn't started. The chain has a name — [**yak shaving**](https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/yak_shaving): a prerequisite that hides another prerequisite until the original task is buried under toil that isn't the task.

No single link in that chain is hard. The damage is the pattern — individually tolerable incidents that quietly become an operating model:

- "I'll just copy the last project." "Works on my machine."
- Tool choice debated again for every repository — Ruff or Black, uv or Poetry.
- Onboarding that takes a day before the first test runs.
- A setup README that drifted from what the tooling actually does.

Python itself raises the stakes. The ecosystem ships no equivalent of `npm create` or `dotnet new` — no official starting point for a working project — and the tooling underneath keeps moving: packaging and environment managers compete, get replaced, and leave layers of guidance behind them. Much of what a search turns up teaches techniques the current PEPs have already superseded, and there is no canonical, up-to-date reference project to copy from. Every project works out "modern" for itself, or keeps whichever year's answer its oldest tutorial gave.

**Less yak. More stack.** is the promise to cut that chain down: the environment arrives working, the project arrives configured, and you start at the task itself.

## The ethos

Three opinions the tool executes rather than recommends:

- **Opinionated defaults, visible overrides.** Every pick — uv, Ruff, Pyright strict, pytest — is a default rather than a mandate: template questions, [`profile.toml`](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/customization/index.md), and plain config edits are the sanctioned escape hatches.
- **Automation over documentation.** When a practice matters, it is encoded — in the installer, the template, or the generated config — instead of written into instructions that drift.
- **Legibility before trust.** You can inspect what generation will do before believing it: `boilerplate new --dry-run` shows the render plan — layer order and destination — without writing anything, `boilerplate graph` shows the layers, `boilerplate compose` shows the merged configuration.

## A whole environment, one pick per slot

A development environment is a set of [slots](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/01-overview/#term-slot) — shell, runtime and package manager, linter, type checker, test runner, editor — and most projects fill them one tool at a time, as each need comes up. Boilerplate fills each slot with one opinionated, overridable pick, at three layers:

- **Machine** — the [installer](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/install/index.md) bootstraps the baseline itself: PowerShell 7 (installed first when missing), Git, VS Code with extensions, uv, and the boilerplate CLI. There is no prerequisites section that quietly assumes an hour of setup.
- **Project** — every generated project arrives with a uv-managed, locked environment and Ruff, Pyright strict, and pytest configured in `pyproject.toml`; its example module and test pass those checks on the first run.
- **Editor** — templates ship `.vscode/` settings and extension recommendations, so the editor and the toolchain agree on interpreter, linting, and formatting.

The [environment overview](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/environment/index.md) walks the full toolchain and how the pieces fit. Environment validation is deliberately thin today ([Implementation Status](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/status/index.md)).

## One path, not a repeated conversation

Boilerplate started in 2024 inside a small enablement team, as a way to stop re-explaining the same project setup to every new project. It was research before it was software: a systematic pass over the landscape — package and environment managers, scaffolders, type checkers, test runners — judged against one brief, *the most modern and lightweight in each*, and against what current PEPs actually prescribe. The stack settled late that year, and the tool was built for colleagues from its first mention. The leverage is structural: the judgment gets absorbed once, upstream, and one maintained path replaces the recurring setup conversation.

The tool holds itself to the standard it hands out: this repository's own CI runs the same checks it configures in every generated project — Ruff, Pyright strict, pytest — plus a strict docs build. See [the local check](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/governance/ci/#the-local-check).

One early user described the before-and-after: "before, it was like having your laundry folded — but on the floor. After, it's like sliding the drawer into the dresser: the clothes go in, and it slides friction-free." Another summed up the install as ending in "a fully suped-up Python environment."

## Built on Copier

Boilerplate stands on [Copier](https://copier.readthedocs.io/) rather than reinventing it: Copier does the rendering, prompting, and answers-file bookkeeping, and templates stay standard Copier templates. Composition metadata lives in a separate `boilerplate.yml` beside `copier.yml`; Boilerplate never modifies or replaces your `copier.yml`, and a template becomes a layer by adding that one file.

Boilerplate adds two things on top. The first is the opinions: Copier is deliberately a general-purpose engine — any language, any layout, bring your own templates and your own judgment — while Boilerplate ships [the ethos](#the-ethos) and [the environment](#a-whole-environment-one-pick-per-slot) above as maintained templates and an installer that keep pace with the toolchain and with current standards. Adopting it with a single template and no composition at all still gets you that.

The second is a layer Copier does not provide natively: declared template composition. [Copier's open issue on updatable template hierarchies and reuse](https://github.com/copier-org/copier/issues/934) shows the demand, and a member of the Copier project [wrote there](https://github.com/copier-org/copier/issues/934#issuecomment-2899021408) that a native composition feature might address updating a project whose parent template is applied from a task, where that template's migrations never run, but would need more thinking and probably an actual implementation. Copier's own [multi-template pattern](https://copier.readthedocs.io/en/stable/configuring/#applying-multiple-templates-to-the-same-subproject) works well when templates touch disjoint files; its practical boundary is overlap. When two templates render the same file — `pyproject.toml` is the recurring example ([discussion #1485](https://github.com/orgs/copier-org/discussions/1485)) — there is no merge: Copier prompts per conflicting file, or the last-applied template wins. With Boilerplate, the *template author* declares composition once — `extends: [project]` in the template's `boilerplate.yml` — and `boilerplate new` renders the full layer stack in one command, with one merged question set and deterministic precedence when layers overlap; the [composition guide](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/templates-hub/composition/index.md) covers the mechanics in depth. A [`profile.toml`](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/customization/index.md) pre-fills org answers (your package index, your registry) across the whole catalog without forking templates.

Already using Copier? Your templates keep working unchanged; composition and the curated environment are what's new.

| Use case                                                   | Recommended tool                                                                                                                           |
| ---------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Your own templates, any language, no opinions wanted       | Copier                                                                                                                                     |
| An opinionated, maintained Python environment and scaffold | Boilerplate                                                                                                                                |
| Single custom template, no composition                     | Copier                                                                                                                                     |
| Multiple templates touching disjoint files                 | Copier's [multi-template pattern](https://copier.readthedocs.io/en/stable/configuring/#applying-multiple-templates-to-the-same-subproject) |
| Layered templates with `extends`, overlapping files        | Boilerplate                                                                                                                                |
| One merged question set across layers                      | Boilerplate                                                                                                                                |
| Org-wide default answers without forking templates         | Boilerplate                                                                                                                                |

## Who it's for

Platform teams and template maintainers who own more than one template and want the common foundation defined once — and individuals who want an opinionated, preconfigured Python scaffold without assembling the toolchain themselves.

# Install

Set up Boilerplate and its Python development environment on Windows, macOS, or Linux. Choose your operating system below and follow the steps appropriate to your platform.

Overview

- **Windows 11:** Recommended path with a fully automated installer.
- **Windows 10:** Older builds, and machines without App Installer, have no `winget`. Install PowerShell 7, Git, and VS Code first and then run the installer, or use the manual path.
- **macOS / Linux:** Manual setup.
- Python installation is handled by `uv`; no preinstallation is required.

Do not run bare `pip install boilerplate`

That name is already taken on PyPI by an unrelated, same-niche package — `pip install boilerplate` silently installs *that* package, not this one. Boilerplate is not published to PyPI; use one of the install commands below. See [adr-008](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/adr-008-distribution-name/index.md) for the full mis-install hazard.

## Before you start

- **Python**: nothing to preinstall — `uv` provisions Python for you.
- **Admin rights**: needed only for the `winget` installs — PowerShell 7 when missing, Git, and VS Code.
- **`-ExecutionPolicy Bypass`**: scoped to that one PowerShell process; it does not change your machine's execution policy.

## Setup options

**Run the installer (no repo clone required)** — it works from the stock Windows PowerShell 5.1: it installs PowerShell 7 via winget (if needed) and relaunches itself under it.

```powershell
powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -Command "irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/TheRealBillSiegler/boilerplate/v0.4.0/scripts/install.ps1 | iex"
```

The script sets up the full Python development environment and installs the Boilerplate CLI. It:

- Installs **Git** and **Visual Studio Code** using `winget`, skipping either one that is already installed. Without `winget`, it continues when the `code` and `git` commands are already on PATH, and stops with an error at the first one that is not.
- Installs [the recommended set](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/environment/vscode/#recommended-extensions) of VS Code extensions.
- Installs **uv**, which will install Python and manage the virtual environment.
- Installs the **boilerplate** CLI using `uv tool install git+https://github.com/TheRealBillSiegler/boilerplate.git@v0.4.0`.

No manual PATH edits needed

The script refreshes PATH for this terminal so you can use `uv` and `boilerplate` immediately.

Already have the repo cloned? Run the local script instead.

```powershell
powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File .\scripts\install.ps1
```

1. Install **PowerShell 7+**

   PowerShell 7+ required

   Boilerplate assumes you are using **PowerShell 7+**. The automated path above installs this for you — this step is only needed here, in Manual Setup.

   Verify your PowerShell installation:

   ```powershell
   $PSVersionTable.PSVersion
   ```

   The **Major** version should be **>= 7**.

   [Follow the official PowerShell docs](https://learn.microsoft.com/powershell/scripting/install/installing-powershell), or install via winget:

   ```powershell
   winget install --id Microsoft.PowerShell -e --source winget --accept-source-agreements
   ```

1. Install **Git** — [download for Windows](https://git-scm.com/download/win) and accept the defaults, or install via winget:

   ```powershell
   winget install --id Git.Git -e --source winget --accept-source-agreements
   ```

1. Install **Visual Studio Code** — [download](https://code.visualstudio.com/) and install, or install via winget:

   ```powershell
   winget install --id Microsoft.VisualStudioCode -e --source winget --accept-source-agreements --override '/VERYSILENT /NORESTART /MERGETASKS="!runcode,desktopicon,addcontextmenufiles,addcontextmenufolders,associatewithfiles,addtopath"'
   ```

1. Install **VS Code extensions** Ensure the `code` CLI is on your PATH, then:

   ```powershell
   $exts = @(
       'ms-python.python',
       'ms-toolsai.jupyter',
       'charliermarsh.ruff',
       'esbenp.prettier-vscode',
       'tamasfe.even-better-toml'
   )
   foreach ($e in $exts) {
       code --install-extension $e
   }
   ```

1. Install **uv** Install using the [Windows instructions](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/getting-started/installation/#__tabbed_1_2).

1. Install the **Boilerplate CLI**

   ```powershell
   uv tool install git+https://github.com/TheRealBillSiegler/boilerplate.git@v0.4.0
   ```

Using a private package feed? See the [Customization guide](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/customization/index.md) for the org-adoption pattern.

Under active verification

These macOS/Linux steps are under active verification — please report any issues.

1. Install **Git**

   ```bash
   # macOS
   brew install git
   # Debian / Ubuntu
   sudo apt-get install -y git
   ```

1. Install **Visual Studio Code** Download and install from [code.visualstudio.com](https://code.visualstudio.com/).

1. Install **VS Code extensions** Ensure the `code` CLI is installed (via "Shell Command: Install 'code' command in PATH" in VS Code), then:

   ```bash
   for e in \
       ms-python.python \
       ms-toolsai.jupyter \
       charliermarsh.ruff \
       esbenp.prettier-vscode \
       tamasfe.even-better-toml; do
       code --install-extension "$e"
   done
   ```

1. Install **uv** Install using the [macOS and Linux instructions](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/getting-started/installation/#__tabbed_1_1).

1. Install the **Boilerplate CLI**

   ```bash
   uv tool install git+https://github.com/TheRealBillSiegler/boilerplate.git@v0.4.0
   ```

Using a private package feed? See the [Customization guide](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/customization/index.md) for the org-adoption pattern.

Install the development version instead

The commands above install a release. To try unreleased changes, install the CLI from the `develop` branch:

```bash
uv tool install git+https://github.com/TheRealBillSiegler/boilerplate.git@develop
```

See [Troubleshooting](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/troubleshooting/index.md) if you hit errors during installation.

## Organization adoption

Boilerplate itself ships with public defaults. Organizations customize in two places, both after the canonical install: point **uv** at the org feed (machine configuration), and drop a **`profile.toml`** with the org's generation defaults. See the [Customization guide](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/customization/index.md) for the pattern and a reference script.

## Verify installation

Test your boilerplate installation by getting the version.

```powershell
boilerplate --version
```

Expected: prints a semantic version and exits 0.

Verify the PATH is correct.

```powershell
Get-Command boilerplate
```

Prints a path (often `%USERPROFILE%\.local\bin\boilerplate`) if PATH is correct.

```bash
command -v boilerplate
```

Prints a path (often `~/.local/bin/boilerplate`) if PATH is correct.

Command not found? See [Troubleshooting](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/troubleshooting/index.md) or the [FAQ](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/faq/index.md).

## Update the CLI

To update, pick the newest version in the docs' version selector and run its install command again; uv replaces the installed CLI with that release. `uv tool upgrade boilerplate` does not move a release install, because the install names a fixed tag.

An install from `develop` follows the branch instead: `uv tool upgrade boilerplate` moves it to the branch's latest commit.

# Quickstart

**Less yak. More stack.** Scaffold fully configured, dependency-locked Python projects with **Boilerplate**.

This guide shows you how to:

1. Scaffold your first project
1. Run the dev loop

This guide scaffolds your first project and runs its tests. Install Boilerplate first — [Setup options](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/install/#setup-options) and [Verify installation](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/install/#verify-installation) — and skim the [toolchain](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/environment/#toolchain) it standardizes.

______________________________________________________________________

## Scaffold a new project

Generate a clean, opinionated project structure, accepting every default in one shot:

```bash
boilerplate new project my-first-project --non-interactive
```

Expected: creates my-first-project/ with:

- src/my_first_project/module.py (with an `add(a, b)` function)
- tests/my_first_project/test_module.py (with tests for `add`)
- pyproject.toml, README.md, .vscode/, and notebooks/
- `__init__.py` with a version string
- additional files

Want to set the project name, description, dependencies, and author yourself? Drop `--non-interactive` and answer the 9 prompts interactively (each has a sensible default — press Enter to accept it):

```bash
boilerplate new project my-first-project
```

Building a Streamlit app? Use the Streamlit template:

```bash
boilerplate new streamlit my-streamlit-app
```

Pin to an exact template version when needed (check the current version with `boilerplate list`; the bundled `project` template is currently at `0.3.0`):

```bash
boilerplate new project@0.3.0 my-versioned-project
```

Planned

`boilerplate update` — moving a generated project to a newer template version — is planned; see the [roadmap](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/roadmap/index.md) for sequencing and the [update model design](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/adr-007-update-model/index.md) for the approach.

Non-interactive (accept defaults) and overwrite a non-empty destination:

```bash
boilerplate new project --non-interactive -f my-first-project
```

`--force` / `-f` overwrites without confirmation

If `my-first-project` already exists, `--force` silently overwrites any files the template writes there, without asking first. It does not delete files the template doesn't manage. There is no undo — make sure any file the template will touch doesn't hold work you want to keep.

### Available templates

Boilerplate ships two first-party templates today — see [Choose a template](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/templates-hub/#choose-a-template) for what each one adds and when to reach for it.

______________________________________________________________________

## The dev loop

The dev loop is the cycle you repeat inside a project; the [Development Environment guide](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/environment/#the-dev-loop) covers it in full.

1. **Enter the project directory**

   ```bash
   cd my-first-project
   ```

1. **Add a dependency**

   ```bash
   uv add pandas pydantic
   ```

   Tip

   Add `--dev` for a development-only dependency.

1. **Open the project in VS Code**

   ```bash
   code .
   ```

   Or: VS Code → File → Open Folder → select my-first-project

1. **Run tests**

   ```bash
   uv run pytest
   ```

   Tip

   Use `-q` for quiet; Use `-vv` for detailed diagnostics.

   Expected: tests run; all passed; exit 0.

# Implementation Status

This page tracks how much of Boilerplate's [design specification](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/01-overview/index.md) is actually implemented in code today. It is maintained by hand: a feature is marked **Implemented** only when code backs it, and usually tests too.

The design docs describe the full target system; this page lists which parts are Implemented, Partial or Planned.

**Legend:** Implemented · Partial · Planned (design-only)

## At a glance

The implemented core is **local template composition**: discover templates from local directories, resolve an `extends` graph, merge their configuration and question schemas, and render through Copier. That pipeline ships end to end and is covered by the test suite, but several of design 04's contracts are still open (graph limits, the `run_worker` contract), so the area is rated Partial below. Beyond the core, two customization mechanisms ship: an env/`.env`-driven `Settings` object (three of design 09's ten Settings fields, plus two code-only extras) and the per-user **profile** (`profile.toml`); the earlier typed Profile model, its resolution chain, and the `boilerplate config` command were retired in favor of the profile. Reproducibility and lifecycle are partial: `new` writes `boilerplate.lock`, and the per-layer update and add engines (three-way merge, migration records) are implemented but driven only by tests, with no command wired to them. *Catalog federation* (remote/Git sources, trust tiers, search) and the *environment-provisioning subsystem* are design-only.

| Design area                                                                                                                         | Status  |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------- |
| [01 — Overview / architecture](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/01-overview/index.md)                    | Partial |
| [02 — Data models](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/02-data-models/index.md)                             | Partial |
| [03 — Template system](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/03-template-system/index.md)                     | Partial |
| [04 — Composition engine](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/04-composition-engine/index.md)               | Partial |
| [05 — CLI reference](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/05-cli-reference/index.md)                         | Partial |
| [06 — Project lifecycle](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/06-project-lifecycle/index.md)                 | Partial |
| [07 — Operational quality](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/07-operational-quality/index.md)             | Partial |
| [08 — Environment provisioning](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/08-environment-provisioning/index.md)   | Planned |
| [09 — Settings & configuration](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/09-settings-and-configuration/index.md) | Partial |
| [10 — Security](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/10-security/index.md)                                   | Partial |

## Detailed status

### 01 — Overview / architecture Partial

- **Implemented:** Service split: resolver / composer / render engine as independent, wired classes
- **Partial:** Atomic / no-partial-output rendering — render is a sequential per-layer overlay with no transactional rollback, so a mid-render failure can leave partial output
- **Partial:** Pluggable repository abstraction — the ABC exists, but only the directory repository is implemented

### 02 — Data models Partial

- **Implemented:** `TemplateMeta`, `TemplateInfo`, `TemplateSpecifier`, `SerializableVersion`, `TemplateCatalog`
- **Partial:** `BoilerplateLock`, `LockLayer` and `MigrationRecord` (`models/`) — implemented; `new` writes the lock, and the update and add engines append migration records, driven only by tests

### 03 — Template system Partial

- **Implemented:** Local template discovery across multiple directory roots (`catalog/`, `repository/directory_repository.py`)
- **Implemented:** `extends`-based layering and topological composition
- **Implemented:** Bundled Jinja extensions and the `project` / `streamlit` scaffold templates
- **Planned:** Catalog federation, remote/Git sources, classification, and trust/verification levels — catalog is local-only; a Git-backed repository remains unimplemented, with no stub in code — `build_template_catalog` (`cli/utils.py`) constructs only the directory repository

### 04 — Composition engine Partial

The most mature area. The resolution → graph → merge → render pipeline works end to end and is heavily tested; the gaps are specific design 04 contracts, not missing pipeline stages.

- **Implemented:** Resolution, graph ordering, and composition (`composition/resolution/`, `composition/graph/`, `composition/composer.py`) — ordering is deterministic: siblings follow `extends` declaration order, with lexicographic order only across independent roots (design 04 Stage 2)
- **Implemented:** Config & question-schema merging — deep-merge of questions, dicts, and tasks, with dedicated strategies for `_jinja_extensions` (union) and `_min_copier_version` (highest wins) (`composition/merging/`). Note: this is *configuration-layer* merging, not file-level three-way merge.
- **Implemented:** Composition serialization to YAML/JSON (`composition/serialization/`)
- **Implemented:** Cycle detection and merge-conflict errors (`composition/graph/exceptions.py`, `composition/merging/exceptions.py`)
- **Implemented:** Version-conflict detection — an `extends` diamond that pins the same template name at two different versions is rejected during resolution, raising `VersionConflictError` with error code `BP_RESOLVE_VERSION_CONFLICT` (design 04 Stage 1) (`composition/resolution/resolver.py`, `composition/graph/exceptions.py`)
- **Planned:** Graph size/depth limits — `BP_GRAPH_*` covers cycles only
- **Partial:** `CopierWorker` abstraction — the `Worker` subclass ships as `ScopedWorker`, and composition renders and updates through it (`composition/rendering/scoped_worker.py`); the `run_worker` / `WorkerResult` contract and the startup `BP_COPIER_COMPAT_FAILED` check are not built
- **Implemented:** Per-layer answers files — each bundled template declares `_answers_file: .copier-answers.<layer>.yml` and ships the answers-file stub; Copier writes one per layer natively during that layer's render, and no canonical `.copier-answers.yml` is written (design 04's per-layer `_answers_file:` contract, the foundation for per-layer update)
- **Implemented:** Scoped rendering — `boilerplate new` asks the merged questionnaire once, then renders each layer under its scoped view (the questions and extensions of that layer and its ancestors), so each answers file records only its own scope; ancestors' file-path extensions load for the descendants that use them (`composition/rendering/engine.py`, `composition/views/`)

The questionnaire pass sees the merged `_jinja_extensions` union (see [What gets merged](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/reference/merging/#what-gets-merged)), so a question default can use any layer's filter instead of crashing; the merged tasks run once, on the last layer.

### 05 — CLI reference Partial

See the [command table](#cli-specified-vs-implemented) below for the specified-vs-implemented command areas.

- **Implemented:** Global options (`--verbose/--quiet/--color/--ci/--version`) and Typer's own did-you-mean on a mistyped command
- **Implemented:** The banner above the top-level help — the braille logo beside the name, the name alone where the logo can't show, and its opt-outs (`cli/display/banner.py`, `cli/display/terminal_probe.py`)
- **Planned:** Design 05's confirmation contracts (plan-then-prompt for mutating commands) — no code; sequencing in the [backlog](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/roadmap/#backlog)

### 06 — Project lifecycle Partial

- **Partial:** Project creation (`new`) — resolves, composes, and renders with `--dry-run`, `--force`, `--non-interactive`, `--no-tasks`, `--data`/`--data-file`, `--format json` (the flag names match design 05's Answer Presets contract except the missing `-d` short flag; `new` rejects `_`-prefixed keys in `--data-file` where the design warns and skips them, and `update` and `add` take no `--data` or `--data-file` yet). It ends by writing `boilerplate.lock` (`composition/rendering/creation_lock.py`).
- **Partial:** Lock-file generation (`boilerplate.lock`) — `new` writes it after a successful render: each layer's name, version, source, commit (null for a bundled folder), checksum, and a hash of each answers file. No command reads it yet
- **Partial:** Project update and layer add — the per-layer update and add engines are implemented (`composition/updating/`, `composition/adding/`) and driven only by tests; the `update` and `add` commands are planned

### 07 — Operational quality Partial

- **Implemented:** Logging via stdlib `logging` — Rich console on TTY; non-TTY / `--ci` stderr gets one strict-JSON object per event with `phase`, `operation`, `request_id`, `success`, and `error_code` on failure, plus `BOILERPLATE_REQUEST_ID` passthrough (`logging_config.py`). Redaction and `duration_ms` terminal events are not implemented.
- **Partial:** Error attribution — a uniform CLI error boundary, exception hierarchy, phase-tagged `BP_{PHASE}_{DESCRIPTOR}` codes, and per-exception remediation hints exist (`cli/utils.py`, `common/exceptions.py`); the `severity` / `retryable` fields are declared but hardcoded (`"error"` / `False`) on every exception and read by nothing yet, and attribution labels and the `--verbose` diagnostic block are not emitted
- **Implemented:** Exit codes — the design's canonical six-value set defined (`constants.py`), with `ACTION_REQUIRED=4` routed in the CLI error boundary (no shipped operation produces exit 4 yet; its first producer is the update conflict pause) and `USER_CANCELLED=130` shipped: Ctrl+C at a prompt exits 130 as clean cancellation
- **Partial:** Advisory locks and the intent journal — implemented (`common/file_lock.py`, `composition/staging/`) and used by the update and add engines, driven only by tests
- **Planned:** Metrics, performance budgets, retry policy, automation gates, and atomic staged writes for `new`

### 08 — Environment provisioning Planned

Design-only. There is no proto/toolchain code, no `.prototools`/`.protolock` generation, and no `env` command group. (The profile covers package index and container registry values — not toolchain versions or provisioning.)

### 09 — Settings & configuration Partial

Two mechanisms ship, both tested: an env-driven `Settings` object and the per-user **profile** (`profile.toml`). The rest of design 09's surface (the full `Settings` field set, catalog source config, revocation file) is not yet built. The typed `Profile` model, its resolution chain, and the `boilerplate config` command group were **retired** in the template-customization redesign; named default sets and a repurposed `config` command are designed but deferred.

- **Implemented:** `Settings` object loaded at every CLI startup — `BOILERPLATE_`-prefixed env vars and `.env`; ships five fields: three of design 09's ten (`default_templates_dir` and `extra_template_dirs` drive template-directory resolution, `debug` drives logging) plus `log_dir` and `file_logging_enabled`, which sit outside design 09's field set and are not consumed yet (`settings/settings.py`)
- **Implemented:** Profile loader: `[defaults]` + `[templates.<name>]` merged from `profile.toml` (`settings/profile.py`)
- **Implemented:** Platform-aware config-root resolution for `profile.toml` (`settings/paths.py`)
- **Planned:** The seven remaining design-09 `Settings` fields (four operation timeouts, `allowed_extension_packages`, `request_id`, `accessible`) and catalog source config (`boilerplate-sources.yml`) — design-only (the revocation file is reserved for Phase 4, not a pending surface)
- **Planned:** Named default sets + a repurposed `config` command to switch between them — designed, deferred
- **Retired** — the strict `Profile` model, the CLI/env/profile/defaults resolution chain, `config show/use/validate`, and the pre-profile migration hint (replaced by `profile.toml`)

### 10 — Security Partial

- **Partial:** YAML safety — boilerplate-owned files load through the shared hardened loader (`common/yaml_loading.py`): safe-load semantics plus duplicate mapping keys as errors and capped alias expansion, per design 03's YAML parsing rules; `copier.yml` parsing is delegated to Copier's own loader; `validate` warns on custom YAML tags in `boilerplate.yml`
- **Partial:** Execution posture — template tasks and Jinja extensions run under Copier's `unsafe` grant, scoped per layer to what that layer's Worker invocation loads (for extensions that is the layer's scoped view, its own and its ancestors' union, and the composition-wide union for the questionnaire pass — see design area 04 above), per the accepted permissive posture in [ADR-003](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/adr-003-permissive-execution/index.md); trust-gated execution is deferred until remote sources ship
- **Planned:** Checksums, signatures, trust verification, and Jinja2 sandbox enforcement — no code exists

| `add`                                | Planned     | Planned; the add engine is implemented and driven only by tests                                                             |

## Known gaps

These are specified in the design docs but no shipped command exercises them — listed here so expectations are clear. Items 2 to 4 have engines implemented and driven only by tests, so they are partial; their commands are not yet wired. The rest are design-only:

1. **Using the lock (`boilerplate.lock`)** — `new` writes it, but no command reads it: there is no `lock verify`, `status` or `update`.
1. **Project update lifecycle** — the per-layer update engine is implemented and driven only by tests; the `update` command is not yet wired, so no shipped command diffs versions or applies an update.
1. **Three-way merge / conflict resolution** — the update engine merges through Copier and pauses on a conflict, driven only by tests; the only merge a shipped command performs is configuration-schema merging. The target semantics (conflict-pause, safe-orphan, never-auto-delete) are specified in [ADR-007](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/adr-007-update-model/index.md).
1. **Migration records & rollback** — the update and add engines append migration records, driven only by tests; no shipped command writes them or exposes a rollback.
1. **Environment provisioning** — the entire proto toolchain subsystem and `env *` commands.
1. **Catalog federation & discovery** — remote/Git sources, `search`, trust tiers, classification.
1. **Security verification pipeline** — checksums, signatures, trust verification, Jinja sandbox.
1. **Operational quality remainder** — metrics, performance budgets, retry policy, and automation gates (advisory locks and the intent journal are partial, above; the phase-tagged error codes and six-value exit taxonomy are shipped; see design area 07 above).
1. **Lifecycle/quality commands** — `status`, `adopt`, `eject`, `doctor`, `test`, `init-template`, `cache warm`.

# Template authoring

Create custom templates for Boilerplate. Templates are directories with two config files: `boilerplate.yml` (metadata for Boilerplate) and `copier.yml` (questions and rendering for Copier).

## Template structure

```text
my-template/
├── boilerplate.yml        # Boilerplate metadata (name, version, extends)
├── copier.yml             # Copier questions, defaults, and tasks
├── README.md.jinja        # Jinja2 template files use .jinja suffix
├── pyproject.toml.jinja
├── _scripts/
│   └── post_generation.py # Referenced by _tasks below
└── src/
    └── {{package_name}}/
        └── __init__.py.jinja
```

## Boilerplate metadata — `boilerplate.yml`

This file tells Boilerplate how to discover, version, and compose your template.

```yaml
# boilerplate.yml
schema_version: "1"       # Metadata schema version

name: my-template          # Used in `boilerplate new my-template`
version: 1.0.0             # PEP 440 — bump when template content changes
description: Short description of what this template scaffolds.

# extends: []              # Optional — list parent templates to inherit from.
#                          # Example: extends: [project]
```

| Field            | Required | Description                                                                          |
| ---------------- | -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `schema_version` | No       | Schema version of `boilerplate.yml`. Defaults to `"1.0"`; `"1"` is the same version. |
| `name`           | Yes      | Template identifier, used in CLI commands.                                           |
| `version`        | Yes      | PEP 440 version string (`boilerplate validate` enforces this).                       |
| `description`    | No       | One-line description shown in `boilerplate list`. Defaults to `""`.                  |
| `extends`        | No       | Parent templates this template layers on top of.                                     |

## Copier configuration — `copier.yml`

This file defines user-facing questions and rendering settings. It follows [Copier's configuration format](https://copier.readthedocs.io/en/stable/configuring/).

```yaml
# copier.yml
_templates_suffix: .jinja

project_name:
  type: str
  help: "The (human-readable) name of the project (e.g. My Project)"
  default: "{{ _folder_name }}"

package_name:
  default: "{{ project_name | replace('-', '_') }}"
  when: false   # Computed, not prompted

description:
  type: str
  help: "A brief description of the project"
  default: "A new Python project."

_tasks:
  - command: ["{{ _copier_python }}", _scripts/post_generation.py]
    when: "{{ _copier_operation == 'copy' }}"
```

The `when` guard limits the task to creation: the script removes itself after it runs, and Copier does not restore a file the project deleted, so the task must not run again on update.

### Key Copier directives

| Directive           | Purpose                                                                                                    |
| ------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `_templates_suffix` | File extension for Jinja2 templates (`.jinja`)                                                             |
| `_exclude`          | Glob patterns to exclude from output                                                                       |
| `_jinja_extensions` | Custom Jinja2 extensions to load                                                                           |
| `_tasks`            | Post-generation commands, run from the generated project root; scripts they call must ship in the template |
| `when: false`       | Hide a question (computed value)                                                                           |

## Template composition

Templates can inherit from other templates using `extends` in `boilerplate.yml`. See the [Composition guide](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/templates-hub/composition/index.md) for merge rules, layer order, and diagnostics commands.

When authoring a child template, its `copier.yml` only needs to declare what it overrides or adds — not the full parent config:

```yaml
# streamlit/copier.yml
dependencies:
  default: ["streamlit", "pydantic>=2"]
```

Declare `_answers_file: .copier-answers.<layer>.yml` in `copier.yml` and ship an answers-file stub — a template file literally named `{{ _copier_conf.answers_file }}.jinja` rendering `_copier_answers` (see `project`'s stub for the reference pattern). Copier writes an answers file only by rendering that stub; the directive alone is inert, and `boilerplate validate` warns when a composition-intended template (one declaring `_answers_file` or `extends`) ships without it. See the [Composition guide § Layer order](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/templates-hub/composition/#layer-order) for what each layer's answers file records.

## Template files

Use Jinja2 syntax with the `.jinja` suffix:

```python
# src/{{package_name}}/__init__.py.jinja
"""{{ project_name }} — {{ description }}."""

__version__ = "0.1.0"
```

Directory names can also use Jinja2 variables: `{{package_name}}/` expands to the value of the `package_name` question.

## Best practices

- **Two config files**: `boilerplate.yml` for Boilerplate, `copier.yml` for Copier. Keep them separate — don't mix concerns.
- **Restate Copier's defaults in `_exclude`.** A declared `_exclude` replaces Copier's built-in list (`.git`, `copier.yml`, `__pycache__`, …) instead of extending it. Copy the bundled templates' block, which also excludes `boilerplate.yml`; otherwise a `copier update` from a git clone copies the clone's `.git` over the project's.
- **Sensible defaults** for all questions so `--non-interactive` works.
- **Use `extends`** to layer on base templates rather than duplicating files.
- **Version your templates** with PEP 440 versions (plain `X.Y.Z` works). The version moves once per release, not once per change — see [when to bump](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/templates-hub/versioning/#when-to-bump).
- **Point the CLI at your template**: custom templates live outside the bundled templates directory, so point the CLI at the directory *containing* `my-template/` with `--templates-dir` (works on `new`, `list`, `graph`, and `compose`; it adds to the search path, so bundled parents stay resolvable for `extends`) or set it persistently via [`BOILERPLATE_EXTRA_TEMPLATE_DIRS`](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/customization/#layers-structure).
- **Test rendering** with `boilerplate new my-template test-output --force --templates-dir <parent-dir>`.
- **Inspect composition** with `boilerplate compose` and `boilerplate graph` before publishing multi-layer templates.

## Keeping a project's work

A project generated from your template is a git repository, and `copier update` reads it as one: it refuses a dirty tree, diffs against the index, and merges through it. Anything outside that index is invisible to the merge. Three habits follow; the rules themselves are in [Template versioning](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/templates-hub/versioning/#authoring-rules).

### Rename through a staged move

Copier deletes every path your new version stops rendering, by name, without comparing content — so a project that edited the old file loses the edit, at exit 0, with nothing in the working tree to show it. A `before`-stage migration that moves *and stages* the file turns that deletion into a conflict carrying both versions:

```yaml
# copier.yml
_migrations:
  - when: "{{ _stage == 'before' }}"
    command:
      - "{{ _copier_python }}"
      - -c
      - |
        import pathlib
        import subprocess

        old = pathlib.Path("tests/smoke_test.py")
        new = old.with_name("test_smoke.py")
        if old.exists() and not new.exists():
            subprocess.run(["git", "mv", str(old), str(new)], check=True)
```

The entry declares no `version`, so Copier runs it on every update; the state check makes it a no-op once the old name is gone. Ship it in the same change as the rename, with a test that drives a real `copier update` from the previous tag — `tests/boilerplate/templates/test_streamlit_update_migration.py` in this repository is the worked example.

### Render nothing your `.gitignore` matches

An ignored file never enters the index, so the merge cannot see it: no conflict marker, no `.rej` file, nothing in history to recover. The reverse holds too — do not ignore a file your README tells the user to commit.

### Say who owns each file

A file your template keeps changing is template-owned: a project that edits it risks a conflict whenever a release touches the same lines, and on a file small enough that one diff hunk spans it, any release at all. A file the project should own after the first render belongs in `_skip_if_exists`; what the list does, and where it applies, is specified in the [Per-Layer Render Loop](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/04-composition-engine/#per-layer-render-loop). Choose per file and say which; silence means template-owned. A file meant to be deleted (a sample module) stays template-owned; project-owned is for the files users are expected to keep and rewrite instead, like the README or the entry point. Both bundled templates' `copier.yml` declare that split.

## Bundled examples

The bundled templates serve as working examples:

- **`project`** — the general-purpose Python template ([project template source](https://github.com/TheRealBillSiegler/boilerplate/tree/main/src/boilerplate/templates/project))
- **`streamlit`** — a template for Streamlit apps, built on `project` ([streamlit template source](https://github.com/TheRealBillSiegler/boilerplate/tree/main/src/boilerplate/templates/streamlit))

Run `boilerplate list` to see all available templates.

## Where next

See the [Composition guide](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/templates-hub/composition/index.md) for merge semantics, or the [Templates Hub](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/templates-hub/index.md) to browse bundled templates.

# Template composition

Composition lets one template build on another through an `extends` list in its `boilerplate.yml`. It reduces duplication and keeps shared conventions centralized.

## Extending a template

`boilerplate.yml` excerpt from the Streamlit template:

```yaml
name: streamlit
version: 0.2.0
description: A Streamlit app, built on the general-purpose template.
extends:
  - project
```

Rules:

1. A parent must be discoverable by name via `boilerplate list`.
1. Multiple parents are supported. Siblings are processed in `extends` declaration order, deterministically; later-declared siblings render later and take precedence on conflicts.

Before you extend

- Lists merge by union only — inherited entries can't be removed or reordered, so design list-type questions to be purely additive.
- Dict questions overlay shallowly — a child overriding one key inside a nested structure replaces the whole structure at that level, not just that key — keep nested config shallow or split it into flat keys.
- File conflicts aren't diagnosed — if a child writes a path the parent also writes, the child's version wins silently, with no warning — diff the output after generation.

Planned

Version-pinned `extends` constraints (`parent@>=1.2`) and file-conflict reporting (`compose --conflicts`) are tracked on the [roadmap backlog](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/roadmap/#backlog).

## Concepts

| Term                 | Meaning                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| -------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Base template        | A template that does not declare parents, e.g., `project`.                                                                                                                                                |
| Derived template     | A template that declares one or more parents via `extends`, e.g., `streamlit`.                                                                                                                            |
| Layer                | One template's contribution at a node of the dependency graph: name@version plus its path; see the [glossary entry](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/01-overview/#term-layer). |
| Layer order          | The order the layers apply (dependencies first, target last).                                                                                                                                             |
| Dependency graph     | Nodes, edges, and the layer order describing template dependencies.                                                                                                                                       |
| Merged configuration | The merged configuration after all layers; a questions-only view is also available.                                                                                                                       |
| Delta                | Per-layer change set: subset of keys this layer adds or overrides relative to previous state.                                                                                                             |

Concept → class: a layer is `CompositionLayer` and its changes are `CompositionLayer.delta`; the sequence and graph are `Composition.sequence` and `CompositionGraph`; the merged configuration is `Composition.final`, with `Composition.merged_questions_schema` as the questions-only view; templates are `TemplateInfo` with parents in `TemplateMeta.extends`. Field-level detail: [Data models § Composition Domain Models](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/02-data-models/#composition-domain-models).

## Layer order

Layering supports multiple parents (a dependency graph) and always executes linearized, dependencies first and the target template last; sibling ordering and conflict precedence follow the rules under [Extending a template](#extending-a-template) above.

Run:

```powershell
uv run boilerplate graph streamlit
```

Output (abridged):

```text
#   Layer       Version   Path
1   project     0.3.0     .../templates/project
2   streamlit   0.2.0     .../templates/streamlit
```

Layers apply in this order: each layer's question schema and internal directives (`_jinja_extensions`, `_tasks`) merge into the accumulated result. See [CLI examples § Inspect a template graph](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/cli-examples/#inspect-a-template-graph) for the full `--format json` payload.

A layer's `copier.yml` declares its own questions and the parent questions it overrides; its ancestors' questions supply every other answer its files and paths use. `streamlit` declares `container_registry` and overrides `dependencies` and `sample_module`, and its files render `project_name`, `project_slug`, `package_name`, `description`, `author_name`, `author_email` and `package_index_url` from `project`'s declarations without restating them. Each layer's own `.copier-answers.<layer>.yml` records the answers to that layer's own questions and its ancestors', and nothing of a sibling or a descendant: `project`'s file lacks `container_registry`, `streamlit`'s has both. `boilerplate new` asks the merged questionnaire once, so you answer each question a single time. See the [Authoring guide](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/templates-hub/authoring/#template-composition) for the `_answers_file` how-to. Because each file is Copier's own, you can also [compose and update with plain Copier](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/templates-hub/plain-copier/index.md).

## Merge & delta semantics

Show the full composition:

```powershell
uv run boilerplate compose streamlit --all --format yaml
```

Merge strategies are a fixed set — per question type under [What gets merged](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/reference/merging/#what-gets-merged), per directive key under [Allowlisted directive keys](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/reference/merging/#allowlisted-directive-keys-and-strategies) — with no way to declare a per-field strategy. Incompatible types for the same question raise `BP_RESOLVE_MERGE_CONFLICT`; see [Determinism and conflict handling](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/reference/merging/#determinism-and-conflict-handling).

## Diagnostics toolkit

| Command                                           | Purpose                           | Typical Use                 |
| ------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------- | --------------------------- |
| `boilerplate list`                                | Discover available templates      | Verify parent existence     |
| `boilerplate graph streamlit`                     | View ordered layers               | Confirm inheritance chain   |
| `boilerplate compose streamlit --stats`           | High-level metrics (layers, keys) | Sanity check complexity     |
| `boilerplate compose streamlit --sections deltas` | Show per-layer differences        | Author focus when extending |
| `boilerplate compose <tpl> --all --format yaml`   | Full introspection                | Deep troubleshooting        |

## Worked example

Goal: Add a Streamlit UI to any standard project without duplicating base scaffolding.

What the streamlit layer contributes:

| Category             | Added Value                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| -------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Runtime Dependencies | `streamlit`, `pydantic>=2`                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| App Entry Point      | `app.py`, reading the project's own `uv.lock` and rendering it as a stack inventory                                                                                                                          |
| Domain Structure     | `models/`, `services/`, and `adapters/` packages encouraging separation                                                                                                                                      |
| Containerization     | `Dockerfile`, container scripts (build/push)                                                                                                                                                                 |
| Developer Experience | VS Code `launch.json` for F5 debugging                                                                                                                                                                       |
| Tests                | A unit test module per layer (`test_locked_package.py`, `test_stack_filter.py`, `test_lockfile.py`, `test_inventory.py`) plus an integration test (`tests/integration/{{ package_name }}/test_app.py.jinja`) |

Because the schema changes are contained (`dependencies` and `sample_module` overrides plus the new `container_registry` prompt), all other prompts remain aligned with the base template—no redundant customization logic.

Observed example specifics for the Streamlit chain:

| Aspect              | Observed                          | Explanation                                                                                                                                                                   |
| ------------------- | --------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `dependencies` list | Default replaced with two entries | Base declares `dependencies` with an empty default; the child question dict shallow-overrides it, so `default` becomes the child's list while `type` and `help` are inherited |
| Absent questions    | Inherited unchanged               | Values simply flow through cumulative state                                                                                                                                   |
| `_tasks`            | Single task from base only        | Child adds none; accumulation == base list                                                                                                                                    |
| `_jinja_extensions` | Three entries (all from base)     | Child declares two, both duplicates of base entries, so union == base list                                                                                                    |

Delta for `streamlit` layer (excerpt):

```yaml
dependencies:
  default:
    - streamlit
    - pydantic>=2
```

Interpretation: the streamlit layer overrides the `dependencies` and `sample_module` defaults and adds one new question, `container_registry` (type `str`, default `ghcr.io`). (`_tasks` never appears in deltas or per-layer values; inspect the accumulated task list in the merged configuration, e.g. `--sections final`.)

File system overlay (illustrative):

| Origin    | Files (examples)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| --------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| project   | `pyproject.toml.jinja`, `README.md.jinja`, `src/{{ package_name }}/__init__.py.jinja`, base test scaffold                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| streamlit | `README.md.jinja` (overrides project's), `src/{{ package_name }}/app.py.jinja`, `src/{{ package_name }}/adapters/lockfile.py.jinja`, `src/{{ package_name }}/models/locked_package.py.jinja`, `src/{{ package_name }}/services/inventory.py.jinja`, `Dockerfile.jinja`, `.vscode/launch.json.jinja`, integration test |

File overlay follows [last-layer-wins semantics](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/reference/merging/#file-overlay); the streamlit layer overrides two project paths, `README.md.jinja` and `.gitattributes`, so those render from the streamlit layer; every other streamlit path is new.

## Author checklist

Recommended workflow:

1. Start from base: design only the deltas you truly need.
1. After edits, run `compose --sections deltas` to ensure minimal surface area.
1. If you added conflicting files, explicitly note the rationale in your template README.

Before publishing:

```text
☐ Parent template listed by `boilerplate list`
☐ Only required deltas introduced (verify with --sections deltas)
☐ New files do not duplicate or fork base files without reason
☐ Dependencies kept minimal and scoped to added functionality
☐ Launch/debug assets only when necessary
```
