- [Commands](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/cli/index.md) — the full CLI reference.

# Boilerplate CLI reference

Use the Boilerplate CLI to scaffold projects, inspect compositions, and list templates. See also [CLI Examples](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/cli-examples/index.md) for common workflows.

## boilerplate

Pairs a Python development environment, one tool for each job, with templates that build on one another to stamp out projects.

Get started:

```text
boilerplate list
boilerplate new project my-app
boilerplate new streamlit my-dashboard
```

Usage:

```text
boilerplate [OPTIONS] COMMAND [ARGS]...
```

Options:

```text
  -v, --verbose                Enable debug logging.
  -q, --quiet                  Hide the banner and progress, success, and hint
                               messages.
  --color <auto|always|never>  Color output.  [default: auto]
  --ci                         Never prompt and log JSON to stderr. Implies
                               --non-interactive on new.
  --version                    Show version and exit.
  --install-completion         Install completion for the current shell.
  --show-completion            Show completion for the current shell, to copy
                               it or customize the installation.
```

### compose

Show the merged configuration a template composes, layer by layer.

- final: the fully merged configuration
- layers: each layer's own values
- states: each layer's configuration after it applies
- deltas: what each layer changed
- stats: summary counts

Prints to stdout by default. --output writes each section to a file in a directory.

Usage:

```text
boilerplate compose [OPTIONS] {template}
```

Options:

```text
  template                Template to use (name or name@version).  [required]
  --sections <str>        Sections to show, comma-separated: final, layers,
                          states, deltas, stats.
  --all                   Show every section.
  --stats                 Show only the summary.
  --format <yaml|json>    Output format.  [default: yaml]
  -o, --output <path>     Directory to write the sections into.
  --quiet                 Print nothing to stdout; pair with --output to only
                          write files.
  --templates-dir <path>  Extra directory to search for templates, in addition
                          to the bundled ones.
```

### graph

Show the layers a template is built from, in the order they apply.

Visualizes template dependencies in three formats:

- table: numbered list with each layer's path
- tree: which template extends which
- json: the same data for tools

Usage:

```text
boilerplate graph [OPTIONS] {template}
```

Options:

```text
  template                    Template to use (name or name@version).
                              [required]
  --templates-dir <path>      Extra directory to search for templates, in
                              addition to the bundled ones.
  --format <table|tree|json>  Output format.  [default: table]
  -o, --output <path>         Write the JSON to this file instead of stdout.
```

### list

List the templates you can create a project from.

Usage:

```text
boilerplate list [OPTIONS]
```

Options:

```text
  --templates-dir <path>      Extra directory to search for templates, in
                              addition to the bundled ones.
  --format <table|json|wide>  Output format.  [default: table]
```

### new

Create a new project from a template.

Usage:

```text
boilerplate new [OPTIONS] {template_spec} [destination]
```

Options:

```text
  template_spec           Template to use (name or name@version).  [required]
  destination             Destination directory. Required unless a terminal
                          can prompt for it.
  -f, --force             Overwrite a non-empty destination. Does not imply
                          --non-interactive.
  --non-interactive       Use defaults without prompting; fail when a required
                          question has none.
  -n, --dry-run           Show the layers and destination without writing any
                          files.
  --no-tasks              Skip the template's post-creation tasks.
  --data <str>            Answer for one question, as key=value. May be
                          repeated.
  --data-file <path>      YAML file of question: answer pairs (UTF-8).
  --format <text|json>    Output format.  [default: text]
  --templates-dir <path>  Extra directory to search for templates, in addition
                          to the bundled ones.
```

### validate

Check that a template directory is well-formed.

Usage:

```text
boilerplate validate [OPTIONS] {template_dir}
```

Options:

```text
  template_dir          Path to the template directory to validate.
                        [required]
  --format <text|json>  Output format.  [default: text]
  --strict              Treat warnings as errors.
```

## Option notes

| Option               | Note                                                                                                                                                                 |
| -------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--color auto`       | Colors stdout and stderr independently, each only when that stream is itself a terminal; turns color off on both when `NO_COLOR` or `BOILERPLATE_ACCESSIBLE` is set. |
| `list --format wide` | Adds each template's path as a column.                                                                                                                               |
| `new --format json`  | One JSON object with `template`, `destination`, and `layers`; `--dry-run` adds `dry_run: true`.                                                                      |

## Shell completion

Tab completion for commands and options is built in. Run this once from the shell you want it in, then restart the terminal:

```bash
boilerplate --install-completion
```

The CLI detects your shell and supports bash, zsh, fish, and PowerShell (Windows PowerShell and PowerShell 7). Installing writes to your home directory:

| Shell      | What `--install-completion` writes                                                                                         |
| ---------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| bash       | `~/.bash_completions/boilerplate.sh`, sourced from `~/.bashrc`                                                             |
| zsh        | `~/.zfunc/_boilerplate`, plus `fpath` and `compinit` lines in `~/.zshrc`                                                   |
| fish       | `~/.config/fish/completions/boilerplate.fish`                                                                              |
| PowerShell | The completion script, appended to your PowerShell profile; also sets the `CurrentUser` execution policy to `Unrestricted` |

To read the script before installing it, or to place it yourself, print it for the detected shell:

```bash
boilerplate --show-completion
```

Completion covers command and option names; template names are not completed.

## Environment variables

Every environment variable the CLI reads. The generic `CI` variable is never read — only the `BOILERPLATE_`-prefixed flags below switch modes. `BOILERPLATE_CI`, `BOILERPLATE_NON_INTERACTIVE`, `BOILERPLATE_ACCESSIBLE`, and `BOILERPLATE_NO_BANNER` are on for any value except unset, empty, `0`, or `false` (case-insensitive); `NO_COLOR` is on by mere presence, any value included; the `Settings`-parsed variables below accept `1/0`, `true/false`, `yes/no`, `on/off`, and exit 2 (CONFIG_ERROR) on anything else. The `Settings` variables are also read from a `.env` file in the working directory. `PYTHONIOENCODING` is forced to `utf-8` while a template renders and restored afterward — it's not read as a setting.

| Variable                                                  | Effect                                                                                                                                                                            | Where it's read                                                          |
| --------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `BOILERPLATE_CI`                                          | Same as the global `--ci` flag: forces CI mode (non-interactive; post-generation tasks still run unless `--no-tasks` is passed) and one-JSON-object-per-event logs on stderr.     | `boilerplate.cli.cli`                                                    |
| `BOILERPLATE_NON_INTERACTIVE`                             | Same as `boilerplate new --non-interactive`: renders without prompting.                                                                                                           | `boilerplate.cli.commands.new`                                           |
| `BOILERPLATE_ACCESSIBLE`                                  | Same as `--color never` (forces color-free output), and hides the banner.                                                                                                         | `boilerplate.cli.display.core`, `boilerplate.cli.display.terminal_probe` |
| `BOILERPLATE_NO_BANNER`                                   | Hides the banner: the braille logo and ASCII name that open the top-level help.                                                                                                   | `boilerplate.cli.display.terminal_probe`                                 |
| `TERM`                                                    | `dumb` or `unknown` hides the banner; `linux` (the Linux text console) prints its name without the braille logo.                                                                  | `boilerplate.cli.display.terminal_probe`                                 |
| `NO_COLOR`                                                | The standard color-disable convention; disables console color, prints the banner's name without its braille logo, and switches log output from Rich to one JSON object per event. | `boilerplate.cli.display.core`, `boilerplate.logging_config`             |
| `BOILERPLATE_DEBUG`                                       | Same as `--verbose` when `--verbose` isn't passed: sets DEBUG-level logging.                                                                                                      | `boilerplate.settings.Settings`, applied in `boilerplate.cli.cli`        |
| `BOILERPLATE_REQUEST_ID`                                  | Correlation ID attached to every structured log line for the invocation; auto-generated once per run when unset.                                                                  | `boilerplate.logging_config`                                             |
| `BOILERPLATE_DEFAULT_TEMPLATES_DIR`                       | Overrides the bundled templates directory searched first.                                                                                                                         | `boilerplate.settings.Settings`                                          |
| `BOILERPLATE_EXTRA_TEMPLATE_DIRS`                         | Adds directories searched after the default, as a JSON array: `["C:/tpls","D:/more"]`.                                                                                            | `boilerplate.settings.Settings`                                          |
| `BOILERPLATE_LOG_DIR`, `BOILERPLATE_FILE_LOGGING_ENABLED` | Parsed and validated at startup (an invalid value exits 2); no command consumes them yet.                                                                                         | `boilerplate.settings.Settings`                                          |
| `APPDATA`                                                 | Locates the config directory holding `profile.toml` on Windows (`%APPDATA%\boilerplate\`).                                                                                        | `boilerplate.settings.paths`                                             |
| `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`                                         | Locates the config directory holding `profile.toml` on POSIX (`$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/boilerplate/`, falling back to `~/.config/boilerplate/`).                                         | `boilerplate.settings.paths`                                             |

## Exit codes

Every command exits with one of six codes (defined in `boilerplate.constants.ExitCode`):

| Code | Name             | Meaning                                                                                                                                                                            |
| ---- | ---------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 0    | SUCCESS          | Command completed.                                                                                                                                                                 |
| 1    | FAILURE          | Unexpected error.                                                                                                                                                                  |
| 2    | CONFIG_ERROR     | Configuration could not be loaded.                                                                                                                                                 |
| 3    | VALIDATION_ERROR | Input failed validation: an unknown command or option, bad answers, a missing interactive terminal (TTY), conflicting options, or a non-empty destination without `--force`.       |
| 4    | ACTION_REQUIRED  | Recoverable pause; user intervention needed. Defined in the taxonomy but not yet produced by any shipped command — its first producer will be the planned `update` conflict pause. |
| 130  | USER_CANCELLED   | Cancelled at a prompt (Ctrl+C).                                                                                                                                                    |

`boilerplate validate <template_dir>` reports a template that fails its own checks (missing or malformed `boilerplate.yml`/`copier.yml`, duplicate keys, schema errors, or a `--strict` warning) on exit code 1 (FAILURE), not 3 — exit 3 there is reserved for a malformed invocation, namely a `template_dir` argument that isn't a directory at all.

## Error codes

Every `BP_*` code in the shipped exception hierarchy. A code the error boundary can render but no command produces is marked as such. The code appears as a bracketed suffix on the `Error:` line (e.g. `[BP_INPUT_DATA_INVALID]`), usually with a `Fix:` line giving the remediation.

| Code                            | When it's raised                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          | Fix                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| ------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `BP_CONFIG_DIR_INVALID`         | A configured template directory — the default templates directory (bundled, or overridden by `BOILERPLATE_DEFAULT_TEMPLATES_DIR`), `--templates-dir`, or a `BOILERPLATE_EXTRA_TEMPLATE_DIRS` entry — doesn't exist, isn't a directory, or can't be read.                                                                                                                                                                  | Point the option or environment variable at a directory that exists and is readable.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `BP_RESOLVE_TEMPLATE_NOT_FOUND` | Defined but not produced by any shipped command; a missing template by name/version surfaces as `BP_RESOLVE_DEP_NOT_FOUND`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               | —                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `BP_VERSION_INVALID`            | Reserved for a version string that fails PEP 440 validation. Defined in the exception hierarchy but not yet produced by any shipped command — an invalid version inside a template reference currently surfaces as `BP_INPUT_SPECIFIER_INVALID` instead.                                                                                                                                                                  | —                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `BP_RENDER_DEST_NOT_EMPTY`      | `boilerplate new` was given a destination directory that already holds files or folders, hidden ones included, without `--force`. Nothing is asked or written.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            | Choose a new or empty directory, or add `--force` to overwrite the files in this one.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `BP_INPUT_FORCE_REQUIRED`       | Defined but not produced by any shipped command.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          | —                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `BP_INPUT_SPECIFIER_INVALID`    | A `name@version` template reference is malformed — an invalid name, or a version segment that isn't PEP 440 compliant, including inside an `extends` reference.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           | Use the format `name` or `name@version`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `BP_RESOLVE_METADATA_INVALID`   | A template's `boilerplate.yml`/`copier.yml` is invalid: schema errors, or a `name@version` tag that disagrees with the directory's declared metadata.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     | Fix the metadata file; `boilerplate validate <template_dir>` reports which check failed.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `BP_INPUT_ANSWERS_MISSING`      | Non-interactive render cannot proceed: a template question has no `default:` and you supplied no value for it. The error message names the specific fields.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               | In priority order: pass `--data key=value` (repeatable, never prompted for) or `--data-file <path>` (a YAML mapping) for the missing answers; or have the template author add a `default:` (ideally computed, e.g. `default: "{{ _folder_name }}"` — see [template authoring](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/templates-hub/authoring/index.md)); or drop `--ci`/`--non-interactive` and answer the prompts. |
| `BP_INPUT_DATA_INVALID`         | `--data`/`--data-file` failed to parse ahead of any render attempt: a `--data` entry with no `=`; an empty or whitespace-only key; a key starting with `_` (Copier's reserved namespace); a `--data-file` path that doesn't exist or isn't UTF-8; content that isn't valid YAML or isn't a mapping; or a data-file key that isn't a string (YAML reads unquoted `on`/`off`/`yes`/`no`/bare numbers as non-string values). | Fix the flag or file and re-run; nothing is rendered when this error fires.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `BP_INPUT_TTY_REQUIRED`         | `boilerplate new` was invoked in interactive mode (the default) but stdin isn't a terminal — typical in CI pipelines, piped input, scripted shells, and `< NUL` redirection on Windows.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   | Pass `--non-interactive` (or the global `--ci`, which precedes the subcommand: `boilerplate --ci new …`), or set [`BOILERPLATE_NON_INTERACTIVE`/`BOILERPLATE_CI`](#environment-variables) once for many call sites; or run from an interactive terminal. `--dry-run` is exempt — it never prompts.                                                                                                                                |
| `BP_INPUT_DEST_REQUIRED`        | `boilerplate new` ran with `--non-interactive` or `--ci` and no destination argument; the current directory is never assumed.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             | Pass the destination as the second argument: `boilerplate new <template> <destination>`. Interactively, the CLI prompts for it.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `BP_RENDER_PROMPT_FAILED`       | Copier's prompt machinery can't display in the current terminal: Git Bash pseudo-TTYs on Windows, Docker entrypoints without `-it`, editor-embedded shells, or Windows CI runners without a real console buffer.                                                                                                                                                                                                          | Run from a real terminal (PowerShell, cmd.exe, a Linux tty, or Docker with `-it`), or pass `--ci` with values that satisfy every question.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `BP_RENDER_USER_CANCELLED`      | You pressed Ctrl+C while `boilerplate new` was showing an interactive prompt; exits `130`, the same code every Ctrl+C in the CLI produces. The render stops without printing collected answers or template paths.                                                                                                                                                                                                         | Re-run `boilerplate new`, or pass `--non-interactive` with answers for every question to skip prompting entirely.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `BP_RESOLVE_DEP_NOT_FOUND`      | An `extends` reference (or a versioned template reference) names a template that can't be resolved in the catalog.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        | Run `boilerplate list` and correct the reference.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `BP_GRAPH_CYCLE`                | The dependency graph formed by `extends` references contains a cycle, including a template that extends itself.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           | Remove the cyclical `extends` reference.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `BP_RESOLVE_VERSION_CONFLICT`   | The same template name resolves to two different versions within one dependency graph.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    | Align all references to a single exact version.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `BP_RESOLVE_MERGE_CONFLICT`     | Layers provide incompatible values for the same question during merge — mismatched types, or no value/version supplied at all.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            | Reconcile the conflicting question across the layers' `copier.yml` files.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `BP_CONFIG_PROFILE_INVALID`     | `profile.toml` exists but isn't valid TOML, or its `[defaults]`/`[templates.<name>]` section isn't a table.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               | Fix the file's TOML syntax or table structure; the error message names the specific section.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |

# Environment

# Development environment

Boilerplate projects include a complete, modern Python development environment. This section documents that [Development Environment](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/01-overview/#term-development-environment) and its parts: the [Toolchain](#toolchain), the [**dev loop**](#the-dev-loop), the [Project Layout](#project-layout), and their [Configuration](#configuration).

## Toolchain

Boilerplate fills each slot the dev loop uses with one preconfigured, overridable tool rather than a menu, and the [toolchain](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/reference/platform/#the-toolchain) lists the picks. They are set up on your machine, in each project and in your editor — see [A whole environment, one pick per slot](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/why/#a-whole-environment-one-pick-per-slot); the [landscape](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/dev-environment-landscape/index.md) holds the full taxonomy.

### uv

**Dependency & environment manager.** An extremely fast package and project manager (written in Rust) that installs and pins Python, manages your virtual environment, and keeps installs reproducible from `pyproject.toml` — day to day, `uv sync`, `uv add <pkg>`, `uv remove <pkg>`. [Official docs](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/)

### Ruff

**Linter & formatter.** One fast tool (also Rust) for both jobs — enforces PEP 8, docstrings, and naming, auto-fixes what it can, and formats on save, so style stays out of your way. [Official docs](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/)

### Pyright

**Type checker.** Catches type errors as you type — live in VS Code via Pylance — so mistakes surface early instead of at runtime. [On GitHub](https://github.com/microsoft/pyright)

### Pytest

**Test runner.** Discovers and runs your tests from the command line or the VS Code Test Explorer, with fixtures, parametrization, and coverage already wired in. [Official docs](https://docs.pytest.org/)

### VS Code

**Editor.** Your workspace, pre-wired so the rest of the toolchain just works — format-on-save, live type hints, and test discovery out of the box. [Setup guide](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/environment/vscode/index.md) [Official docs](https://code.visualstudio.com/docs)

### Git

**Version control.** Tracks your project's history, makes branching and experimentation safe, and syncs with remotes like GitHub. [Official docs](https://git-scm.com/doc)

## The dev loop

The **dev loop** is the cycle you repeat inside a project, which is test-driven development's red-green-refactor: write a failing test, make it pass with the least code, then refactor with the tests still green. Then run the checks, commit, and start the next turn. Steps 1 and 2 get a project ready; steps 3 and 4 are the loop.

### 1. Start or clone a project

**New project**:

```powershell
boilerplate new <template>
```

Add dependencies as you go — `uv add <pkg>`, or `uv add --dev <pkg>` for a development-only dependency.

**Existing project**:

1. Clone the project:

   ```powershell
   git clone <repo>
   ```

1. Synchronize the dependencies:

   ```powershell
   uv sync
   ```

   This installs or updates dependencies based on your `pyproject.toml`.

   To upgrade dependencies:

   ```powershell
   uv sync --upgrade
   ```

### 2. Open VS Code

```powershell
code .
```

Launch a fully configured editor with linting, auto-formatting, type checks, etc.

Warning

Opening a cloned project before `uv sync` can leave VS Code without a detected interpreter — see [the fix](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/environment/vscode/#troubleshooting-the-interpreter-isnt-detected).

### 3. Red, green, refactor

- **Pytest** runs your tests, via the command line or the VS Code Test Explorer. Write a test that fails (red), make it pass with the least code (green), then refactor while it stays green:

  ```powershell
  uv run pytest
  ```

The checks run alongside:

- **Ruff** handles styling and lint checks in real time and formats on save — or run it yourself:

  ```powershell
  uv run ruff format .
  uv run ruff check --fix .
  ```

- **Pyright** highlights type issues as you code — or run it yourself:

  ```powershell
  uv run pyright
  ```

### 4. Commit and repeat

Commit each turn that passes its tests and checks, then start the next one. Many commits make one pull request.

```powershell
git commit
```

## Project layout

A consistent project layout helps everyone understand the codebase at a glance — see [Project structure](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/templates-hub/project/#project-structure) for the generated tree.

- **`.vscode/`**: Local editor settings and recommended extensions ensure a consistent VS Code experience
- **`src/`**: Houses production code. Separating it from tests and configuration files prevents naming conflicts and maintains clarity
- **`src/your_package/`**: Contains the main application code, including sub-packages and modules
- **`tests/`**: Mirrors the structure of your main package with corresponding test files
- **`.gitignore`**: Lists files and directories (e.g., virtual environments, build artifacts, temporary files, sensitive data) that Git should ignore
- **`README.md`**: Provides an overview of your project's purpose, setup, and usage

## Configuration

### What boilerplate configures for you

Generated projects arrive with the toolchain pre-wired. Beginners can ignore the specifics and just code; the exact configuration is here when you want it.

The shipped configuration (click to expand)

- **Ruff** (`[tool.ruff]`) — `fix = true` and a broad rule set (~26 categories: pyflakes, pycodestyle, isort, pydocstyle with the **Google** convention, annotations, bugbear, pathlib, pyupgrade, and more), plus docstring code formatting. `tests/` and `__init__.py` get sensible per-file ignores.
- **Pyright** (`[tool.pyright]`) — `typeCheckingMode = "strict"` over `src/` (tests relaxed). Type-checking runs live via Pylance in VS Code and from the CLI with `uv run pyright`; `pyright` ships in the dev group.
- **pytest** (`[tool.pytest.ini_options]`) — `log_cli = true`, with `pytest-cov` and `pytest-mock` in the dev group.
- **VS Code** (`.vscode/`) — Ruff as the default formatter for Python and notebooks, format-on-save, and pytest discovery enabled. The interpreter isn't pinned; the Python extension auto-detects `.venv` in the workspace root.

The authoritative configuration is the generated `pyproject.toml` and `.vscode/` — these summaries point you at it, not away from it. The [`pyproject.toml` guide](https://packaging.python.org/en/latest/guides/writing-pyproject-toml/) explains the file itself.

## Where next

- [VS Code](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/environment/vscode/index.md) — interpreter selection, extensions, and troubleshooting for the generated `.vscode/` setup.
- [Developer platform architecture](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/reference/platform/index.md) — the reference model this environment implements.

# VS Code configuration

Boilerplate projects ship a `.vscode/` folder so the editor is ready the moment you open the project — linting, formatting, type hints, and test discovery all work with no manual setup.

```text
.vscode/
├─ extensions.json
└─ settings.json
```

New to VS Code? After generating or cloning a project, open the folder and accept the prompt to install the recommended extensions.

## Recommended extensions

When you open a generated project, VS Code reads `.vscode/extensions.json` and offers to install these. That file is the authoritative list; this page explains what each one is for:

- **Python** (`ms-python.python`) — the core Python experience: run and debug code, pick the interpreter, and **Pylance**, which provides IntelliSense, go-to-definition, and live type checking as you type.
- **Jupyter** (`ms-toolsai.jupyter`) — open and run `.ipynb` notebooks inside VS Code.
- **Ruff** (`charliermarsh.ruff`) — linting and formatting, wired in as the default formatter for Python and notebooks.
- **Even Better TOML** (`tamasfe.even-better-toml`) — syntax highlighting and validation for `pyproject.toml` and other TOML files.
- **Prettier** (`esbenp.prettier-vscode`) — formatting for non-Python files (JSON, Markdown, YAML).

## Workspace settings

`.vscode/settings.json` connects the editor to the project's tools:

- **Ruff** is the default formatter for Python *and* notebooks, with **format-on-save** enabled.
- **pytest** discovery is on, so tests appear in the Testing sidebar.
- **Pylance** runs in workspace mode with auto-import suggestions, and honors the `[tool.pyright]` settings in `pyproject.toml` (strict over `src/`) — so the type errors you see inline match what the configured checks enforce.
- **Debugging** — set a breakpoint and press `F5` to launch the debugger with the workspace interpreter.

The interpreter path isn't set in `settings.json` — the Python extension auto-detects `.venv` in the workspace root, and that works the same on Windows, macOS, and Linux.

## Troubleshooting: the interpreter isn't detected

Most common right after generating or cloning a project, before the virtual environment exists:

1. Run `uv sync` to create `.venv`.
1. Open the Command Palette (`Ctrl+Shift+P`, or `Cmd+Shift+P` on macOS) → **Python: Select Interpreter**.
1. Choose the `.venv` interpreter in your project folder.

If an extension doesn't activate, reload the window: Command Palette → **Developer: Reload Window**.

## Troubleshooting: Ruff not formatting automatically

Check VS Code settings include:

```json
{
  "[python]": {
    "editor.defaultFormatter": "charliermarsh.ruff"
  }
}
```

Tip

Still not formatting? Command Palette → **Developer: Reload Window**.

## Troubleshooting: tests not discovered

- **Cause:** The test framework is not enabled or the environment is not activated.
- **Solution:**
  1. Run `uv sync` so `.venv` exists, then select it (**Python: Select Interpreter**).
  1. In VS Code, open the Command Palette and run "Python: Discover Tests".
  1. Select `pytest` as the test framework.
- **Verify:**
  - Tests appear in the VS Code Test Explorer.
  - Running `uv run pytest` in the terminal should show all tests passing.

## Where next

Other symptoms (lint errors, template rendering errors)? See [Troubleshooting](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/troubleshooting/index.md). Back to the [Development Environment overview](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/environment/index.md).

Boilerplate: a Python development environment paired with layered templates.

Boilerplate pairs a Python development environment, one tool for each job, with templates that build on one another to stamp out projects. Built on Copier.

### Composition

Composition feature package.

Authoritative implementation for dependency resolution and composition.

## `Composer`

Layers and merges template configurations - domain operation.

### `compose(resolution, *, include_states=False, include_deltas=False)`

Compose resolved templates into an ordered, layered Composition.

Walks `resolution.execution_sequence`, extracts each template's complete copier config, and merges cumulatively: later layers override question values; coordination keys (`_tasks`, `_secret_questions`, `_jinja_extensions`, `_min_copier_version`) merge per `CopierConfigMerger`; layer-local underscore keys are dropped from `final` but kept in their own layer's `values`. Sequence entries missing from `resolution.templates` are skipped. Pure computation — no I/O, no rendering.

Parameters:

| Name             | Type         | Description                                                                                                                                                                  | Default    |
| ---------------- | ------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------- |
| `resolution`     | `Resolution` | Resolved template set with a dependency-ordered execution_sequence.                                                                                                          | *required* |
| `include_states` | `bool`       | Populate CompositionLayer.state_after with the full merged state after each layer.                                                                                           | `False`    |
| `include_deltas` | `bool`       | Populate CompositionLayer.delta with changes versus the previous layer's state (always a dict, {} when unchanged; \_tasks never appears — it is excluded from layer values). | `False`    |

Returns:

| Type          | Description                                                                                                                                                                       |
| ------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Composition` | Dependency graph, execution sequence, per-layer values (cumulative questions plus that layer's own directives, \_tasks excluded), and the final merged schema used for rendering. |

## `Resolver`

Resolves template dependencies from a catalog.

Methods in this class are pure with respect to inputs and the provided registry; no side effects beyond logging. Resolution walks the `meta.extends` chain, validates references exist in the registry, and returns a complete mapping of template specifiers to their direct dependency specifiers along with a map of specifier to TemplateInfo.

Contract:

- Input `template_ref` may be `name` or `name@version`.
- Registry must implement lookups for both latest and versioned resolution.
- No cycle detection is performed here (handled by the graph layer).
- Dependency lists preserve the order specified in `meta.extends`.

### `resolve(template_ref, registry)`

Resolve a template reference into a complete dependency map and templates.

Parameters:

| Name           | Type              | Description                                               | Default    |
| -------------- | ----------------- | --------------------------------------------------------- | ---------- |
| `template_ref` | `str`             | Template identifier (e.g., name or name@version).         | *required* |
| `registry`     | `TemplateCatalog` | Catalog used to resolve templates and their dependencies. | *required* |

Returns:

| Type         | Description                                                 |
| ------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Resolution` | Frozen model containing the dependency map (by specifier    |
| `Resolution` | string) and a templates map from specifier to TemplateInfo. |

Raises:

| Type                            | Description                                                                                                               |
| ------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `DependencyNotFoundError`       | If any referenced template cannot be found.                                                                               |
| `InvalidTemplateSpecifierError` | If any extends reference is a malformed name@version string.                                                              |
| `VersionConflictError`          | If the same template name resolves to two different versions in the graph (diamond dependency with version disagreement). |

### Repository

Template repository implementations for Boilerplate.

## `DirectoryTemplateRepository`

Bases: `TemplateRepository`

Directory-based template repository implementing TemplateRepository.

Scans the specified directory for templates, validates their metadata, and loads them for use by coordinators such as TemplateCatalog.

Limitations

- Only one version per template name is supported at a time.
- Overwriting a template directory replaces the previous version.

### `load_templates()`

Return the templates discovered when this repository was constructed.

Discovery runs once, in `__init__`; this method only hands back the result, so repeated calls cost nothing and see no filesystem changes.

Returns:

| Type                 | Description              |
| -------------------- | ------------------------ |
| `list[TemplateInfo]` | All available templates. |

## `BoilerplateLock`

Bases: `BaseModel`

The lock Boilerplate writes into a project root after each operation.

The lock records the last complete operation, so its layer versions match what each layer's files were last rendered against. Fields a later minor schema adds are ignored on read.

### `root_name`

The name of the root template, which `add` never changes.

## `ChangeClassification`

Bases: `StrEnum`

The size of an update, the highest bump across its layers.

## `JoinedVia`

Bases: `StrEnum`

The way a layer entered the project the lock describes.

`EXTENDS` covers the root template and every layer its `extends` closure reaches. `ADD` is a layer `boilerplate add` introduced, which the root's target version does not govern.

## `MigrationRecord`

Bases: `BaseModel`

One operation Boilerplate recorded: its versions, outcome and, if paused, plan.

A `conflict` record is what a paused update resumes from: `targets` names the version the walk was updating each layer to, and `finished` the layers whose steps the walk completed.

Attributes:

| Name             | Type                   | Description                                                                                      |
| ---------------- | ---------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `id`             | `str`                  | A positive integer, sequential from "1", stored as a string.                                     |
| `from_version`   | \`str                  | None\`                                                                                           |
| `to_version`     | `str`                  | The root template specifier after the operation; for an add record, the added layer's specifier. |
| `timestamp`      | `AwareDatetime`        | When the record was written (UTC).                                                               |
| `status`         | `MigrationStatus`      | How the operation stands.                                                                        |
| `error`          | \`str                  | None\`                                                                                           |
| `classification` | \`ChangeClassification | None\`                                                                                           |
| `targets`        | \`Mapping[str, str]    | None\`                                                                                           |
| `finished`       | \`tuple[str, ...]      | None\`                                                                                           |

## `MigrationStatus`

Bases: `StrEnum`

How an operation recorded in `.boilerplate/migrations.yml` stands.

Each record is appended once, when its operation ends; the state of a run cut off before then is kept in the restore marker, not in the log. Exit codes: `SUCCESS`, `ADOPTED` and `CREATED` are 0, `CONFLICT` is 4 and `FAILED` is 1.

## `RestoreKind`

Bases: `StrEnum`

What the copy back of a marked run brings into the checkout.

Attributes:

| Name       | Type | Description                                                    |
| ---------- | ---- | -------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `COMPLETE` |      | A walk that finished every layer.                              |
| `PAUSED`   |      | A walk a conflict paused; it runs no tasks and writes no lock. |

## `RestoreMarker`

Bases: `BaseModel`

What a run cut off between its copy back and its record needs to be finished.

The marker is written before the copy back changes a file and removed after the run appends its record, so a marker found when a command starts belongs to a run that was cut off in between. It lives in the git directory, apart from the staging folder that the stale cleanup removes.

Attributes:

| Name            | Type                | Description                                                                                                               |
| --------------- | ------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `operation`     | `RestoreOperation`  | The command the run belongs to.                                                                                           |
| `kind`          | `RestoreKind`       | Whether the walk finished every layer or a conflict paused it.                                                            |
| `phase`         | `RestorePhase`      | How far the run got after its walk.                                                                                       |
| `start_commit`  | `str`               | The commit HEAD pointed at when the run began, a full object id.                                                          |
| `result_commit` | `str`               | The staging worktree's last per-layer commit, the start commit when no layer finished; a full object id.                  |
| `targets`       | `Mapping[str, str]` | Each layer of the walk, in walk order, with the version the walk was moving it to; never empty, and one layer for an add. |
| `finished`      | `tuple[str, ...]`   | The layers whose steps a paused walk finished, in walk order, the paused layer excluded; empty for a complete run.        |
| `paused_layer`  | \`str               | None\`                                                                                                                    |
| `started_at`    | `AwareDatetime`     | When the run began.                                                                                                       |

# Merging and precedence rules

Authoritative specification

The authoritative design specification for merge strategies and composition is [Composition engine](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/04-composition-engine/index.md). This page provides supplementary implementation-level reference. For the file-level three-way merge, conflict-pause, and safe-orphan semantics designed for the future `update` command, see [ADR-007](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/adr-007-update-model/index.md).

How configuration values are combined across template layers, with clear rules and deterministic outcomes.

## A two-layer merge

A base template and an app template that extends it, each with its own `copier.yml`:

```yaml
# base template — copier.yml
python_version:
    default: "3.12"
license:
    default: "Apache-2.0"
_tasks:
    - "uv sync"
```

```yaml
# app template — copier.yml (its boilerplate.yml declares extends: [base])
python_version:
    default: "3.13"
_tasks:
    - "git init"
```

Composing the app template produces a single questionnaire: `python_version` defaults to `3.13` (the later layer overrides), `license` survives from the base, and `_tasks` accumulates to `["uv sync", "git init"]`. The rules below generalize this.

## What gets merged

`boilerplate new` asks the merged questionnaire once, over every layer's questions, and a question default can use a filter from any layer's `_jinja_extensions`. Each layer then renders through its own Copier `Worker` invocation, applied in composition order, under its scoped view: the questions and importable `_jinja_extensions` of that layer and its ancestors, answered from that one pass. A layer's files and questions can use only what its own layer or an ancestor declares; a sibling's or a descendant's questions, filters and hooks are not visible to it. A file-path extension an ancestor declares (`_extensions/file.py:Class`) loads from that ancestor for each descendant that renders, and a layer's `.copier-answers.<layer>.yml` records its scoped view's answers only.

- Non-underscore keys (questions): merged across layers to form a single questionnaire.

  - dicts: later layer keys override earlier ones (shallow override).
  - lists: de-duplicated concat in order (first-seen wins).
  - scalars: later value overrides earlier value.

- Underscore-prefixed keys (directives): not merged, except a small allowlist below. All other underscore keys are treated as layer-local and skipped.

## File overlay

Each layer renders into the same destination through its own Copier `Worker` invocation, in composition order. Only the first layer's write respects `--force`; every later layer always overwrites, so a file that two layers both ship at the same path ends up with the last layer's content — there is no three-way diff or per-line merge. A layer that adds files at new paths never touches an earlier layer's files. `boilerplate new` ignores every template's `_skip_if_exists` list, so `--force` overwrites every file; where the lists apply is specified in the [Per-Layer Render Loop](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/04-composition-engine/#per-layer-render-loop).

## Allowlisted directive keys and strategies

- `_min_copier_version`: highest PEP 440 version (intersection by max).
- `_tasks`: accumulate in order (lists concatenate, scalars append).
- `_secret_questions`: accumulate in order.
- `_jinja_extensions`: union with original order preserved (dedupe).

Everything else starting with `_` is layer-local. These are discovered dynamically from `copier.Template` attributes at runtime and excluded from merging.

## Determinism and conflict handling

- Key order: keys are processed in first-seen order across layers.
- Type safety: incompatible types for the same question raise a merge conflict.

## Debugging merges

Run `boilerplate compose <template> --sections layers,deltas` to see each layer's contribution and what changed between them.

# Developer platform architecture

This page is the reference model behind Boilerplate: a toolchain of one tool per slot, picked from a tool landscape, built into the development environment and carried by the starter templates; golden paths run on it, and guardrails check the work. Each element has a single responsibility, from cataloging available tools to enforcing standards automatically.

In platform-engineering terms, an internal developer platform (IDP) is the self-service layer an organization runs for its own developers — templates plus CI/CD, provisioning, deployment, and operations, usually behind a portal. Boilerplate is open-source tooling for the scaffolding-and-environment slice of that: the toolchain, development environment, starter templates, and dev-time guardrails, with the golden path pre-built — where most platform tools hand you the machinery and leave the path to you. Deployment and operations are out of scope.

Scope

The reference implementation documented here is Boilerplate's own: Python-focused, with one toolchain. It is one worked example, not a general prescription for other contexts.

## The model

```
flowchart TD
    accTitle: Platform reference model overview
    accDescr: The Tool Landscape sits outside a Developer Platform boundary. Curation picks the Toolchain from the landscape, and the Toolchain is a part of the Development Environment. The Toolchain runs the Golden Path and is carried into projects by the Starter Templates, and Guardrails check both the path and the templates.
    L["Tool Landscape\nDescriptive context"]

    subgraph Platform["Developer Platform"]
        subgraph E["Development Environment"]
            P["Toolchain\nOne pick per slot"]
        end
        G["Golden Path\nPrescriptive workflow"]
        T["Starter Templates\nImplementation scaffolds"]
        R["Guardrails\nAutomated enforcement"]
    end

    L ==>|curation picks| P
    P ==>|runs| G
    P ==>|carried into projects by| T
    G ==>|checked by| R
    T ==>|checked by| R
```

Hold "Alt" / "Option" to enable pan & zoom

| Element                 | Type           | Question                   | Artifact                                |
| ----------------------- | -------------- | -------------------------- | --------------------------------------- |
| Tool landscape          | Descriptive    | What exists?               | Survey, catalog                         |
| Toolchain               | Prescriptive   | What do we use?            | Toolchain list                          |
| Golden path             | Prescriptive   | How do we work?            | Workflow definition                     |
| Development environment | Implementation | What is our setup made of? | Installer, `pyproject.toml`, `.vscode/` |
| Starter templates       | Implementation | How do we start?           | Project scaffolds                       |
| Guardrails              | Enforcement    | How do we comply?          | Automated policies                      |

The landscape describes available options; the toolchain and path prescribe specific choices; the environment and templates automate setup; guardrails automate verification.

## The tool landscape

The tool landscape is the descriptive catalog of tools, technologies, and practices available in a domain.

It sits outside the platform itself — it's the knowledge base platform decisions draw from — and answers *what tools and categories exist?*

Boilerplate maintains this as [The Development Environment Landscape](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/dev-environment-landscape/index.md), a taxonomy covering language runtimes, dependency management, code quality, testing, and CI/CD tooling.

Category names in the toolchain below are drawn from it.

## The toolchain

The toolchain is the subset of the landscape Boilerplate commits to supporting, sometimes called a curated stack. It answers *what do we use?*

The [Environment guide](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/environment/index.md) documents how each pick is configured and used day to day.

### Boilerplate reference implementation: Toolchain

| Category                                        | Standard                                                   | Rationale                                                                                                                                              |
| ----------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| **Python interpreter**                          | Python 3.12+                                               | Modern syntax (match statement, current type-hint features), active security support                                                                   |
| **Environment & package/dependency management** | uv                                                         | Fast dependency resolution and installs, pip-compatible, integrated venv management                                                                    |
| **Linters & code formatters**                   | ruff                                                       | Combines linting and formatting in one tool, replaces flake8/black/isort, minimal config                                                               |
| **Type checkers**                               | pyright (strict mode)                                      | Native VS Code integration via Pylance; strict mode catches more than default mode                                                                     |
| **Testing frameworks**                          | pytest + pytest-cov                                        | Fixture-based testing with a large plugin ecosystem; coverage via `pytest --cov`                                                                       |
| **Build tools**                                 | uv build (`uv_build` backend; `hatchling` as the override) | Standards-compliant (PEP 517/660/639); `uv_build` is uv's own backend for pure-Python code, `hatchling` covers build hooks and a version from git tags |
| **Version control**                             | Git                                                        | Branching and merging underpin template composition and CI workflows                                                                                   |
| **CI/CD**                                       | GitHub Actions (recommended)                               | Boilerplate's own gate runs on it                                                                                                                      |
| **Documentation generators**                    | MkDocs Material                                            | Markdown-native authoring, built-in navigation and search                                                                                              |
| **IDEs & editors**                              | VS Code                                                    | Extension ecosystem (Pylance, Ruff, pytest), remote development support                                                                                |

Planned

Generated projects don't scaffold CI config or a deploy-time and runtime guardrail layer: wire the three quality-check commands into your own CI provider's workflow. See the [backlog](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/roadmap/#backlog).

Templates scaffold the interpreter, dependency-management, lint/format, type-checking, testing, and build rows. The CI/CD and documentation rows are recommended picks you wire yourself.

For detailed configuration and usage, see:

- [Environment overview](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/environment/index.md)
- [uv guide](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/)
- [Ruff guide](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/)
- [Pyright guide](https://github.com/microsoft/pyright)
- [pytest guide](https://docs.pytest.org/)

## The golden path

A golden path is a workflow whose decisions are already thought out for you ([glossary](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/01-overview/#term-golden-path)). Golden paths nest: each starter template is a golden path to a starting point, and the dev loop is the golden path for the work that follows. The path below strings them together for a general Python project: a template's path to a starting point, the dev loop, then pull requests, CI and release. Deploy and operate appear for context; they are outside Boilerplate's scope. The term is Spotify's; Netflix calls the same idea the paved road. It answers *how do we work?*

The path is not mandatory — developers may diverge when circumstances warrant — but it's the most-supported, lowest-friction route, and platform investment (documentation, templates, CI automation) centers on it.

### From new project to production

```
flowchart TD
    accTitle: Golden path from new project to production
    accDescr: Four groups in order. Start: create the project, then set up its environment. Dev loop: red, write a failing test; green, make it pass; refactor; then run the checks and commit, and the next change starts the loop again. Pull request, CI and release: many commits are pushed as a pull request, CI builds and checks it, it merges, and many merges make a release. Outside Boilerplate's scope: deploy, then operate. The next change, or a CI failure, starts another turn of the dev loop.
    subgraph start["Start"]
        direction TB
        A[Create the project] --> B[Set up the environment]
    end
    subgraph loop["Dev loop"]
        direction TB
        C["Red: write a failing test"]
        D["Green: make it pass"]
        E[Refactor]
        F[Run the checks and commit]
        C --> D --> E --> F
        F -->|next change or CI failure| C
    end
    subgraph ship["Pull request, CI and release"]
        direction TB
        G[Push a pull request] --> H[CI builds and checks]
        H --> I[Merge]
        I -->|many merges| J[Release]
    end
    subgraph ops["Outside Boilerplate's scope"]
        direction TB
        K[Deploy] --> L[Operate and monitor]
    end
    start --> loop
    loop -->|many commits| ship
    ship --> ops
```

Hold "Alt" / "Option" to enable pan & zoom

### Tool engagement by stage

| Stage                   | Platform Tools                | Guardrails Active           | Template Support                  | Guide                                                                                                                                                                                |
| ----------------------- | ----------------------------- | --------------------------- | --------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| **Project creation**    | uv, copier                    | —                           | ✓ Scaffold structure              | [Quickstart](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/quickstart/index.md), [Templates Hub](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/templates-hub/index.md) |
| **Environment setup**   | uv (sync, venv)               | —                           | ✓ Pre-wired configs               | [Install](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/install/index.md), [Environment](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/environment/index.md)           |
| **Feature development** | VS Code, Pyright (live)       | ✓ Format-on-save (optional) | ✓ Project structure guidance      | [Environment](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/environment/index.md)                                                                                             |
| **Code quality**        | ruff check, ruff format       | —                           | ✓ Config locked in pyproject.toml | [Ruff guide](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/)                                                                                                                                           |
| **Testing**             | pytest, pytest-cov            | —                           | ✓ Test skeleton                   | [pytest guide](https://docs.pytest.org/)                                                                                                                                             |
| **Build**               | uv build                      | —                           | ✓ pyproject.toml build config     | [Environment](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/environment/index.md)                                                                                             |
| **Operate**             | Logs, metrics, error tracking | —                           | —                                 | —                                                                                                                                                                                    |

### The path in practice

| Stage             | Command                                                                        | What you get                                                                                                     |
| ----------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Project creation  | `boilerplate new project my-project`                                           | `src/`, `tests/`, `notebooks/`, `.vscode/`, `pyproject.toml`, README, `.gitignore`                               |
| Environment setup | `scripts/install.ps1`, then `uv sync`                                          | Git, uv, VS Code, and extensions on Windows (macOS/Linux install the same tools manually), then the project venv |
| Code quality      | `uv run ruff check --no-fix` · `uv run ruff format --check` · `uv run pyright` | Lint, formatting, and strict type checks                                                                         |
| Testing           | `uv run pytest`                                                                | Auto-discovery under `tests/`; coverage available via `pytest --cov`                                             |

Running the three quality checks plus tests on every push is the recommended CI setup.

## Starter templates

Starter templates are project scaffolds that encode platform decisions so developers can immediately follow the golden path. They answer *how do we start?*

### Boilerplate reference implementation: Templates

| Template                                                                                           | Description                                                  | Key Features                                         |
| -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------- |
| [project](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/templates-hub/project/index.md)     | A general-purpose Python project, with its tools configured. | Complete pyproject.toml, test suite                  |
| [streamlit](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/templates-hub/streamlit/index.md) | A Streamlit app, built on the general-purpose template.      | Streamlit app scaffold, container deployment configs |

See [Choose a template](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/templates-hub/#choose-a-template) for the full catalog. Templates use [Copier](https://copier.readthedocs.io/) for scaffolding. Complex projects can compose multiple templates; see [Template composition](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/templates-hub/composition/index.md).

## Guardrails

Guardrails are automated policies that convert platform standards from documentation into enforced behavior. They answer *how do we comply?*

### Boilerplate reference implementation: Guardrails

| Guardrail             | Enforcement Point | Tool/Mechanism        | Remediation                                                               |
| --------------------- | ----------------- | --------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Lint compliance**   | Dev (optional)    | `ruff check`          | `uv run ruff check --fix`                                                 |
| **Format compliance** | Dev (on-save)     | `ruff format --check` | `uv run ruff format`                                                      |
| **Type safety**       | Dev (live)        | `pyright --strict`    | Add type hints; see [Pyright guide](https://github.com/microsoft/pyright) |
| **Test passage**      | Dev (on-demand)   | `pytest` + coverage   | Fix failing tests; add tests for uncovered code                           |

These four are what's active today: lint, format, type, and test checks.

Ruff, Pyright, and pytest are all configured in `pyproject.toml`; see [Configuration](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/environment/#configuration) for the exact section names.
