## Part 2.5: Project Adoption

### Overview

Adoption bridges existing Copier-managed projects into Boilerplate lifecycle management. It creates the Boilerplate state files (`boilerplate.lock`, `.boilerplate/migrations.yml`) without modifying project files. After adoption, the project can use `status`, `lock verify`, and `update` as if it had been created with `boilerplate new`.

### Preconditions

Before adoption can proceed, all of the following MUST hold:

- At least one Copier answers file MUST exist in the project directory (confirms the project is Copier-managed). Adoption accepts both Copier's default singular `.copier-answers.yml` (legacy projects without `_answers_file:`) and per-layer `.copier-answers.<layer>.yml` files (projects scaffolded from Boilerplate-enabled templates).
- `boilerplate.lock` MUST NOT exist (the project is not already managed by Boilerplate). If it exists, fail with exit code `3`: `"Project already managed by Boilerplate. Use 'boilerplate update' instead."`
- The template referenced by the discovered answers file(s) MUST be resolvable in the catalog

### Adoption Pipeline

```text
1. Read     →  Parse each `.copier-answers.*.yml` (or the legacy singular `.copier-answers.yml`) for template source and answers
2. Resolve  →  Resolve template in catalog; if boilerplate-enabled, resolve full extends chain
3. Checksum →  Compute template source checksums for each layer
4. Lock     →  Write boilerplate.lock (same schema as creation)
5. Init     →  Write .boilerplate/migrations.yml with initial "adopted" entry
```

Each pipeline step follows the same rules as creation: the per-layer `copier_answers_file_hashes` are computed the same way, checksums use the same algorithm, lock files use the same schema and [Atomic Staged Write Pattern](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/07-operational-quality/#atomic-staged-write-pattern), and `created_at`/`updated_at` are both set to the current UTC timestamp. The migration record uses `adopted` (not `success`) as its status value, distinguishing adopted projects from created projects in the audit trail.

### What Is NOT Done

Adoption is a metadata-only operation. The following actions are explicitly **not** performed:

- No files are rendered or written to the project directory (beyond the state files)
- No template tasks are executed
- No git operations are performed (no commits, no branching)
- No environment provisioning is triggered
- Copier answers files (whichever form the project uses — singular `.copier-answers.yml` or per-layer `.copier-answers.<layer>.yml`) are read but never modified

The project's existing files remain exactly as they were before adoption.

> **Adopted projects MAY use Copier's default singular `.copier-answers.yml` file.** Adopted projects scaffolded by plain Copier (or by Boilerplate before per-layer files were the default) lack the per-layer `_answers_file:` contract (see [04 §Render Behavior](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/04-composition-engine/#render-behavior)). The `boilerplate.lock.copier_answers_file_hashes` mapping for an adopted single-layer project carries one entry, with the layer's template name as the key and the singular file's hash as the value.

### Copier-Only Templates

When the resolved template has no `boilerplate.yml`, it is a Copier-only template. Adoption still succeeds, but with reduced capabilities:

- A minimal lock file is written with a single layer and no composition metadata (no `extends` chain)
- The project can use `status` and `lock verify` to check template version and checksum integrity
- The project **cannot** use composition features (`compose`, `graph`) because there is no `boilerplate.yml` defining the composition
- `update` delegates entirely to Copier's single-template update mechanism

### Acceptance Criteria

| Scenario                                                                                                    | Expected Outcome                                                       |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Valid Copier project, template in catalog                                                                   | `boilerplate.lock` and `.boilerplate/migrations.yml` written, exit `0` |
| Project already has `boilerplate.lock`                                                                      | Rejected with `"Project already managed by Boilerplate"`, exit `3`     |
| No Copier answers file found (neither singular `.copier-answers.yml` nor any `.copier-answers.<layer>.yml`) | Rejected with `"No Copier answers file found"`, exit `3`               |
| Template not found in catalog                                                                               | `BP_RESOLVE_TEMPLATE_NOT_FOUND`, exit `1`                              |
| Copier-only template (no `boilerplate.yml`)                                                                 | Minimal lock file written (single layer, no composition), exit `0`     |

### Performance Contracts

See [Operational quality](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/07-operational-quality/index.md) for all performance targets.

**Cross-reference**: See [CLI reference](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/05-cli-reference/index.md) for the full `adopt` CLI specification.

______________________________________________________________________

## Part 2.6: Project Ejection

### Overview

Ejection is the exact inverse of [adoption](#part-25-project-adoption): it removes the Boilerplate-owned management state from a project, leaving every rendered file in place. After ejection, the directory is no longer Boilerplate-managed — `update`, `status`, and `lock verify` no longer apply — but it remains a usable plain Copier project (or plain files). Like adoption, ejection never modifies the project's rendered output.

### What Is Removed

Ejection deletes only Boilerplate-owned artifacts:

- `boilerplate.lock` (if present).
- The entire `.boilerplate/` directory (project-domain `migrations.yml`, and the environment-domain `environment.yml` if present).

### What Is Kept

- The Copier answers files — per-layer `.copier-answers.<layer>.yml`, or the legacy singular `.copier-answers.yml` — are **Copier-owned** and left untouched. An ejected project can still be managed directly with `copier update`.
- All rendered project files.
- `.prototools` and any proto-installed tools. **Ejection NEVER touches proto state.** Tool teardown is proto's responsibility: the proto install store is shared across projects, so removing it on one project's behalf is unsafe. This mirrors the ownership boundary that adoption respects in the other direction — Boilerplate manages only the files it owns.

### Idempotency

Ejection is a no-op only when NEITHER `boilerplate.lock` NOR `.boilerplate/` is present: it warns and exits `0`. Otherwise it removes whichever of the two exist — `boilerplate.lock` (if present) and the entire `.boilerplate/` directory. The directory is checked independently because `env apply` can create `.boilerplate/environment.yml` with no lock present (an environment-only project); keying the no-op on `boilerplate.lock` alone would orphan that state. This makes ejection safe to run repeatedly and safe to script.

### Concurrency and Locking

Ejection is a mutating operation and MUST acquire the standard advisory mutex on the project before removing state, under the universal rule in [§Concurrency](#concurrency) (same as `new`, `update`, `add`, `adopt`, and `env apply`). The lock target is the existing-project target under [§Concurrency](#concurrency); for an environment-only project (no lock, only `.boilerplate/`) that is not a git repository, the mutex falls back to the `new`-style sentinel (`.boilerplate-lock-{destination_name}` in the project's parent directory).

### No Recovery Needed

Ejection is a delete, not a staged write: there is no staging directory, no intent journal, and no backup to roll back or resume. Consequently it reuses none of update's merge or staging-worktree machinery. A user who ejects by mistake can re-`adopt` the project — adoption regenerates `boilerplate.lock` and `.boilerplate/migrations.yml` from the existing Copier answers files (see [Part 2.5](#part-25-project-adoption)).

### Acceptance Criteria

| Scenario                                                                  | Expected Outcome                                                                                      |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Managed project (`boilerplate.lock` present)                              | `boilerplate.lock` and `.boilerplate/` removed; rendered files and `.copier-answers.*` kept; exit `0` |
| Environment-only project (`.boilerplate/` present, no `boilerplate.lock`) | `.boilerplate/` removed; rendered files and `.copier-answers.*` kept; exit `0`                        |
| Neither `boilerplate.lock` nor `.boilerplate/` present                    | No-op: warning emitted, nothing removed, exit `0`                                                     |
| `--dry-run`                                                               | Removal list printed, nothing removed, exit `0`                                                       |
| Filesystem/permission failure during removal                              | `BP_FILESYSTEM_PERMISSION`, exit `1`                                                                  |

**Cross-reference**: See [CLI reference](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/05-cli-reference/index.md) for the full `eject` CLI specification.

______________________________________________________________________

## Part 3: Artifact Fetching

For remote templates (not local directories), the system MUST:

1. Fetch template artifacts from remote git hosting services (e.g., GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket)
1. Cache fetched artifacts locally with SHA-256 integrity validation
1. Initialize git submodules before any YAML parsing
1. Retry transient network failures with exponential backoff (max 3 attempts by default)
1. Detect and report missing or broken submodule references with recovery suggestions

**Caching**: Templates fetched from remote repositories MUST be cached by their `checksum`. Subsequent operations with the same checksum MUST use the cached artifact without re-fetching.

**Retry policy**: See [Operational quality](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/07-operational-quality/index.md) for the full retry specification.

# Operational Quality

## Purpose

Cross-cutting operational quality controls that apply to every feature slice: stable error codes, error attribution, structured logging, performance contracts, retry policy, the Atomic Staged Write Pattern, concurrency control, and platform portability. The security model itself lives in [Security model](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/10-security/index.md).

______________________________________________________________________

## Error Codes

### Design Principles

1. Error codes MUST be stable once published — **from 1.0**. During `0.x` (pre-release; see [Versioning & Compatibility](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/governance/versioning/index.md)) codes MAY still change as the surface settles, and the rename to the `BP_{PHASE}_{DESCRIPTOR}` scheme is pre-1.0 hygiene, not a frozen contract. From 1.0, a published code MUST NOT change its meaning.
1. Each code MUST map to exactly one root cause.
1. Each code MUST carry: phase, severity, retryable flag, and remediation guidance.
1. Codes MUST NOT leak sensitive internal details.

### Code Namespace

All error codes use the prefix `BP_` followed by the phase and a short descriptor:

```text
BP_{PHASE}_{DESCRIPTOR}
```

### Phase Prefixes

| Phase prefix      | Scope                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| ----------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `BP_RESOLVE_`     | Template resolution and dependency traversal                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `BP_VERSION_`     | Version parsing and constraint evaluation                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `BP_GRAPH_`       | Dependency graph building and validation                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `BP_LOCK_`        | Lock file reading, writing, and validation                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `BP_RENDER_`      | Template rendering and staging                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `BP_INPUT_`       | User input validation                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `BP_CONFIG_`      | Configuration loading                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `BP_FETCH_`       | Remote template fetching (network, authentication)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `BP_GIT_`         | Git binary availability and Git command failures                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `BP_ENV_`         | Environment provisioning (`env apply` command group)                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `BP_CONCURRENCY_` | Operation-level concurrency control: advisory-lock acquisition and mutex contention. Distinct from `BP_LOCK_`, which is content-level operations on the lock file artifact.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `BP_FILESYSTEM_`  | Local filesystem failures (permission denial, path-length limits) raised by Boilerplate's I/O routines independent of pipeline stage. Example: `BP_FILESYSTEM_PERMISSION`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `BP_BUNDLE_`      | Integrity verification for archive and wheel-bundle template sources (archive extraction failures, checksum mismatches). Example: `BP_BUNDLE_CHECKSUM_FAILED`. The prefix covers all non-Git archive-based sources.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `BP_UPDATE_`      | The update walk and adding a layer: drift between the lock and the answers files, an incomplete answers file, a resume whose targets differ from the paused update's, a resolved source that diverges from the lock (`BP_UPDATE_SOURCE_DIVERGED`, [10 §Verification Pipeline](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/10-security/#verification-pipeline)), staging preconditions, and a task that fails after the copy back. Example: `BP_UPDATE_LAYER_DRIFT`. |
| `BP_COPIER_`      | Copier-engine compatibility failures (version mismatch, unsupported Copier feature). Example: `BP_COPIER_COMPAT_FAILED`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |

> **Mapping to pipeline stages**: Error code phases are orthogonal to the operational pipeline stages defined in [Project lifecycle](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/06-project-lifecycle/index.md). The creation pipeline stages (Resolve → Compose → Render → Lock → Init) may trigger errors from multiple phases: the Resolve stage may produce `BP_RESOLVE_*`, `BP_VERSION_*`, or `BP_GRAPH_*` errors; the Render stage may produce `BP_RENDER_*` or `BP_GIT_*` errors; the Lock stage may produce `BP_LOCK_*` errors. Error code phases group errors by their root cause domain, not by the pipeline stage in which they occur.

### Error Code Registry

Each error code carries severity, retryable flag, a human-readable description, remediation guidance, and attribution. The registry grows as new failure modes are identified, but published codes are immutable from 1.0 (see Design Principle 1). Domain-specific codes are documented in their owning specification (e.g., `BP_ENV_*` in [§08 Environment Provisioning](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/08-environment-provisioning/index.md)).

### Error Message Format

Every error emitted to the user MUST include the following components, presented in inverted pyramid order (most actionable first):

1. **Error description**: A concise, human-readable `Error: ...` line with the `BP_*` code as a bracketed suffix
1. **Reason**: The root cause or context (indented below)
1. **Fix**: A concrete, actionable remediation step (indented, labeled "Fix:")
1. **Code**: The stable `BP_*` code (shown as suffix on the Error line)
1. **Attribution**: Which component owns the failure — shown only in `--verbose` mode
1. **Exit code**: Shown only in `--verbose` mode

**For interactive (TTY) output**, error messages MUST use the inverted pyramid pattern — lead with the human-readable description, promote the fix, demote metadata:

```text
Error: Render failed while processing template "streamlit-app".   [BP_RENDER_TEMPLATE_FAILURE]
  Missing include file _base/project/copier.yml.
  Fix: git submodule update --init --recursive
```

**For verbose mode** (`--verbose`), the full diagnostic format is shown:

```text
Error: Render failed while processing template "streamlit-app".   [BP_RENDER_TEMPLATE_FAILURE]
  Missing include file _base/project/copier.yml.
  Fix: git submodule update --init --recursive
  Attribution: YAML
  Exit code: 1
```

**For JSON output** (`--format json`), all fields are included in the JSON error object.

**Multi-step remediation**. When the fix requires more than one action, the `Fix:` line MAY expand into a multi-line block introduced by `→` arrows:

```text
Error: Template not found in catalog: pyhton-web   [BP_RESOLVE_TEMPLATE_NOT_FOUND]
  Searched catalogs: official, community.
  Did you mean 'python-web' (92% match)?
  Fix:
    → boilerplate catalog sync
    → boilerplate new python-web
```

Each arrow is a discrete remediation step. The arrow prefix is reserved for remediation-step lines; other guidance uses normal indentation.

### Error Attribution

| Attribution       | Meaning                                                  |
| ----------------- | -------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Boilerplate`     | The failure is in Boilerplate's own logic                |
| `Copier`          | Copier reported a rendering or task error                |
| `Git`             | A git operation failed                                   |
| `YAML`            | YAML parsing or include resolution failed                |
| `User`            | The error is due to invalid user input                   |
| `Network`         | A remote operation failed due to connectivity            |
| `System`          | A required system dependency is missing or misconfigured |
| `proto`           | The proto toolchain manager reported an error            |
| `Template Author` | The error is due to a defect in template configuration   |

**Attribution decision rules for boundary cases**:

- Copier fails due to invalid Jinja2 in a template → **Template Author** (the template has a syntax error)
- Copier fails due to an internal bug → **Copier** (Boilerplate has no control over Copier internals)
- Git authentication fails → **User** if credentials are misconfigured; **Network** if the server is unreachable
- Template declares an invalid `_min_copier_version` → **Template Author** (the template metadata is wrong)
- Lock file checksum mismatch → **System** (disk corruption or external modification)

When multiple parties are involved, attribute to the **root cause** — the party whose action or configuration caused the failure, not the component that reported it.

## Structured Logging

### Logging Levels

| Level     | When to use                                              |
| --------- | -------------------------------------------------------- |
| `ERROR`   | Operation failed; user action required                   |
| `WARNING` | Non-fatal issue the user should know about               |
| `INFO`    | Normal progress and completion events                    |
| `DEBUG`   | Detailed diagnostic information (enabled by `--verbose`) |

### Required Log Fields

Every structured log event MUST include: the operation phase, the specific operation, the template being processed (if applicable), a correlation ID (`request_id`), success/failure status, duration, and the `BP_*` error code on failure.

Task execution events MUST additionally include the command executed, the source template, execution order, exit code, and duration. Task stdout and stderr MUST be captured and logged at DEBUG level to enable post-incident investigation of what tasks ran and which template authored them.

**Privacy invariants**:

- Logs MUST NOT contain secrets, passwords, API tokens, or PII
- Personal data MUST be redacted before emission
- Only structural identifiers (template names, versions, paths) are permitted

### Redaction

Log redaction MUST be systematic rather than per-log-statement. A centralized redaction mechanism MUST scrub sensitive patterns (credentials, tokens, URL userinfo) from all log output, including captured subprocess output, before emission. Sensitive values MUST use a type that refuses to serialize to string representations, preventing accidental leakage.

### Log Output

**Terminal**: When stderr is a TTY and `NO_COLOR` is not set, use rich-formatted output with colors and structured layout. Non-TTY stderr receives a single JSON object per log event.

**Structured output**: All machine-readable log output is emitted as JSON to stderr. Logging is stderr-only by design — no file-based logging, rotation, or external aggregation. Consumers that need persistence may redirect stderr.

**Correlation ID passthrough**: When `BOILERPLATE_REQUEST_ID` is set in the environment, its value MUST be used as the correlation ID for all log entries in that invocation, overriding any auto-generated ID. This enables parent service correlation in pipeline and orchestration contexts.

### Subprocess Correlation

The per-invocation `request_id` MUST be propagated to all subprocesses as the environment variable `BOILERPLATE_REQUEST_ID`. When `BOILERPLATE_REQUEST_ID` is already set in the environment (e.g., by a parent orchestration process), Boilerplate MUST use the provided value rather than generating a new one. This enables correlation with parent process traces and distributed tracing systems. While external tools (Copier, Git, proto) do not consume this variable, it enables:

- Correlation of Boilerplate's structured logs with subprocess output captured at DEBUG level
- External log aggregation systems to group all activity from a single Boilerplate invocation

All subprocess stdout and stderr MUST be captured and logged at DEBUG level with the `request_id` and `phase` fields attached.

### Phase Vocabulary

The `phase` log field uses a closed enum aligned with the operation pipeline: `resolve`, `fetch`, `render`, `update`, `lock`, `catalog`, `env_apply`, plus `internal` for events outside any pipeline phase (bootstrap, configuration loading, third-party library records). Implementations MUST NOT emit `phase` values outside this set without first extending the enum here. This pipeline-phase vocabulary is distinct from the error-code phase prefixes defined above.

### Logging Invariants

- There MUST be exactly one terminal log event per high-level request (success or failure). Step-level events MAY occur en route, but the terminal event is the canonical record.
- Every terminal log event with `success: false` MUST carry a `BP_*` `error_code` field. No anonymous failures.
- `duration_ms` MUST appear only on the terminal log event, never on step events.

______________________________________________________________________

## Performance Contracts

**Invariants**:

- DX commands (status, validate, shell completions) MUST complete within 500ms on a developer machine with a local catalog of up to 200 templates.
- Long-running operations MUST show progress feedback.
- Algorithmic complexity MUST be linear in the size of the template graph.

### Retry Policy

Only errors marked `retryable: true` in the error code registry MAY be retried. Non-retryable errors (validation failures, not-found, cycles, conflicts) MUST fail immediately.

Retryable errors use exponential backoff with jitter. Between retry attempts, the staging directory MUST be completely removed and recreated to prevent corrupted results from partial output.

**Default parameters**:

| Parameter        | Value       | Description                                                                                           |
| ---------------- | ----------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Base delay       | 1 second    | Initial delay before first retry                                                                      |
| Maximum delay    | 30 seconds  | Cap on exponential growth                                                                             |
| Maximum attempts | 3           | Total attempts including the initial try                                                              |
| Jitter           | Full jitter | Random value between 0 and the computed delay (`delay = random(0, min(max_delay, base * 2^attempt))`) |

These defaults apply to all retryable operations (network fetches, transient subprocess failures). Individual operations MAY override `max_attempts` via configuration but MUST NOT disable jitter.

**Transient vs. deterministic classification**: Rendering failures (`BP_RENDER_TEMPLATE_FAILURE`) are retryable only for transient causes (subprocess timeout, OOM kill). Deterministic failures (Jinja2 syntax errors, missing variables) MUST fail immediately. Implementations MUST classify the error before deciding retryability.

### Network Timeouts

All network operations MUST enforce a configurable timeout to prevent an operation from waiting indefinitely on unresponsive servers. Network timeouts and rendering timeouts are independent and independently configurable.

______________________________________________________________________

## Security Model

The full security model lives in [Security model](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/10-security/index.md). Operational invariants that gate the security checks (atomic-write pattern, concurrency control, retry policy, redaction mechanism, structured logging) remain in this document; the security rules cite them where needed.

______________________________________________________________________

## Atomic Staged Write Pattern

Both project creation ([§06](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/06-project-lifecycle/index.md)) and environment provisioning ([§08](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/08-environment-provisioning/index.md)) follow the same staged-write-with-intent-journal pattern. This section defines the shared invariants; each feature documents its specific file names, phase values, and recovery procedures.

**Core invariant**: All destructive operations follow a stage → validate → commit sequence. Work is performed in an isolated staging directory. An intent journal tracks the current phase for crash recovery. On success, staged output is atomically moved into place and the journal is deleted. On failure or interruption, the staging directory is cleaned up and the project directory is left in its pre-operation state. For `update` and `add` the commit step is the copy back, which is not atomic: a copy back that fails is undone ([06 §Undo](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/06-project-lifecycle/#undo)), and one cut off midway is finished or set aside as the restore marker directs ([06 §Interrupted copy back](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/06-project-lifecycle/#interrupted-copy-back)).

**Stale cleanup**: Before creating a new staging directory, stale staging directories (older than 1 hour; see [Project lifecycle](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/06-project-lifecycle/index.md)) from previous interrupted operations are detected and cleaned up. For `update` and `add`, whose staging directory holds a git worktree ([06 §Staging worktree](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/06-project-lifecycle/#staging-worktree)), the cleanup removes only worktrees Boilerplate created, identified by the journal and the owner check, and then runs `git worktree prune` in the project the journal's `destination` names, which drops the registration of a worktree whose folder is gone. A staging folder is stale only when it is older than the window and no running operation holds the exclusive lock each operation takes on its journal for the operation's lifetime: age alone would remove an update that is waiting at a prompt. `git worktree prune` runs only in this cleanup, never when an operation removes its own worktree, so the user's own worktree registrations are left alone.

**Intent journal invariants**:

- Written atomically and updated before each phase transition.
- Deleted on successful completion.
- If present but unparseable after a crash: left for user inspection without automated recovery.

**Restore marker**: For `update` and `add`, the state of a copy back cut off midway is kept in a restore marker in the project's git directory, not in the staging folder and not in the intent journal, so it outlives the stale cleanup. It is written and rewritten with the single-file invocation below ([06 §Interrupted copy back](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/06-project-lifecycle/#interrupted-copy-back)).

**Signal handling**: Process termination signals MUST trigger the same cleanup as a failure. Untrappable signals are handled by stale cleanup and journal recovery on the next invocation.

**Retry behavior**: On retry, the previous attempt's staging directory and intent journal are cleaned up before creating a new staging directory.

**Single-file invocation**: When the staged unit is a single append-only file rather than a directory tree, the same stage → validate → commit principle applies via tmp-then-rename: read existing content, construct the updated content in memory, write to a sibling temporary file (`<filename>.tmp.{random_suffix}`) in the same directory, then atomically rename it to the target name. This prevents a crash during write from leaving a truncated file. Used by `.boilerplate/migrations.yml` and similar single-file audit logs.

### Concurrency Control

Boilerplate does not support concurrent mutating operations on the same target. Before any mutating operation, Boilerplate MUST acquire a platform-native advisory file lock (POSIX `fcntl`/`flock`; Windows `LockFileEx`) with a configurable timeout (default: 60 seconds, `BOILERPLATE_LOCK_TIMEOUT`). If the lock cannot be acquired, fail with `BP_CONCURRENCY_CONTENTION`. The lock is held for the duration of the operation and MUST be released when the operation completes or the holding process exits (the OS releases advisory file locks on process termination). On POSIX, ownership means the lock file's UID matches the effective UID. On Windows, ACL-based ownership applies.

______________________________________________________________________

## Platform Portability

Cross-cutting platform constraints that apply across all Boilerplate operations.

### Path Limits (Windows)

Boilerplate MUST fail fast before rendering if any rendered file path would exceed the Windows path limit and long paths are not enabled. `boilerplate doctor` MUST check this setting.

### Filesystem Differences

- Line endings: first-party templates carry a `.gitattributes` with `* text=auto eol=lf`, and third-party templates should ([03 §Template Authoring Constraints](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/03-template-system/#template-authoring-constraints)). `boilerplate doctor` SHOULD validate that the file is present and declares it.
- Git submodule paths can be problematic on NTFS. Submodule initialization failures MUST produce clear errors with remediation (see [Project lifecycle](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/06-project-lifecycle/index.md)).

### Network Filesystems

Advisory file locking is unreliable on network filesystems. `boilerplate doctor` MUST detect network filesystems and warn. Staging directories SHOULD be created on local storage when possible.

### WSL2 Cross-Filesystem Access

Accessing Windows filesystems from WSL2 incurs significant I/O overhead. Template sources and project directories on the native WSL2 filesystem perform significantly better.

### Environment Variables (Windows)

Windows treats environment variables as case-insensitive. This cannot be enforced for `BOILERPLATE_`-prefixed variables on Windows.

______________________________________________________________________

## Exit Code Reference

Exit codes are defined in [Data models](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/02-data-models/index.md). An implementer MUST use those codes exactly -- no custom codes beyond those defined in §02.

# Environment Provisioning

## Purpose

`boilerplate env apply` and `boilerplate env status`: resolving the `EnvironmentProfile` `extends` chain, merging tool versions and packages across profile layers, generating `.prototools` in proto's native format, invoking proto for tool installation, and writing the `.boilerplate/environment.yml` provenance record.

______________________________________________________________________

## State Files

A Boilerplate-managed environment contains the following state files after a successful `env apply`:

| File                           | Owner                                     | Purpose                                                                                     |
| ------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `.prototools`                  | Boilerplate (generated) / proto (runtime) | Declares resolved tool versions for proto; generated by Boilerplate from the merged profile |
| `.protolock`                   | proto                                     | Records exact resolved tool versions and checksums; written by proto after install          |
| `.boilerplate/environment.yml` | Boilerplate                               | Records which profile was applied, the resolved `extends` chain, and a hash of `.protolock` |

**Ownership invariants**:

- Boilerplate MUST NOT write to `.protolock`. That file is owned by proto.
- External tools MUST NOT write to `.boilerplate/environment.yml`. That file is owned by Boilerplate.
- `.boilerplate/environment.yml` MUST only be written after a fully successful provisioning operation. It MUST never reflect a partial state.
- `boilerplate-env.yml` is the declarative input owned by the profile author. Boilerplate reads it; it MUST NOT be modified during provisioning.

______________________________________________________________________

## Part 1: Profile Resolution

### Purpose

Profile resolution transforms the root `EnvironmentProfile` and its `extends` chain into a flat, ordered list of profiles and a single merged tool version map ready for `.prototools` generation.

### Resolution Algorithm

Resolution takes the root profile specifier and a catalog as inputs, and produces a flat, ordered list of profiles (base-first, derived-last) as output. The algorithm performs a depth-first traversal of the `extends` chain, resolving each profile from the catalog.

**Inputs**: Root profile specifier, profile catalog.

**Output**: Ordered profile chain (base-first, derived-last; root profile always last).

**Invariants**:

- **Cycle detection**: A cycle in the `extends` chain MUST be detected and reported as `BP_ENV_EXTENDS_CYCLE` with the full cycle path (e.g., `base -> python -> base`).
- **Diamond deduplication**: A profile reachable via multiple paths is included once, at the position first encountered during traversal.
- **Missing profiles**: If the root profile cannot be found, fail with `BP_ENV_PROFILE_NOT_FOUND`. If a parent in the `extends` chain cannot be found, fail with `BP_ENV_EXTENDS_NOT_FOUND`.
- **Determinism**: Given the same profile definitions, the resolved chain MUST always be identical. Traversal order is determined by the `extends` declaration order in each profile. This parallels the template composition tie-breaking rule in [§04 Composition Engine](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/04-composition-engine/index.md).

### Tool Version Merging

After the profile chain is resolved, tool versions are merged across all layers using a **last-writer-wins** policy: the chain is walked base-first, and each profile's tool declarations overwrite earlier values for the same tool name. The most-derived profile (last in topological order) wins for any given tool.

This is simpler than template composition's four named merge strategies (see [§04](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/04-composition-engine/index.md)) because tool versions are simple scalars, not the complex nested structures that template configurations contain.

The result is a flat `{tool_name: version_string}` map covering every tool declared in any profile in the chain.

### `packages` Field Merging

After tool version merging, the `packages` field (map of platform key to list of `PackageRequirement`) is merged across the extends chain:

- For each platform key, `PackageRequirement` lists are **accumulated** in topological order (base first, derived last).
- When multiple profiles declare the same package (by `name`) for the same platform, the **last-writer-wins**: the most-derived profile's version constraint replaces earlier entries for that package name.
- The result is a flat `{platform: [PackageRequirement, ...]}` map. Platform keys not present in a profile are inherited unchanged from ancestor profiles.
- Tools with version constraints (e.g., `>=3.10`) that cannot be resolved to a single exact version MUST cause `BP_ENV_VERSION_UNRESOLVABLE`. Constraint-only entries are not valid for `.prototools` generation. Implementations SHOULD emit a descriptive error: `"Profile '{name}' declares tool '{tool}' with version constraint '{constraint}' which cannot be resolved to an exact version. Declare an exact version for provisioning."`

### `allowed_proto_plugins` Enforcement

After tool version merging, the combined allowlist is computed by intersecting all non-empty `allowed_proto_plugins` lists across the chain.

**Enforcement rules**:

- An empty `allowed_proto_plugins` list on a profile means **no restriction from that layer** — not "block all tools."
- If ALL profiles in the chain have an empty `allowed_proto_plugins` (the default), the combined allowlist is empty, meaning **no restriction applies** and all resolved tools are permitted.
- If ANY profile in the chain declares a non-empty `allowed_proto_plugins`, the combined allowlist is the **intersection** of all non-empty lists across the chain. This ensures that a base profile's allowlist acts as a ceiling — derived profiles can only narrow the set, never expand it.
- After computing the combined allowlist: for each tool in the resolved tool map, if the combined allowlist is non-empty and the tool name does NOT appear in the combined allowlist, raise `BP_ENV_PLUGIN_NOT_ALLOWED`.
- Error message MUST identify the disallowed tool, the requesting profile, and the restricting profile: `"Tool '{tool}' is not in the allowed_proto_plugins intersection. Requested by profile '{requesting_profile}'. Not present in allowlist defined by profile '{restricting_profile}'. Contact the platform team to update the base allowlist."`

> **Note (non-normative):** intersection is a ceiling, not a floor — derived profiles can only narrow the allowlist, never expand it (expansion would be privilege escalation through profile composition). A tool absent from the base allowlist requires the platform team to update the base profile.
>
> **Trust model scope**: Environment profiles do not use the template trust gate (trusted/untrusted) because the security surface differs. Template tasks execute arbitrary shell commands gated by trust. Proto plugins execute in a WASM sandbox with constrained host access. The `allowed_proto_plugins` intersection mechanism is the security control for profiles — it provides an equivalent ceiling guarantee (base profiles restrict derived profiles) without requiring task-trust classification.

______________________________________________________________________

## Part 2: `.prototools` Generation

Boilerplate generates proto's native configuration file (`.prototools`) from the merged tool version map. The generated file is written to the project root.

### Generation Rules

- Only tools with resolved exact versions are included. Unresolvable versions MUST have already caused `BP_ENV_VERSION_UNRESOLVABLE` during the merge step.
- Tool entries MUST be sorted lexicographically by name for deterministic output and clean diffs.
- Path values MUST use forward slashes on all platforms for cross-platform compatibility.

### Ownership and Versioning

- `.prototools` is a **generated output** owned by Boilerplate in the provisioning context; `boilerplate-env.yml` is the **declarative input**.
- `.prototools` MAY be committed to version control as a development convenience -- proto reads it at runtime to determine which tool versions to activate.
- The output is reproducible: re-running `boilerplate env apply` with the same profile produces an identical `.prototools`.
- Entries added manually to `.prototools` outside of Boilerplate are not tracked and will be overwritten on the next `env apply`.

______________________________________________________________________

## Part 3: Proto Integration

### Proto Binary Discovery

- proto MUST be discoverable via `PATH`.
- `boilerplate doctor` MUST verify proto is installed and emit an actionable message if not found.
- If proto is not found during `env apply`, the operation MUST fail immediately with `BP_ENV_PROTO_NOT_FOUND` before any staging or I/O occurs.

### ProtoWorker Interface

The ProtoWorker abstracts proto's CLI behind a stable contract owned by Boilerplate. Implementations MUST isolate all proto invocations behind this interface so that proto version upgrades require changes only in the worker implementation.

**`install_tool(tool_name, version, timeout)` → `InstallResult`**

| Parameter   | Type    | Description                              |
| ----------- | ------- | ---------------------------------------- |
| `tool_name` | string  | Tool identifier (e.g., `python`, `node`) |
| `version`   | string  | Exact version to install                 |
| `timeout`   | integer | Maximum seconds for this installation    |

**`InstallResult`**:

| Field       | Type           | Description                    |
| ----------- | -------------- | ------------------------------ |
| `success`   | boolean        | Whether installation completed |
| `tool_name` | string         | The tool that was installed    |
| `version`   | string         | The exact version installed    |
| `error`     | string or null | Error message on failure       |

**`trigger_proto_lockfile()` → path**

Invokes proto's native lockfile generation (proto writes `.protolock`; Boilerplate does NOT) and returns the path to the resulting file. The method exists so the worker can report the lockfile path to caller code that needs to compute `proto_lock_hash` for the EnvironmentProvisionRecord. The worker MUST NOT itself write or modify `.protolock`.

**Behavioral contracts**:

- The worker MUST NOT modify `.prototools` — that file is generated by Boilerplate and consumed by proto.
- If `install_tool` fails, the error message MUST identify the specific tool and version.
- Proto availability MUST be verified before any installation attempt; if proto is not found, fail with `BP_ENV_PROTO_NOT_FOUND`.

### Invocation

Boilerplate invokes proto to install the resolved tools. All resolved tools MUST be installed before the commit phase proceeds. Implementations SHOULD invoke proto per-tool for granular error attribution. Bulk invocation MAY be used when per-tool invocation is impractical, but the error message MUST still identify the specific tool and version that failed.

### Timeout

Proto installation is subject to a configurable timeout, independent of the rendering timeout. Proto installation is network-bound (downloading tool binaries), so the timeout must accommodate cold-cache downloads of large toolchains.

### Failure Handling

- If any proto install invocation fails, the provisioning MUST fail with `BP_ENV_APPLY_FAILED`.
- The proto error output MUST be included in the structured log.
- The human-readable error message MUST identify the specific tool and version that failed.

### `.protolock` Relationship

proto writes `.protolock` to the project root after successful installation, recording exact tool versions, checksums, and platform metadata.

**Ownership boundaries**:

- Boilerplate MUST NOT write, modify, or delete `.protolock`. It is owned by proto.
- Boilerplate reads `.protolock` after a successful install to compute the `proto_lock_hash` field for `.boilerplate/environment.yml`.
- If proto did not write `.protolock`, `proto_lock_hash` is `null`.
- `boilerplate env status` reads both `.boilerplate/environment.yml` and `.protolock` to report the current environment state.

______________________________________________________________________

## Part 3.5: Package Requirements

### Purpose

After profile resolution and tool version merging, the merged `packages` map is evaluated for the current platform. This section specifies how declared `PackageRequirement` entries are handled during `env apply` and related commands.

### Platform Detection

Boilerplate detects the current platform (Windows, WSL2, Linux, macOS) and evaluates only packages declared for that platform. Packages for other platforms are silently ignored.

### Behavior During `env apply`

A declared package installs when the `system-package` provider kind covers it, under the trust gate ADR-009 §Trust specifies ([ADR-009](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/adr-009-environment-provider-protocol/index.md)); Boilerplate MUST NOT invoke a package manager outside that gate, because an ungated install would violate the "orchestrate, don't replace" principle and introduce privilege escalation and safety concerns.

For a package with no covering provider, requirements stay **advisory, not automatically installed**. Boilerplate **validates** that the package is present on the system by checking for binaries on PATH or querying the platform's package manager. Missing packages produce a WARNING with the recommended install command. Success is silent.

### Pipeline Integration

- **Plan display**: When packages are declared for the current platform, the provisioning plan MUST include a `Package requirements:` section listing each package with the provider that installs it, or the command to install it by hand when no provider covers it. This gives the user visibility before confirming.
- **Post-install check**: Covered packages install with the tools in step 4; a failed covered install raises `BP_ENV_APPLY_FAILED`, the same as a failed tool install: no record is written, and rerunning recovers. Uncovered packages are still checked after the installs and before the provenance record is written, and a missing one only warns. Warnings are appended to the success-path output and also surface via `env status`.

### `env status` Integration

The `env status` command SHOULD check package availability for the current platform and report missing packages as warnings, using the same detection logic described above.

______________________________________________________________________

## Part 4: Provisioning Pipeline

`boilerplate env apply` runs a single linear flow under an advisory lock. The provenance record (`.boilerplate/environment.yml`) is written only after a fully successful install, so it never reflects a partial state. If a step fails, the lock is released and the user re-runs `env apply`; because `.prototools` generation and proto install are idempotent, re-running converges to the resolved state.

### Flow

```text
1. Resolve       →  Load profile, resolve extends chain, merge tool versions, enforce allowlist
2. Plan/Confirm  →  Diff current vs. resolved; prompt for confirmation
3. Generate      →  Acquire advisory lock; write .prototools via staged write
4. Proto Install →  Invoke proto install for all resolved tools; install covered packages through their provider
5. Record Write  →  Write .boilerplate/environment.yml; release lock
```

### 1 — Resolve

Loads the target profile, resolves the `extends` chain (see §Profile Resolution), merges tool versions (last-writer-wins), and enforces the plugin allowlist. Produces a resolved tool map and ordered profile chain.

Failures at this step (`BP_ENV_PROFILE_NOT_FOUND`, `BP_ENV_EXTENDS_CYCLE`, `BP_ENV_EXTENDS_NOT_FOUND`, `BP_ENV_VERSION_UNRESOLVABLE`, `BP_ENV_PLUGIN_NOT_ALLOWED`) are validation errors — no files are modified.

### 2 — Plan and Confirm

Computes the diff between the current environment state (from `.boilerplate/environment.yml`, if present) and the resolved tool map. Displays a provisioning plan showing installs, upgrades, and unchanged tools.

**Behavioral rules**:

- No differences: report "already up to date" and exit with no changes.
- `--dry-run`: display the plan and exit without writing.
- `--format json` without `--yes` or `--dry-run`: fail (JSON mode requires explicit intent to prevent interactive prompts in automation).
- `--yes` or `--ci`: proceed without prompting.
- Otherwise: prompt for confirmation (default: No).
- Major version boundary crossings MUST be annotated with a warning.

### 3 — Generate `.prototools`

Acquires the advisory lock per [07-operational-quality.md §Concurrency Control](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/07-operational-quality/#concurrency-control), then writes the resolved `.prototools` to the project root using the staged write (temp file + rename) from the [Atomic Staged Write Pattern](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/07-operational-quality/#atomic-staged-write-pattern). All subsequent steps occur under the lock.

### 4 — Proto Install

Invokes proto to install each resolved tool, subject to the timeout defined in §Proto Integration. It also installs covered packages through their provider (see §Part 3.5), with the same failure rule. Progress is reported when running interactively.

**If any installation fails, tool or covered package**: the lock is released and `BP_ENV_APPLY_FAILED` is raised with the failing tool or package name, version, and installer output. The provenance record is not written; re-running `env apply` is the recovery path.

### 5 — Record Write

Computes the `proto_lock_hash` from `.protolock` (if present), writes `.boilerplate/environment.yml` atomically (see §`.boilerplate/environment.yml` Schema), and releases the advisory lock. Emits a completion summary (profile, tools installed, duration) in both human-readable and JSON output formats.

### Signal Handling

Signal handling follows the [Atomic Staged Write Pattern](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/07-operational-quality/#atomic-staged-write-pattern). The advisory lock MUST be released on cleanup. An interrupted `env apply` leaves no provenance record; the recovery story is to run `env apply` again.

______________________________________________________________________

## Part 5: `.boilerplate/environment.yml` Schema

The `.boilerplate/environment.yml` schema is defined in [02-data-models.md §EnvironmentProvisionRecord](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/02-data-models/index.md). The `.boilerplate/` directory is created if it does not exist. Key write invariants:

### Example

```yaml
schema_version: "boilerplate/environment@1"
boilerplate_version: "0.3.0"
profile_name: python-dev
profile_version: "1.2.0"
extends_chain:
  - base@1.0.0
  - python-dev@1.2.0
applied_at: "2026-03-20T14:30:00Z"
tools:
  node: "20.11.0"
  python: "3.12.2"
proto_lock_hash: "a3f1c9b2d8e4f7a1c3e5b7d9f2a4c6e8b0d2f4a6c8e0b2d4f6a8c0e2b4d6f8a0"
```

### Write Invariants

- The file MUST be written atomically (temp file + rename).
- The file MUST only be written after proto has successfully installed all tools (step 4 of the provisioning flow).
- Keys MUST be sorted deterministically for clean diffs.
- The `tools` map keys MUST be sorted lexicographically.

### Schema Versioning

The `schema_version` field enables forward-compatible evolution. Boilerplate MUST parse any `environment.yml` sharing the same major version (`boilerplate/environment@1`). Minor version bumps add optional fields; major bumps may change semantics. When Boilerplate encounters a file with an unrecognized major version, it MUST warn and treat the file as absent rather than failing hard — the environment may still be usable even if the record cannot be interpreted.

______________________________________________________________________

## Part 6: Concurrency

Environment provisioning follows the shared concurrency control pattern. See [07-operational-quality.md §Concurrency Control](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/07-operational-quality/#concurrency-control). The lock is acquired when `.prototools` is generated and released after the provenance record is written (or on failure). Network filesystem caveats apply (see [07-operational-quality.md §Platform Portability](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/07-operational-quality/#platform-portability)).

______________________________________________________________________

## Part 7: Platform-Specific Behaviors

General platform portability rules are in [07-operational-quality.md §Platform Portability](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/07-operational-quality/#platform-portability). This section covers environment-provisioning-specific platform details.

- **Windows**: where file rename is not atomic, the staged write uses a copy-verify-replace pattern. Tool names in `.prototools` MUST be lowercase for case-insensitive filesystem compatibility.
- **WSL2**: `boilerplate doctor` MUST detect Windows-hosted proto and warn about path mapping issues. Recommend installing proto natively within WSL2.
- **All platforms**: proto MUST be on PATH.

______________________________________________________________________

## Part 8: `env status`

### `boilerplate env status`

Reports the current environment state by reading `.boilerplate/environment.yml` and `.protolock`. Shows the applied profile, tools, and whether the protolock hash is consistent. Warns if no environment record exists or if the protolock hash has drifted since the last apply.

______________________________________________________________________

## Part 9: Error Reference

Environment provisioning uses the `BP_ENV_*` error code family, plus `BP_CONCURRENCY_CONTENTION` and `BP_FILESYSTEM_*` for infrastructure failures. See [07-operational-quality.md §Phase Prefixes](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/07-operational-quality/#phase-prefixes) for the phase registry and [07-operational-quality.md §Error Message Format](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/07-operational-quality/#error-message-format) for the standard message format.

______________________________________________________________________

## Part 10: Profile Lifecycle, Drift, and Compatibility

### Profile Lifecycle Phases

A profile passes through several phases during its useful life. Each phase produces a distinct artifact and has distinct failure modes:

| Phase        | Trigger                                                 | Primary output                                                      | Typical failures                                                               |
| ------------ | ------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Authoring    | Author edits `boilerplate-env.yml`                      | Profile draft                                                       | Schema validation failure; unsatisfiable `extends` chain                       |
| Publication  | Catalog ingest assigns immutable version                | Published profile                                                   | Duplicate version; missing required sections                                   |
| Installation | `boilerplate env apply`                                 | `.prototools`, `.protolock` (proto), `.boilerplate/environment.yml` | `BP_ENV_PROFILE_NOT_FOUND`, `BP_ENV_PLUGIN_NOT_ALLOWED`, proto install failure |
| Update       | `boilerplate env apply` against a newer profile version | Updated state + refreshed `.boilerplate/environment.yml`            | Breaking change; lock conflict                                                 |
| Removal      | (Future scope) Tool removal via proto                   | Cleanup record                                                      | Out of scope                                                                   |

Phase events feed structured logging (per §07 Phase Vocabulary, where the relevant phase is `env_apply`).

### Drift

After a profile is applied, the live environment can diverge from the recorded state — for example, a tool version drifts from `.protolock`, the recomputed `.protolock` hash no longer matches `EnvironmentProvisionRecord.proto_lock_hash`, a declared tool is missing, the cached profile version differs from the catalog, or the host OS/arch differs from provision time. `boilerplate env status` reports such drift as warnings. The remediation in every case is to re-run `boilerplate env apply`.

### Template-Profile Compatibility

When a template declares `requires_profile`, applying or updating it verifies compatibility with the project's environment state: the required profile resolves in the catalog, the project's resolved profile name and version satisfy the template's range, and the tools the template depends on are present in the resolved profile chain. These checks are owned by the resolve/composition path ([§04 Composition Engine](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/04-composition-engine/index.md)) at `new` and `update` time. On read-only commands a mismatch is a warning surfaced via `env status`, not a hard failure.

______________________________________________________________________

## Acceptance Criteria

| Scenario                            | Expected Outcome                                                            |
| ----------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Valid single-profile apply          | `.prototools` written, proto succeeds, `environment.yml` written, exit 0    |
| Profile with `extends` chain        | Chain resolved base-first, versions merged (last-writer-wins), exit 0       |
| Profile not found                   | `BP_ENV_PROFILE_NOT_FOUND`, no files modified, exit 3                       |
| Cycle in `extends` chain            | `BP_ENV_EXTENDS_CYCLE` with full cycle path, exit 3                         |
| Tool not in `allowed_proto_plugins` | `BP_ENV_PLUGIN_NOT_ALLOWED`, no files modified, exit 3                      |
| `proto install` fails               | `BP_ENV_APPLY_FAILED`, `environment.yml` not written, exit 1                |
| `--dry-run`                         | Plan displayed, no files modified, exit 0                                   |
| No changes detected                 | "Environment is already up to date.", exit 0                                |
| Interrupted `env apply`             | No provenance record written; re-running `env apply` completes provisioning |
| proto not installed                 | `BP_ENV_PROTO_NOT_FOUND`, immediate exit 3 before any I/O                   |
| Concurrent `env apply`              | Second invocation fails with `BP_CONCURRENCY_CONTENTION` after timeout      |

### Performance Contracts

See [§07 Operational Quality](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/07-operational-quality/index.md) for all performance targets. Environment provisioning is I/O and network intensive; the dominant cost is proto downloading tool binaries. Boilerplate's own orchestration overhead (profile resolution, diff computation, `.prototools` generation) MUST be negligible relative to proto install time.

# Settings and Configuration Files

## Purpose

The user-authored runtime configuration surface: the `Settings` object, a per-user profile (`profile.toml`), and the `boilerplate-sources.yml` catalog-source file — the YAML and environment-variable inputs the operator owns, separate from the domain schemas in [Data models](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/02-data-models/index.md).

See [Product overview](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/01-overview/index.md) for the glossary. See [Security model](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/10-security/index.md) for the security constraints that apply to the configuration files specified here (YAML tag rejection, path traversal validation).

______________________________________________________________________

## Settings

The `Settings` object holds all runtime configuration. It is loaded once at CLI startup and passed to all application services. Settings MUST be immutable after construction.

**Loading order** (later sources override earlier):

1. Compiled-in defaults
1. `.env` file in the current working directory (if present) — standard `KEY=VALUE` format, one assignment per line, `#` for comments
1. OS environment variables

All `Settings` field names are prefixed with `BOILERPLATE_` when read from the environment, using the flat field name directly (e.g. `BOILERPLATE_DEBUG`). [Profile](#profile) has no environment-variable layer — it is TOML-file-only.

| Field                        | Env Var                                  | Type           | Default                                 | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| ---------------------------- | ---------------------------------------- | -------------- | --------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `default_templates_dir`      | `BOILERPLATE_DEFAULT_TEMPLATES_DIR`      | path           | `{user_data_dir}/boilerplate/templates` | The user's standing template directory, searched before `extra_template_dirs`. Starts empty; first-party templates do not live here.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `extra_template_dirs`        | `BOILERPLATE_EXTRA_TEMPLATE_DIRS`        | list of paths  | `[]`                                    | Additional template directories searched after `default_templates_dir`. OS environment values are split on the platform path separator. When both sources provide `extra_template_dirs`, OS environment entries are placed before `.env` file entries in the resulting list (giving OS entries higher search priority). Deduplication preserves the first occurrence. |
| `debug`                      | `BOILERPLATE_DEBUG`                      | boolean        | `false`                                 | Enable debug-level logging; overridden to `true` by `--verbose` flag                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `render_timeout`             | `BOILERPLATE_RENDER_TIMEOUT`             | integer        | `300`                                   | Maximum seconds for a single template render                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `proto_timeout`              | `BOILERPLATE_PROTO_TIMEOUT`              | integer        | `600`                                   | Maximum seconds for a proto install invocation. See [§08](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/08-environment-provisioning/index.md).                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `fetch_timeout`              | `BOILERPLATE_FETCH_TIMEOUT`              | integer        | `60`                                    | Maximum seconds for a single network operation. See [§07](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/07-operational-quality/index.md).                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `lock_timeout`               | `BOILERPLATE_LOCK_TIMEOUT`               | integer        | `60`                                    | Maximum seconds to acquire advisory lock. See [§06](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/06-project-lifecycle/index.md).                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `allowed_extension_packages` | `BOILERPLATE_ALLOWED_EXTENSION_PACKAGES` | list of string | `[]`                                    | System-wide allowlist of Python package names whose Jinja2 extensions are permitted during rendering. See [§03 Template System](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/03-template-system/index.md).                                                                                                                                             |
| `request_id`                 | `BOILERPLATE_REQUEST_ID`                 | string or null | `null`                                  | Correlation ID for structured log events. When set (typically by CI pipelines or orchestration tools), the value is included in every structured log event as the `request_id` field. See [§07 Operational Quality](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/07-operational-quality/index.md).                                                     |
| `accessible`                 | `BOILERPLATE_ACCESSIBLE`                 | boolean        | `false`                                 | When enabled (any value except unset, empty, whitespace-only, `0`, or `false`, case-insensitive), activates all accessibility accommodations: no color, append-mode progress, text-only status labels, no banner. See [§05 CLI Reference](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/05-cli-reference/index.md).                                     |

**`template_dirs`** (computed, not configurable): the concatenation of `[default_templates_dir] + extra_template_dirs`. This is the ordered list of directories the catalog build process searches. First-party templates — the published per-template git repositories ([ADR-006](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/adr-006-template-distribution/index.md)) — are registered by the catalog build as an implicit final source after all `template_dirs` entries — see [03 §Template Directory Resolution Order](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/03-template-system/#template-directory-resolution-order); they are not a Settings path.

`{user_data_dir}` resolves to the platform-appropriate user data directory (e.g., `%LOCALAPPDATA%` on Windows, `~/.local/share` on Linux).

If loading the Settings object fails for any reason, the CLI MUST print an error and exit with code `2` (`CONFIG_ERROR`).

______________________________________________________________________

## Profile

Per-user default answers for template questions, read from `profile.toml` at the config root. Grammar: `[defaults]` (any template) and `[templates.<name>]` (one template, overrides `[defaults]`). Keys are open — they are template question names; boilerplate validates none of them. Loader: `boilerplate.settings.profile.load_profile(template_name)`; missing file yields `{}`, malformed TOML raises `ProfileError`.

The config root is platform-specific: `%APPDATA%\boilerplate` on Windows, and `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/boilerplate` (falling back to `~/.config/boilerplate`) on POSIX.

**Precedence**, high to low: the user's interactive answer › `[templates.<name>]` › `[defaults]` › the template's own default. Defaults pre-fill prompts — the user can still override at the prompt; `--non-interactive` takes them as-is.

______________________________________________________________________

## Catalog Source Configuration File

**File location**: `{user_data_dir}/boilerplate/boilerplate-sources.yml`

This file defines the template and profile catalog sources that Boilerplate searches during resolution. It is a single YAML document with one top-level key.

**Top-level structure**:

| Field     | Type                | Required | Description                                |
| --------- | ------------------- | -------- | ------------------------------------------ |
| `sources` | list of SourceEntry | Yes      | Ordered list of catalog source definitions |

**SourceEntry schema**:

| Field             | Type           | Required | Default     | Constraints                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| ----------------- | -------------- | -------- | ----------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `name`            | string         | Yes      | —           | Human-readable source identifier. MUST be unique across all entries.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `type`            | enum           | Yes      | —           | One of: `filesystem`, `git`, `archive`. `wheel_bundle` is a deferred seed-cache type ([ADR-006](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/adr-006-template-distribution/index.md)), not yet available for configuration.
