The `http`, `github`, and `oci` types are reserved for future versions.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `location`        | string         | Yes      | —           | URI or filesystem path to the source. Interpretation depends on `type`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `credentials`     | string or null | No       | `null`      | **Reserved for Phase 4 (remote / third-party sources).** Reference to a credential — an environment variable name or vault path. MUST NOT contain a literal secret value. See Validation Rules below.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `priority`        | integer        | No       | `100`       | Lower number = higher priority. Ties broken by registration order (position in the `sources` list).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `trust_level`     | enum           | No       | `untrusted` | `trusted` or `untrusted`. Governs sources configured in this file; the implicit first-party source — the published per-template repositories ([ADR-006](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/adr-006-template-distribution/index.md)) — is `trusted` by default and does not appear here. Trusted sources may execute tasks with user consent; untrusted sources execute tasks only with explicit user authorization via `--allow-tasks` (or `--allow-untrusted`) — see [§03 Task Execution Safety](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/03-template-system/#task-execution-safety). A lock file MAY record an independent free-form string field (`trust_tier`) for forward compatibility, but resolution logic treats only this binary enum. Absence of a recorded trust value MUST NOT fail resolution. |
| `expected_commit` | string or null | No       | `null`      | For TOFU (trust-on-first-use) pinning: the expected commit hash on first clone of a `git` source. When set, Boilerplate records the commit on first use and rejects subsequent fetches whose tip does not descend from it. Ignored for `filesystem` and `archive` types.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |

Source types that define additional fields (`checksum` for `archive`) are specified in the corresponding source model section: [ArchiveSource](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/02-data-models/#archivesource). Those fields are included inline in the YAML entry alongside the common fields above.

**Example**:

```yaml
sources:
  - name: official
    type: git
    location: https://github.com/org/templates.git
    trust_level: trusted
    priority: 10
  - name: team-local
    type: git
    location: /home/dev/templates
    trust_level: untrusted
  - name: offline-archive
    type: archive
    location: /opt/boilerplate/archives/starter-kit.tar.gz
    checksum: "sha256:a1b2c3..."
```

**Validation rules**:

1. **Credential safety** (Phase 4): The `credentials` field is reserved for Phase 4 (remote / third-party sources). Until then, when the field is present, Boilerplate MUST reject values that appear to be literal credentials. Literal secrets MUST never appear in this file.
1. **Trust enforcement**: A source entry with `trust_level: trusted` enables task execution subject to the user consent prompt; `trust_level: untrusted` (the default) blocks task execution unless the user explicitly authorizes it with `--allow-tasks` (or `--allow-untrusted`); see [§03 Task Execution Safety](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/03-template-system/#task-execution-safety). There is no intermediate tier.
1. **File permissions (POSIX)**: On POSIX systems, the file MUST be readable only by the owner. Boilerplate SHOULD warn or refuse to load the file if permissions are more permissive.
1. **Duplicate rejection**: Duplicate `name` values across entries MUST be rejected at parse time. Duplicate YAML keys within a single mapping MUST also be rejected.
1. **Unknown fields**: Unknown fields within a source entry SHOULD produce a warning but MUST NOT cause a hard failure, to allow forward compatibility with newer schema versions.

See [10-security.md §Catalog Source Configuration](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/10-security/#catalog-source-configuration) for the full security constraints on catalog source configuration (YAML tag rejection, path traversal validation).

# Security Model

Target model

This describes the target security model. For what is enforced today, see [ADR-003](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/adr-003-permissive-execution/index.md) and the [Status](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/status/index.md) page.

## Purpose

This document specifies the cross-cutting security rules for Boilerplate. Security rules that are inseparable from local context live in their owning documents; this document does not restate them. Related specs:

- **Trust model** (binary trusted/untrusted classification, task-execution consent gating): [Template system and discovery](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/03-template-system/index.md)
- **Lock file integrity** (checksums, atomic writes): [Data models](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/02-data-models/index.md), [Project lifecycle](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/06-project-lifecycle/index.md)
- **Operational invariants that gate security checks** (atomic-write pattern, concurrency control, retry policy): [Operational quality](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/07-operational-quality/index.md)
- **YAML parsing, input validation, privacy, threat model**: this document

See [Data models](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/02-data-models/index.md) for exit codes. See [CLI reference](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/05-cli-reference/index.md) for CLI output conventions. See [Settings and configuration files](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/09-settings-and-configuration/index.md) for the operator-authored configuration files referenced below.

______________________________________________________________________

## Threat Model

Boilerplate operates in a trust boundary between template authors (who provide executable content via Jinja2 extensions and `_tasks`) and project consumers (who run `boilerplate new`). The threat scenarios that the design mitigates:

| Scenario                     | Vector                                                 | Impact                                          |
| ---------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------- |
| Tampered template source     | Git repo compromise; commit replaced after publication | Malicious code in rendered project              |
| Malicious Jinja2 extension   | Unsafe extension loaded at render                      | Code execution at render time                   |
| Malicious `_tasks` execution | Template tasks run shell commands at user privilege    | Code execution post-render                      |
| Dependency-chain poisoning   | Transitive template replaced with malicious version    | Integrity loss; unexpected behavior             |
| Answers-file manipulation    | User-supplied answer values hijack rendering           | Misconfiguration; secret leakage                |
| Lock-file forgery            | Stale or fabricated lock claims success                | Reproducibility failure; bypass of verification |
| Catalog metadata spoofing    | False version, author, or trust claim                  | Trust erosion; misattribution                   |
| Credential leakage           | Secrets in logs, URLs, or error messages               | Authentication compromise                       |
| Supply-chain compromise      | Boilerplate's own dependencies tampered                | Tool-level code execution                       |

Each threat is mitigated by a specific design control:

| Threat                       | Mitigation                                                                                                             | Reference                                                                                                                                                                   |
| ---------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Tampered template source     | Commit-pinned lock + per-layer checksum                                                                                | §06 Lock Files; §02 `boilerplate.lock`                                                                                                                                      |
| Malicious Jinja2 extension   | Module-import blocklist + `SandboxedEnvironment` + user consent (`--allow-extensions`)                                 | [§03 Jinja2 Extension Safety](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/03-template-system/#jinja2-extension-safety)                                      |
| Malicious `_tasks` execution | Default-deny task gating: tasks run only after the consent prompt or `--allow-tasks`; `--no-tasks` skips them entirely | [§03 Task Execution Safety](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/03-template-system/#task-execution-safety)                                          |
| Dependency-chain poisoning   | Lock integrity verified before render; per-node provenance recorded                                                    | §06; `boilerplate lock verify`                                                                                                                                              |
| Answers-file manipulation    | Immutable answers on update (Copier contract); answer values bypass Jinja2 pipeline                                    | [§03 Copier Integration Contract](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/03-template-system/#copier-integration-contract); §Answer Preset Safety below |
| Lock-file forgery            | Lock integrity check before render/update                                                                              | `boilerplate lock verify`                                                                                                                                                   |
| Catalog metadata spoofing    | Trusted/untrusted source classification; metadata hash + provenance per source                                         | [§03 Trust and Verification Levels](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/03-template-system/#trust-and-verification-levels)                          |
| Credential leakage           | Git credential helper exclusivity; redaction processor; URL credential stripping                                       | §Credential Handling below; [§07 Redaction](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/07-operational-quality/#redaction)                                  |
| Supply-chain compromise      | Pinned dependencies + lock; out of scope for the spec but addressed in repo CI                                         | (engineering practice)                                                                                                                                                      |

______________________________________________________________________

## Verification Pipeline

Security checks run at defined phases — never lazily. A check that detects a violation MUST fail the operation with a `BP_*` error before any irreversible work proceeds:

| Phase        | Security check                                                                                            | Failure mode                                                                               |
| ------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Fetch        | Verify resolved commit matches lock (if lock present); record content checksum                            | `BP_FETCH_CHECKSUM_MISMATCH`                                                               |
| Resolve      | Every node in the dependency graph has provenance (source URL + commit-or-checksum; trust value optional) | `BP_RESOLVE_PROVENANCE_MISSING`                                                            |
| Render (pre) | Lock integrity verified; extension allowlist evaluated; user consent gates fired                          | `BP_LOCK_INTEGRITY_FAILED`, `BP_RENDER_UNSAFE_EXTENSION`, `BP_RENDER_TASKS_NOT_AUTHORIZED` |
| Update       | New resolution diffed against existing lock; unexpected source changes flagged                            | `BP_UPDATE_SOURCE_DIVERGED`                                                                |

______________________________________________________________________

## Security Invariants

Across all operations, the following invariants MUST hold; violation is a contract bug:

- Every resolved template node in `boilerplate.lock` MUST record its source URL, its commit, and its checksum; a node missing any of these MUST fail resolution. The commit and checksum MUST be verified before render or update proceeds. A trust value (the optional `trust_tier` field) MUST be recorded when the source declares one, but its absence MUST NOT fail resolution (local sources declare no trust value).
- The full template source MUST be available before YAML parse or Copier invocation; the canonical statement of this submodule-initialization-before-render rule lives in [§03](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/03-template-system/#boundary-invariants).
- A Jinja2 extension MUST NOT be loaded unless its package is on the system-wide allowlist AND user consent has been granted.
- Answer-preset values MUST never pass through `jinja2.Environment.from_string()` (architectural, not validation-based).

______________________________________________________________________

## Credential Handling

Boilerplate MUST use the Git credential helper (`git credential fill` / `git credential approve`) as the exclusive mechanism for authenticating to remote Git repositories. Embedding credentials directly in Git URLs (e.g., `https://token@host/repo`) is prohibited. Credentials in URLs are exposed in process argument lists (visible via `ps` or Task Manager), shell history, CI logs, and Git's own diagnostic output.

If the Git credential helper is not configured or fails to provide credentials, Boilerplate MUST fail with `BP_GIT_AUTH_FAILED` and provide remediation guidance directing the user to configure `git credential-manager` or the appropriate platform credential helper.

______________________________________________________________________

## File Permissions

Boilerplate MUST create files and directories with sensible default permissions unless the template explicitly overrides them. Staging directories MUST be restricted to owner-only access to prevent other users from reading or modifying in-progress renders. On Windows, Boilerplate relies on the default ACL inheritance of the parent directory.

______________________________________________________________________

## Trust Boundaries

All external inputs MUST be validated at trust boundaries before processing. A trust boundary exists wherever data enters Boilerplate from an external source: user CLI arguments, YAML files on disk, answer presets, and template content.

- **Remote template source responses**: Content fetched via `git clone` from remote repositories transitions from untrusted network data to local filesystem content. The initial fetch is trust-on-first-use (TOFU); subsequent fetches are validated against the lock file's commit hash and content checksum.
- **Proto plugin execution**: WASM plugins executed by proto during environment provisioning represent a trust boundary. Plugins are fetched from the proto plugin registry and execute tool installation logic. *Reserved for Phase 4 (remote / third-party sources):* a proto WASM plugin allowlist that constrains which plugins are permitted. Currently, toolchains are provisioned from local, operator-authored profiles only.

______________________________________________________________________

## Checksum Scope

**Checksum scope clarification**: Two distinct checksums appear in Boilerplate's data model:

1. **Template source checksum**: computed from the template directory contents at the locked commit (pre-render). The exclusion list for this checksum is: `.git/`, `__pycache__/`, `.mypy_cache/`, `.pytest_cache/`, `.ruff_cache/`, `node_modules/`. See [§06 Project Lifecycle](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/06-project-lifecycle/index.md) for the authoritative list.
1. **Rendered output checksum**: computed from the project directory contents after rendering. The exclusion list for this checksum SHOULD be extensible: template authors MAY declare `checksum_excludes` in their `boilerplate.yml` to add project-specific exclusions (e.g., `.venv/`, `.tox/`, `node_modules/`, `.pytest_cache/`). Boilerplate ships with default exclusions: `.git/`, `__pycache__/`, `.boilerplate/`. Exclusions are matched as prefix paths relative to the project root.

______________________________________________________________________

## Catalog Source Configuration

Catalog sources beyond the default filesystem directories are configured in a `boilerplate-sources.yml` file. This file defines catalog sources with their type, location, priority, and trust classification. The full schema, validation rules, and read protocol are specified in [09-settings-and-configuration.md §Catalog Source Configuration File](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/09-settings-and-configuration/#catalog-source-configuration-file), including credential references, file permissions, and trusted/untrusted classification.

______________________________________________________________________

## YAML Parsing Security

YAML parsing MUST follow the security rules defined in [03-template-system.md §YAML Parsing Rules](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/03-template-system/#yaml-parsing-rules).

______________________________________________________________________

## Jinja2 Sandbox

See [§03 Template System §Jinja2 Sandbox](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/03-template-system/#jinja2-sandbox) for the normative spec.

______________________________________________________________________

## Answer Preset Safety

Answer preset values MUST be treated as literal strings and passed to Copier without Jinja2 rendering. Implementations MUST NOT attempt to detect or reject Jinja2 syntax in answer values (a value like `{{ example }}` may be a legitimate literal string, e.g., documenting a Jinja2 template). Instead, the safety guarantee is architectural: answer values bypass the Jinja2 rendering pipeline entirely. They are injected as pre-resolved answers into Copier's data context, never passed through `jinja2.Environment.from_string()`.

> **Double-rendering risk**: An answer value containing Jinja2-like syntax (e.g., `{{ secret }}`) is passed to Copier as a literal and never re-rendered, so its curly braces appear in output as text, not as a Jinja2 expression. This single-pass guarantee is a property of Copier's pipeline, not Boilerplate's. Implementations MUST verify this behavior against the supported Copier version range in integration tests.

Note: each layer's `.copier-answers.<layer>.yml` is a separate artifact owned by Copier (per the per-layer pattern). Boilerplate MUST NOT write to or validate any of them.

______________________________________________________________________

## Input Validation

All user-provided inputs -- CLI arguments, interactive prompts, and file-based inputs -- MUST be validated against expected formats before use. The `BP_INPUT_INVALID_FORMAT` error code MUST be raised for any input that fails validation.

______________________________________________________________________

## Privacy

- Logs, error messages, and diagnostic output MUST NOT contain secrets, passwords, API tokens, or PII.
- Personal data MUST be redacted before emission to any output channel (terminal, log file, structured log event).

Answers to questions marked `secret: true` (Copier's secret question flag) MUST NOT reach any file Boilerplate writes. Copier leaves them out of each `.copier-answers.<layer>.yml`, which is why that file is safe to pass to `--data-file` as an answer preset; a secret answer is supplied again on the next run through `--data` from an environment variable, or through a `--data-file` kept outside version control; a literal on the command line lands in shell history.

See also [§07 Redaction](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/07-operational-quality/#redaction) for the systematic log redaction mechanism and [§07 Structured Logging](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/07-operational-quality/#structured-logging) for required log fields and privacy invariants.

______________________________________________________________________

## Error Message Hygiene

Error messages presented to users MUST NOT leak internal file paths, stack traces, or implementation details. Diagnostic details SHOULD be available only via `--verbose` or `DEBUG`-level logging.

In `--verbose` mode, Boilerplate MAY include additional diagnostic context such as resolved template paths, Copier invocation arguments (excluding credentials), and timing details. Verbose output MUST NOT include: credential values, answer values marked as secret (`secret: true`), full file contents, or environment variable values. Template source URLs are acceptable in verbose output but MUST have any embedded credentials stripped.

______________________________________________________________________

## CI/CD Lock Verification

**RECOMMENDED CI gate**: Include `boilerplate lock verify` as a step in your CI pipeline. This step SHOULD run before any `boilerplate update` invocation in CI.

`boilerplate lock verify` checks:

- All template layer sources are reachable and contain the locked commits
- Template layer content checksums match recorded values
- Each `.copier-answers.<layer>.yml` hash matches its entry in `copier_answers_file_hashes` (if present)

It does NOT verify:

- Lock file integrity (no cryptographic signature; the file is trusted as-is)
- That re-rendering would produce identical output (Copier behavioral differences across versions may affect output)
- Answer correctness (only that answers haven't changed since last operation)

`lock verify` is a supply chain drift detector, not a full integrity guarantee. For stronger assurance, combine with content signing (planned for a future release). Example GitHub Actions step:

```yaml
- name: Verify template lock integrity
  run: boilerplate lock verify
```

# ADR-001: Build vs. Adopt Analysis

**Status**: Accepted

> **Scope note.** This ADR records the build-vs-adopt *decisions* and the supply-chain assessment. The Copier integration *mechanism* is recorded separately in [ADR-002](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/adr-002-copier-internals-shim/index.md).

## Context

Each responsibility was evaluated against the modern tool landscape to decide build vs. delegate. This ADR records the architectural decisions and supply chain assessments.

## Guiding Principles

1. Prefer modern, proven third-party solutions. Build only what doesn't exist.
1. Enterprise-grade: evaluate supply chain risk of every dependency.
1. No shim-based tools in the stack. Every dependency must provide native Windows execution.
1. "Orchestrate, don't replace" — applied consistently across all pillars.

## Decision: Two-Pillar Orchestration Architecture

Boilerplate is an orchestration layer with two pillars:

| Pillar                       | Orchestrated Tool                                     | Boilerplate Adds                                                                                                                                              |
| ---------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Templates**                | Copier (rendering, answers, three-way merge)          | Composition (`extends` DAG), lock files, catalog, trust model                                                                                                 |
| **Environment Provisioning** | proto (tool installation, 800+ tools, cross-platform) | Profile composition (`extends`), `.boilerplate/environment.yml` (profile provenance), enterprise trust. Tool-level locking delegated to proto's `.protolock`. |

### Template Composition is the Core Differentiator

Composition gives "the experience of a singular template, built from many variants." This is Boilerplate's reason to exist. No other tool provides declarative template composition on top of Copier. Copier's own template inheritance ([Issue #934](https://github.com/copier-org/copier/issues/934)) has been open since Jan 2023 with no implementation.

### Environment Provisioning Orchestrates proto

[proto (moonrepo)](https://moonrepo.dev/proto) handles the hard part of environment management: installing 800+ tools across platforms via WASM plugins. Boilerplate uses proto's native `.prototools` schema and adds what proto lacks: profile composition, `.boilerplate/environment.yml` (profile provenance), and enterprise trust/validation, with tool-level version locking delegated to proto's `.protolock`, and proto invoked via subprocess behind a `ProtoWorker` interface.

### Implementation Language: Python

Python is the right choice because Boilerplate builds directly on Copier (a Python library) — Rust would force subprocess invocation, losing type safety, shared error handling, and direct use of Copier's `Template`/`Worker` objects. Performance is not a concern: operations are I/O-bound (YAML, files, git), not CPU-bound.

**Copier integration mechanism.** Boilerplate depends on Copier's *internal* `Template`/`Worker` classes (not its public API): it subclasses `Template` to present a merged question schema and hands each layer's scoped view, the merged schema of the layer and its ancestors, to Copier, at compose and at update, through a `Worker` subclass that holds that view in its fields. This coupling is deliberate and contained behind a single audited import shim — see [ADR-002](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/adr-002-copier-internals-shim/index.md) for the mechanism, rationale, and version pin. (A file-based merged-template approach, which avoids the internal dependency, was evaluated and not adopted.)

## Supply Chain Decisions

*Last assessed: 2026-03-20. These ratings should be re-assessed periodically (at least quarterly or when a dependency releases a major version).*

| Dependency       | Risk       | Decision                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    | Last Assessed |
| ---------------- | ---------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------- |
| Copier           | MEDIUM     | Accept — internal `Template`/`Worker` used via the audited shim in [ADR-002](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/adr-002-copier-internals-shim/index.md). Mature project, active development, BSD-3 license. See [copier-org/copier](https://github.com/copier-org/copier); check [scorecard.dev](https://scorecard.dev) for current OpenSSF score. | 2026-03-20    |
| proto            | MEDIUM     | Accept — abstracted via a `ProtoWorker` interface. Younger project from [moonrepo](https://github.com/moonrepo/proto), active development, MIT license. Note: the `unstable-lockfile` feature flag signals `.protolock` is not yet stabilized — monitor for breaking changes.                                                                                               | 2026-03-20    |
| uv               | LOW        | Python toolchain foundation (no shims). Check [scorecard.dev](https://scorecard.dev) for current OpenSSF score.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             | 2026-03-20    |
| Typer            | MEDIUM-LOW | Accept — wraps Click (Pallets); fallback straightforward.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   | 2026-03-20    |
| packaging        | LOW        | Accept — PyPA, no alternative for PEP 440. Declared as a direct dependency.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 | 2026-06-09    |
| logging (stdlib) | NONE       | Chosen — logging via the stdlib `logging` module (Rich console on TTY, plain formatter otherwise). `structlog` was evaluated but **not adopted**; there is no third-party logging dependency.                                                                                                                                                                               | 2026-06-09    |
| graphlib         | NONE       | Python stdlib                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               | 2026-03-20    |
| deepmerge        | HIGH       | **Rejected** — inactive maintenance; merge strategies built inline (`composition/merging/`).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                | 2026-03-20    |
| mise             | HIGH       | **Rejected** — shim-based on Windows (violates the no-shims principle).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     | 2026-03-20    |
| oras-py          | HIGH       | **Deferred** (remote distribution) — immature Python SDK.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   | 2026-03-20    |

Zero shim-based dependencies in the final stack.

### proto Plugin Trust

proto's value is its 800+ tool plugins, but each plugin is third-party WASM code. Boilerplate SHOULD mitigate this by:

1. Maintaining an allowlist of vetted plugins in the environment profile schema.
1. Evaluating plugin signature verification when proto supports it.
1. Documenting the trust boundary: Boilerplate trusts proto; proto trusts its plugin authors; the user trusts the profile author's plugin selections.

This is an accepted residual risk for the environment subsystem, documented so it is not forgotten.

## Consequences

- Environment management orchestrates proto rather than building first-party tool resolvers.
- Merge strategies are built inline rather than depending on `deepmerge`.
- Remote (OCI) template distribution is deferred.
- A first-party trust model is required by Phase 4 entry, per [ADR-003](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/adr-003-permissive-execution/index.md); OCI signatures are deferred until remote distribution lands.

# ADR-002: Depend on Copier's internal Template/Worker via a single audited shim

**Status**: Accepted

## Context

Copier does not expose `Template` or `Worker` in its public API (`copier.__all__` is `load_settings, run_copy, run_recopy, run_update, Phase, Settings, VcsRef`). Boilerplate's composition engine is built on these internal classes: `MergedTemplate` subclasses `Template` to present a consolidated question schema, and every layer's render, at compose and at update, runs through a `Worker` subclass that exposes the layer's scoped view, the consolidated schema of the layer and its ancestors ([design 04 §Scoped view](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/04-composition-engine/#scoped-view)), rather than through Copier's public `run_copy`/`run_update`. These are private symbols Copier may relocate without a deprecation cycle.

## Decision

Funnel all coupling to Copier internals through one module, `src/boilerplate/integrations/copier_types.py`, importing from the modules where Copier actually defines them (`copier._main.Worker`, `copier._template.Template`), and pin Copier to a tested range (`copier>=9.15,<10` in `pyproject.toml`). A relocation of these symbols then breaks one file, loudly, via the guard test (`tests/boilerplate/integrations/test_copier_types.py`) during CI rather than at render time for a user.

**Compose and update share one way in.** Both hand Copier each layer's scoped view through the same `Worker` subclass, built on the `Worker` that `copier_types.py` imports. Compose renders every layer through it, `boilerplate update` runs Copier's update once per layer through it, and every use of Copier internals on either path MUST go through the shim.

**The scoped views live in fields of a `Worker` subclass**, two per update step, and the subclass's `template` property builds `template` from the view in those fields that matches the render Copier is making, together with the `src_path`: the scoped view joined from the recorded versions of the layer and its ancestors for the old copy, which renders the layer's recorded source at its recorded `_commit`, and the scoped view joined from their target versions for the in-place render and the new copy. The property tells the old copy from the other two renders by the render's destination, not by `vcs_ref`, because the three renders can carry one ref when only an ancestor moves; the name prefixes it reads are listed under Audited internals, and the in-place render's destination is the project. Copier's update builds its three renders (the old copy, the in-place render and the new copy) with `dataclasses.replace`, which constructs each new worker from dataclass fields. A template set on one worker instance reaches none of the three renders; `replace` copies a view held in fields into all of them.

**Audited internals (read at Copier 9.18.1).** The shim and its guard test MUST cover each Copier internal Boilerplate depends on: `copier._main.Worker` and `copier._template.Template`; `Worker._apply_update`'s construction of its three renders with `dataclasses.replace`; the `copier._main.old_copy.` and `copier._main.new_copy.` temporary-directory name prefixes (the `prefix` arguments of those two `TemporaryDirectory` calls), which the `template` property reads to tell the old copy from the other renders; the `vcs_ref` the old copy (the subproject template's commit) and the new copy (`resolved_vcs_ref`) carry, which is why the property cannot select a view by ref; and the private `copier._main._operation` ContextVar, which the post-walk task run sets to `"update"` because only `run_copy`, `run_recopy` and `run_update` set it (the `as_operation` decorator) and Copier's task runner reads it (in `Worker._execute_tasks`). The post-walk task run also enters Copier's tasks phase (`copier._types.Phase.TASKS`, the phase `Worker.run_copy` sets with `Phase.use` around Copier's own task run), so a task's `when:` sees `_copier_phase == "tasks"` as it does under Copier. The `Worker` subclass also overrides and calls `Worker._ask`, which compose's questionnaire pass calls to ask the full merged schema once without rendering, since Copier has no public call that only asks. It calls `Worker._execute_tasks` for the post-walk task run, and `Worker._render_context` and `Worker._external_data` for the rejected-answer check, which validates a recorded answer through `copier._user_data.AnswersMap` and `Question` as `_ask` does. A template Copier never builds itself registers its cleanup through `Worker._cleanup_hooks` and `Template._cleanup`, because rendering a VCS template clones it into a temporary directory that only `_cleanup` removes.

A relocation of `Worker` or `Template` inside Copier breaks compose and update in `copier_types.py` alone, where the guard test reports it, and the `copier>=9.15,<10` pin bounds the Copier versions both paths run on. A test MUST drive one per-layer update through the subclass, since a symbol check does not see the `dataclasses.replace` contract the update walk depends on.

## Options considered

- **Scattered `from copier import …` across the codebase** — every upgrade break surfaces in many files, and the top-level import path emits a deprecation warning.
- **Reimplement Copier's render/merge** — large, duplicates Copier, contradicts ADR-001.
- **Vendor/fork Copier** — maintenance burden out of proportion to the need.
- **Single audited import shim + version pin** (chosen) — one change point on upgrade; the deep `_main`/`_template` paths avoid the deprecation warning.
- **Selecting the view by `vcs_ref`** — rejected: when only an ancestor moves, the old copy, the new copy and the in-place render carry one ref and need different views.
- **A merged template set on one worker instance** — rejected: `dataclasses.replace` rebuilds the update renders without it ([Verification (2026-09-30)](#verification-2026-09-30)).

## Consequences

- One file changes when Copier relocates these symbols; the import stays warning-free; ruff + pyright-strict clean.
- Coupled to a private API: every Copier upgrade must be re-validated against the shim's guard test and the per-layer update test.
- The `>=9.15` floor is pragmatic, not a verification gap: 9.15 is the version in use and tested, and we deliberately do not support or look further back (possibly ever). The `<10` cap forces re-validation at Copier's next major.
- **Re-architecture:** this decision stands until the Copier integration is re-architected (e.g., adopting the evaluated file-based merged-template approach); this ADR is then rewritten in place.

## Verification (2026-06-09)

`copier_types.py` is the only site importing Copier internals (grep); `MergedTemplate` subclasses the shim's `Template` (`composition/rendering/models/merged_template.py:14`); the guard test is present.

## Verification (2026-09-30)

Empirical run against the bundled `project` and `streamlit` templates (Copier 9.18.1, Windows, local git clones, `--defaults`, `skip_tasks`): both layers cloned into tagged git repositories, a project composed by `boilerplate new` and rehomed to the clones. Each new tag edited the README line that renders `project_name` and appended a file rendering seven inherited answers; a user line appended to the README before the first update had to survive.

| Mechanism                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               | Orders                                                                 | Result                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| A `Worker` subclass holding the merged questions and the extension union in fields, `template` built from them; `Worker.run_update()` called on the subclass instance per layer with the union of the per-layer answers files as `data` (the merge order of the union was not recorded) | `project` then `streamlit`, and `streamlit` then `project`; v2 then v3 | All 8 updates exit 0, with no conflict markers, no `.rej` files and no unmerged paths; the five inherited answers that Copier records persist in `streamlit`'s answers file after every update; the two derived values render (`widget_co`, `widget-co`); the package directory and the user line survive |
| `worker.template` set to the merged template on one instance                                                                                                                                                                                                                            | Both orders                                                            | The first `streamlit` update exits 0 but its answers file loses the five inherited answers and the derived values render empty; the second update pauses with conflict markers in `README.md` and the probe file                                                                                          |

## Verification (2026-10-06)

Empirical run against the bundled `project` and `streamlit` templates (Copier 9.18.1, Windows, git 2.55, one tagged git repository per layer, `project` and `streamlit` composed at v4 under their scoped views): `project` v5 removed a question its v4 files rendered, and `project` was updated v4 to v5 through a `Worker` subclass holding one scoped view per ref. The old copy rendered under the v4 view with the value recorded in `project`'s answers file, also in a control run that passed no data at all, and the update finished with no conflict markers, no `.rej` files and no unmerged paths; the answers file then dropped the removed question. The per-layer views, their answers files and their extensions are recorded in [ADR-015 §Verification (2026-10-06)](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/adr-015-idiomatic-artifacts/#verification-2026-10-06).

## Relationship to other ADRs

- [ADR-001](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/adr-001-build-vs-adopt/index.md) records the *decision to adopt Copier*. This ADR records the *mechanism* of that integration: Boilerplate depends on Copier's internal `Worker` and `Template` through the shim. A file-based merged-template approach that would avoid the internal dependency was evaluated and not adopted.
- [ADR-015](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/adr-015-idiomatic-artifacts/index.md) — the update walk this shim serves: every render of every layer's update sees the layer's scoped view at the versions it renders.

# ADR-003: Render with Copier `unsafe` — no task/extension consent gate

**Status**: Accepted (current posture; deliberately diverges from the target security model)

## Context

The security design ([Security model](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/10-security/index.md), [Template system and discovery](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/03-template-system/index.md)) specifies a default-deny posture: template tasks and Jinja2 extensions run only behind user consent (`--allow-tasks`/`--allow-extensions`), a package allowlist, an import blocklist, a `SandboxedEnvironment`, and a binary trust model. **None of that is implemented** — see [Implementation status](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/status/index.md) (trust / sandbox / consent: "no code exists").

## Decision

Every operation that runs a layer through Copier's `Worker` grants `unsafe` per layer, exactly where that layer needs it: when the `_jinja_extensions` union of the layer's scoped view is non-empty ([04 §Copier Worker Interface](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/04-composition-engine/#copier-worker-interface)) or when the operation will run the layer's tasks or migrations. Compose, `update` and `add` follow this one rule. A layer's `update` step reads two views, the recorded release's and the target's, and needs the grant when either does. A layer that needs nothing keeps Copier's own consent gate. There is no prompt, sandbox, trust level, or blocklist anywhere — whatever a template declares, executes.

Public exposure is sanctioned under this posture while template sources are local and deliberately chosen: strangers installing the CLI and rendering templates is in scope and does not wait for the trust model.

The posture keys on the template's source, not the destination, so `new` and `add` are equal under it.

## Rationale

- The trust / consent / sandbox infrastructure is not built; gating on a non-existent system would block all rendering.
- Template sources are **local-only** — the bundled first-party templates, plus local directories the user supplies deliberately (`--templates-dir`), which are user-chosen rather than first-party: `build_template_catalog` (`cli/utils.py`) constructs a `DirectoryTemplateRepository` directly, and a Git-backed repository remains unimplemented. The code an `unsafe` render executes is code the user already has on disk and chose to render — the same trust act as running any downloaded script.
- Publication changes who runs boilerplate, not where template code comes from, so going public leaves that boundary intact.
- Recording the gap explicitly so it is a conscious posture, not silent drift.

## Consequences

- Rendering a template that declares tasks or extensions executes them as arbitrary local code with no gate. Acceptable **only while sources are local and deliberately chosen** — bundled first-party templates or user-supplied directories.
- **This MUST be tightened before** remote/Git sources, a catalog with third-party entries, or community templates ship. That work is the trust model in [Security model](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/10-security/index.md) and will get its own ADR when built.
- The design docs describe the *target* (default-deny); this ADR is the honest record of the *current* posture and the divergence.

## Expiry

This ADR records a **temporary** posture, not the target. It expires when the trust / consent / sandbox model ([Security model](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/10-security/index.md)) is implemented — which MUST happen before any remote, catalog, or community template source ships. A new ADR will then record default-deny as the current posture and supersede this one.

## Verification (2026-08-15)

`composition/rendering/engine.py` computes `layer_needs_unsafe` from the merged extension union and the layer's runnable tasks, and passes `"unsafe": layer_needs_unsafe` per `Worker` invocation. Grep across `src/` for `trust|sandbox|consent|blocklist` → no implementation.

# ADR-004: Coarse exit-code taxonomy, with fine diagnosis in BP\* codes

**Status**: Accepted

## Context

A CLI can expose either a rich set of numeric exit codes or a coarse set plus a separate diagnostic channel. The design ([Data models](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/02-data-models/index.md)) argues against exit-code proliferation.

## Decision

The CLI defines exactly six exit codes — `SUCCESS=0, FAILURE=1, CONFIG_ERROR=2, VALIDATION_ERROR=3, ACTION_REQUIRED=4, USER_CANCELLED=130` (`constants.py`; the canonical table is [Data models](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/02-data-models/index.md) §Exit Codes) — and maps the `BoilerplateError` exception hierarchy onto them in one place, the `cli_error_handler` decorator (`cli/utils.py`); the `ActionRequiredError` base exception routes to `ACTION_REQUIRED=4`. `USER_CANCELLED=130` uses 128+SIGINT, the Click/Typer convention for Ctrl-C, and `cli_error_handler` maps `UserCancelledError`, raised when the user cancels an interactive prompt, to it ([Data models](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/02-data-models/index.md) §Exit Codes). Fine-grained diagnosis is carried by per-exception `BP*` codes and `remediation` hints (surfaced as `Fix:` lines), not by additional exit codes.

## Options considered

- **Rich numeric exit codes per error class** — couples scripts to internal taxonomy; proliferates.
- **Six coarse codes + structured BP\* codes/remediation** (chosen) — stable script contract, with rich human/machine diagnosis carried out-of-band.

## Consequences

- Scripts branch on a small, stable set; detail comes from the `BP*` code + message.
- A new error maps to one of the coarse codes; contributors add a `BP*` code + remediation rather than a new exit code.
- `ACTION_REQUIRED=4` is reserved for recoverable workflow pauses ([Data models](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/02-data-models/index.md) §Exit Codes) — the operation needs user intervention before it can complete, as distinct from a hard failure (exit 1). `MergeConflictError` (the composition config-merge error) is a hard failure and stays on exit 1; the update file-conflict pause is the condition that exits 4.

## Verification (2026-06-09, re-verified 2026-07-16)

`constants.py` defines the six-value `ExitCode` IntEnum; `cli/utils.py` `cli_error_handler` maps exception classes to them; `common/exceptions.py` carries `error_code` + `remediation`; covered by `tests/boilerplate/cli/test_utils.py`.

# ADR-005: Integrity model — filesystem-permission-based; cryptographic signing deferred

**Status**: Accepted

## Context

In Boilerplate's current operational model, **one file** carries security-relevant content that could be tampered with to alter behavior:

1. **The lock file** (`boilerplate.lock`) — records the committed state of every template layer in a composition, the per-layer Copier-answers hashes, and the resolved layer ordering. `lock verify` uses it as the source of truth for supply-chain drift detection.

An attacker who can write to this file can neutralise a key control: corrupting or substituting the lock file silences drift detection. Its integrity therefore matters.

It is a local file on the operator's machine. The immediate threat the current control addresses is an unprivileged local process with write access to it — not remote substitution. The current release addresses this with filesystem permissions and defers cryptographic signing, which the spec names as "planned for a future release."

## Decision

The current release relies on **filesystem-permission-based integrity** for the lock file (`boilerplate.lock`) — the sole filesystem-permission-protected artifact — and performs **no cryptographic signature verification**.

For the lock file, the spec states ([10-security §lock verify](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/10-security/index.md)):

> Lock file integrity (no cryptographic signature; the file is trusted as-is)

and:

> `lock verify` is a supply chain drift detector, not a full integrity guarantee. For stronger assurance, combine with content signing (planned for a future release).

## Options considered

### (a) Cryptographic content signing — DEFERRED to a future release

Sign the lock file (e.g., with a project-scoped key, Sigstore, or a similar content-signing scheme) so that tampering is detectable regardless of filesystem ACLs. The spec explicitly names this as "planned for a future release." It is the stronger long-term control. It is deferred for now: the signing infrastructure is not yet built, and at the current scope filesystem permissions are the proportionate control for a file that lives on the operator's own machine.

### (b) Filesystem-permission-based integrity — CHOSEN (current)

Rely on OS-level access controls (POSIX permissions / Windows ACLs) to prevent unauthorised writes. Warn at runtime on overly permissive configurations. No implementation cost beyond the warning check; consistent with the current posture of treating the lock file as a local file guarded by filesystem permissions.

### (c) No integrity control at all — REJECTED

Treating the lock file as fully trusted without any check or guidance would silently degrade the security posture below what the spec intends and provide no operational signal when ACLs are mis-set. The warning-on-permissive-ACL requirement distinguishes option (b) from this rejected baseline.

## Consequences

- `lock verify` is a **drift detector**, not an integrity guarantee. A local adversary with write access to the lock file can substitute values undetected.
- This limitation is **acknowledged in-spec** and is acceptable today, where the lock file lives on the operator's machine and cryptographic content signing is not yet available.
- This decision **SHOULD be revisited** when cryptographic content signing — the spec's "planned for a future release" — is implemented, which strengthens integrity beyond filesystem ACLs; a new ADR will record that change.

## Authoritative spec references

- [10-security §lock verify](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/10-security/index.md) — lock-file integrity scope and the deferred content-signing note

## Relationship to other ADRs

[ADR-003](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/adr-003-permissive-execution/index.md) records a related gap: permissive `unsafe` rendering with no consent gate, ahead of the trust model. Like this ADR, it is a conscious, bounded current posture that expires when the target control is implemented — there, the trust model; here, cryptographic content signing.

# ADR-006: Git-backed template distribution — monorepo authoring, published per-template repos

**Status**: Accepted

> **Scope note.** This ADR **commits** the PROD-001 item `first_party_template_distribution` — the `update` spine depends on it. For what exists in code today, see [Implementation status](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/status/index.md).

## Context

`boilerplate update` orchestrates `copier update`, which performs the three-way merge. Copier's update is **git-only**: it computes the merge base by diffing the template's old git ref against the new ref. Templates authored as subdirectories of the package have no per-template git history and no version tags, and a `pip install`-ed wheel carries no `.git` at all, so a layer rendered from the wheel cannot be updated by `copier update`.

[ADR-015](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/adr-015-idiomatic-artifacts/index.md) sharpens what a distribution channel has to satisfy: the per-layer answers file is the **distribution contract**. Whatever Copier records there as `_src_path` and `_commit` must stay resolvable by vanilla Copier, on any machine, indefinitely — that is what keeps every git-backed layer updatable, by `boilerplate update` and by the escape hatch, a hand-run vanilla `copier update -a .copier-answers.<layer>.yml` per layer with its ancestors' answers passed as data ([ADR-015](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/adr-015-idiomatic-artifacts/#decision)). A channel that cannot be named in an answers file and re-resolved later is not a channel.

## Decision

Templates are **authored in a monorepo** (templates as subdirectories — good authoring DX, atomic cross-template changes). At **release time** each template is **deterministically extracted** (`git subtree split`) into its own git repository carrying full history and `vX.Y.Z` tags. Those repositories are **published, and they are the canonical first-party distribution channel.**

- **What gets recorded.** `new` and `compose` render first-party layers from the published repository, so the answers file records the published URL as `_src_path` and a real tag as `_commit`, and the lock records the same. Nothing a user's project points at is machine-local.
- **Versioning.** Per-template tags (`vX.Y.Z`). The Template Specifier `name@version` maps to "the `name` repo at tag `vX.Y.Z`", and Copier's `--vcs-ref` is an honest passthrough. One repository per template gives each template its own version stream natively, with no mapping layer.
- **A repository is a release train.** Templates share a version stream only when they genuinely release together — one repository carries exactly one PEP 440 tag series, and Copier resolves "latest" from it.
- **The wheel bundle is deferred.** Shipping bundles inside the wheel and cloning them to a per-user cache remains available as an *offline seed cache*, built only on demonstrated demand. A cache path **MUST NEVER** be recorded as `_src_path`: Copier records the source it actually used, and masking a local path behind a canonical URL would mean rewriting Copier's answers file, which [ADR-015](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/adr-015-idiomatic-artifacts/index.md) forbids. Until such a cache exists, the offline and air-gapped story is org-local clones or mirrors of the published repositories — pure Copier mechanics, portable inside the org, with rehoming a one-line `_src_path` edit.
- **Third-party parity.** A single-template repository is Copier's mainstream idiom, so third-party authors get first-party treatment by doing the ordinary thing. Monorepo authoring plus extraction is tooling we may share later, never a convention anyone must adopt to be a first-class template.
- **Reproducibility invariant.** The extraction is deterministic over un-rewritten history: same source commit → same extracted SHA across builds, so a lock's and an answers file's recorded `commit` keeps resolving against the published repositories. Published repository history is therefore **append-only** — never force-pushed, never re-created — because users' answers files and locks record commit SHAs from it, and a re-extraction that produced different SHAs would orphan every recorded commit.

**URL durability is a cutover coupling.** Published repository names are recorded permanently in user projects, so their naming rides the public-cutover naming decision and must be settled before the first release that records them.

**Sequencing.** The build-pipeline responsibility is deterministic extraction plus publishing; the per-user cache leaves the critical path entirely. One consequence is *open*, not settled: because a project is only updatable if its answers files name a resolvable git source, un-stubbing the git source became a prerequisite of the updatable-project outcome rather than a catalog-federation nicety. The [roadmap](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/roadmap/index.md) owns that sequencing question.

## Options considered

- **Shared bundle or monorepo served directly to Copier** (one repository, templates as subdirectories via `_subdirectory:`, simplest build) — rejected on two independent grounds. Copier reads `_subdirectory` from the repository's *root* config, so serving several templates from one repository requires a root `copier.yml` with a dynamic `_subdirectory` and every template's questions `when:`-gated in that one file; per-template question schemas stop being self-contained artifacts. And one repository carries exactly one PEP 440 tag series, so independently versioned templates either release in lockstep — exporting spurious version bumps to downstream `extends` constraints — or become invisible to Copier's version resolution.
- **Published per-template repositories (chosen)** — clean Copier semantics (one template, one repository, plain tags, no `_subdirectory:`), forkable artifacts, per-template version streams, at the cost of build-time extraction and a determinism discipline: don't rewrite history, pin the split tool.
- **Authoring in separate repositories from the start, federated by submodules** — dominates on artifact realness but makes a coupled cross-template change three commits, adds contributor friction at debut, and turns a pinned set back into lockstep by another name. Deferred as an organization convention, not the first-party mechanism.
- **Extraction into bundles shipped inside the wheel** — rejected: the per-layer answers file is the distribution contract, and a per-user cache path recorded as `_src_path` does not resolve on any other machine. The bundle survives only as the deferred seed cache above, which is never the recorded source.

## Consequences

- A new build-pipeline responsibility: deterministic per-template extraction plus publishing, with tags kept in sync with each template's `boilerplate.yml` version — the release-pipeline half of that is INT-010 (see the [intentions register](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/intentions/index.md)). Publishing the extracted repositories falls outside INT-010 as currently scoped: its `not_included` excludes template publishing and registry hosting, so no intention owns the canonical channel today. Either INT-010 widens or a new intention takes it; that ownership question is open, and this ADR does not settle it.
- First-party templates become ordinary remote `git` sources, which meets [ADR-003](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/adr-003-permissive-execution/index.md)'s own stated trigger for tightening: its permissive render posture is acceptable only while sources are **local** and deliberately chosen, and its rationale — that an unsafe render executes code the user already has on disk — does not hold for a template fetched over the network. Whether that trip-wire re-scopes (to third-party or otherwise untrusted provenance) or fires as written (consent gating lands with the git source) is an open question ADR-003 owns and must resolve before the git source ships. This ADR does not decide it.
- A default install needs network access on first use: first-party layers render from the published repositories, so scaffolding no longer works from the wheel alone. That interacts with the designed `--offline` semantics ([design 05](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/05-cli-reference/index.md)) — an offline run depends on an org-local clone or mirror already being present — and it is what the deferred seed cache would address.
- The create path carries the git dependency as well as `update`: a project is updatable only if what `new` and `compose` recorded is a resolvable git source.
- `update` dogfoods against the published repositories, or against local clones during development — Copier treats the two identically.
- Air-gapped *environment provisioning* is a separate, harder problem (proto/tools) owned by Environment Provisioning ([design 08](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/08-environment-provisioning/index.md)), not here.

## Relationship to other ADRs

- [ADR-001](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/adr-001-build-vs-adopt/index.md) — "orchestrate Copier"; this is how first-party templates become git-orchestratable.
- [ADR-003](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/adr-003-permissive-execution/index.md) — making first-party templates remote git sources meets ADR-003's own trigger for tightening the permissive render posture; whether that trip-wire re-scopes to untrusted provenance or fires as written is ADR-003's open question, to be resolved before the git source ships.
- [ADR-007](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/adr-007-update-model/index.md) — consumes the per-template git history this ADR ships.
- [ADR-015](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/adr-015-idiomatic-artifacts/index.md) — supplies the answers-file-as-contract invariant this decision is derived from.

# ADR-007: Safe-update model — conflict is a pause, structural change is migration-driven

**Status**: Accepted

## Context

`boilerplate update` performs a per-layer `copier update`; Copier performs the only merge (INT-003, [04 §Safe Update](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/04-composition-engine/index.md)). Three questions bear on the update model: (1) what happens on a merge conflict, (2) what happens when the template's `extends` chain changed since lock time (the [ADR-001](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/adr-001-build-vs-adopt/index.md) HIGH-severity gap), and (3) whether `update` must walk one version at a time within a layer when a template version can carry a migration. On (1), [06 §Step 5](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/06-project-lifecycle/#step-5-failure-and-conflict) specifies that a conflict brings back the finished layers with Copier's markers and exits 4 (`ACTION_REQUIRED`), after which the user resolves, commits and reruns `boilerplate update`, and [Data models](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/02-data-models/index.md) records the pause as the `conflict` MigrationRecord state. The `MergeConflictError → exit 1` row in the [Data models](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/02-data-models/index.md) Error-Hierarchy table is a *different* condition — the composition-time config-merge error (two layers declaring incompatible values for one key, per [Composition engine](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/04-composition-engine/index.md)) — unrelated to the update file-conflict. This ADR states the model on (1) and decides (2) and (3).

## Decision

**A conflict is a designed pause, not a failure.** On a layer reporting conflicts, `update` stops the walk, copies the layers finished so far into the working tree as uncommitted changes with Copier's conflict markers, records a `conflict` MigrationRecord, writes no lock, and exits **4 (`ACTION_REQUIRED`)**. The user resolves the markers, commits as with plain Copier, and reruns `boilerplate update`; the rerun resumes from the `conflict` record, which names each layer's target and the layers the walk finished, and writes the new lock and a `success` record. The user sets the partial update aside as [06 §Setting a partial update aside](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/06-project-lifecycle/#setting-a-partial-update-aside) describes. **Every other error before the copy back removes the staging worktree** ([06 §Staging worktree](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/06-project-lifecycle/#staging-worktree)), which leaves the working tree unchanged with no lock and no migration record, and exits by the error's class (1 for an unexpected failure). INT-003's "atomic, no partial state" guarantee applies to *failures*; a pause is intentional.

**A changed `extends` chain is handled by author migrations, not provenance inference.**

- *Added* layer → a fresh `copier copy` that writes only paths not already present, so a descendant's file keeps its precedence as at compose, + new answers file, folded into the lock; the update reports the colliding paths it left.
- *Removed* layer (one that joined through `extends` and that the root's target no longer reaches; a layer `add` introduced stays, [06 §Step 3](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/06-project-lifecycle/#step-3-build-updateplan)) → Boilerplate drops it from the managed set; **file cleanup is the job of a Copier `_migrations` script in the template that removed the dependency** (the removed layer's own migrations never run, because it is no longer in the chain). Copier runs migrations across the version range in a single pass — Boilerplate does not loop (see [§Version jumps](#version-jumps-stay-single-pass-migrations-are-jump-safe-by-authoring-contract)).
- *No migration provided* → **safe-orphan + WARN**: leave the files in place (now unmanaged), name them, and give guidance. Boilerplate **never infers file provenance and never auto-deletes.**
- Dry-run preview cannot predict migration file effects (they are arbitrary scripts — Copier's `--pretend` has the same limit); the plan shows version/layer deltas and *which* migrations will run.

**Update behavior is per-layer**, keyed on git-backing (see [ADR-006](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/adr-006-template-distribution/index.md)): published-repo and local-git layers update three-way. A plain local-directory layer (`commit: null`, marking a non-git source) does not update: Copier has no two-way fallback, so a layer with no recoverable old ref refuses to update, and `boilerplate update` skips it with a warning ([ADR-015](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/adr-015-idiomatic-artifacts/index.md) point 5; [§06](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/06-project-lifecycle/#step-4-three-way-merge)).

**`commit: null` costs a ref to check out, not recoverable information — but it does not heal itself.** The lock records the layer's *version* even when `commit` is null, and Copier reconstructs the three-way merge base by *re-rendering* the old version rather than storing one, so nothing needed for a later merge is lost. What a null commit does withhold is the ref Copier checks out to do that re-render, and Copier resolves that ref from `_commit`/`_src_path` in its own answers file — which [ADR-015](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/adr-015-idiomatic-artifacts/index.md) forbids Boilerplate from rewriting. A first-party layer created before [ADR-006](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/adr-006-template-distribution/index.md)'s published repositories exist therefore stays **copy-only** until its `_src_path` is rehomed to the published repository by hand: the documented one-line edit of [ADR-015](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/adr-015-idiomatic-artifacts/index.md) point 5. After that edit the recorded version resolves to a tag, Copier reconstructs the base by re-render, and the three-way merge proceeds normally. Copy-only is permanent **only** for *genuinely* non-git sources (a user's plain local directory, which never gains a tag). Recording the real `commit` at creation stays strictly stronger (an immutable pin vs. a mutable tag) and remains the target.

**Git-backed distribution ([ADR-006](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/adr-006-template-distribution/index.md)) is not a prerequisite of lock creation.** Because a `commit: null` lock withholds only a ref and no recoverable information (above), `new` / `lock` / `verify` / `adopt` do not wait on the published distribution; what they cannot promise for a layer created before it is a clean three-way `update`, which needs the one-line `_src_path` rehome first. The rehome is a user-run edit, so the distribution work gates the clean-three-way quality of update-apply and does not block lock creation. Where it lands in the sequence is the roadmap's call.

### Version jumps stay single-pass; migrations are jump-safe by authoring contract

`update` crosses a layer's version range in a single pass and does not walk one version at a time, even when the crossed versions carry migrations. The evidence is in [§Verification](#verification-2026-07-28), which established:

- **Copier's migration model is fix-up, not replay.** A migration's `version:` key is a *gate* (`target ≥ version > source`), not a checkpoint. In a v1→v3 jump every crossed migration runs exactly once, in list order, all against the same tree — the pre-update tree for `before`-stage entries, the fully rendered target tree for `after`-stage ones (the default stage). **No intermediate tree is ever materialized.** A migration that assumes it sees the tree as of the version it names is therefore wrong under any jump.
- **The migration list comes only from the target version's `copier.yml`.** Nothing is read from intermediate tags. Two consequences bind template authors: every historical migration entry MUST be carried forward in every later release, or jumpers silently skip it; and a stepped walk executes each intermediate tag's *own copy* of a migration, so stepping and jumping can run **different code** for the same nominal migration — stepping is not a safer subset of jumping, it is a different execution.

**Why stepping is not adopted anyway** (reasoning from the above, not separately measured): each step is another three-way merge against the same layer, so each is another chance to pause on the same overridden files, and — because migrations are arbitrary commands with no layer awareness (below) — another chance for a base-layer migration to touch overlay-owned files. Stepping also requires Boilerplate to enumerate and walk intermediate tags: a loop Copier does not provide (verified absent from its update path in 9.15.0), which [ADR-001](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/adr-001-build-vs-adopt/index.md) says we do not build for ourselves.

**The authoring contract that makes single-pass safe** (first-party templates MUST; documented for third parties):

1. **Jump-safe:** a migration inspects actual state before acting and is idempotent — never "the tree is at version N-1, so move X to Y" but "if X exists, move it to Y." It must be correct when run against the target tree with any supported older version as the source.
1. **Carried forward:** historical migration entries stay in `_migrations` in every later release, in ascending version order — Copier executes the list in declaration order rather than sorting by version (read from Copier's source; ordering was not exercised empirically).
1. **Layer-scoped by discipline:** a migration touches only files its own template owns. Copier has no ownership model — a base-layer migration can overwrite an overlay-owned file silently, and a later update of the owning layer will not detect, conflict on, or repair it.
1. **Conflict-aware:** an `after`-stage migration MUST tolerate conflict markers in files it reads. Migrations run even when the merge left unresolved conflicts — Copier reports exit 0 and writes the new `_commit` regardless — and a migration that exits non-zero fails the whole update. Destructive or parsing work belongs behind a state check, not in a bare `after` migration.

**Orchestration consequences.** `boilerplate update` MUST detect the conflict pause itself — via git unmerged paths or a marker scan, never Copier's exit code — and MUST halt the layer walk at the first paused layer rather than running later layers over an unresolved tree. `--skip-tasks` does **not** skip migrations (documented Copier behavior), so there is no built-in defer; the pause envelope is Boilerplate's.
