An update that actually crosses a declared migration requires Copier's `--trust` (a template whose migrations all fall outside the crossed range does not), which `boilerplate update` supplies for first-party templates under [ADR-003](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/adr-003-permissive-execution/index.md) and must gate for untrusted sources — note that the first release introducing a migration is where an otherwise-working non-interactive pipeline starts failing (Copier exits 4 and applies nothing at all) unless trust is passed.

**A paused update resumes from its `conflict` record, not from version comparison.** The `conflict` MigrationRecord names each layer's target version and the layers the paused walk finished ([02 §MigrationRecord](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/02-data-models/#migrationrecord)). When it is the last record, `update` skips the finished layers, walks the remaining layers to the recorded targets and refuses an explicit `--target-version` that differs from them ([04 §Safe Update](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/04-composition-engine/#safe-update)). A layer whose own version did not move still ran under its ancestors' new versions in the paused walk, so only the record tells a finished layer from an unfinished one.

**Deferred, not rejected:** an opt-in `--via <version>` stepped walk, if a first-party migration is ever found that cannot be made jump-safe. That is a template-authoring failure with a tooling escape hatch, not the default model; building it before such a case exists would add a version-walking loop with no demonstrated need.

## Options considered

- **Rollback-on-conflict** — simpler (drops the conflict-pause path), but it throws away the merge attempt and hands the user nothing to resolve; it fights Copier's native model. Rejected.
- **A Boilerplate-owned backup directory with `update --continue` and `update --abort`** — rejected: the staging worktree leaves the checkout untouched until the walk ends, a paused update can be set aside ([06 §Setting a partial update aside](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/06-project-lifecycle/#setting-a-partial-update-aside)) and a rerun of `update` finishes it, so a second state machine adds nothing Copier and git lack ([ADR-001](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/adr-001-build-vs-adopt/index.md)).
- **Pause-with-markers (chosen)** — Copier-native, preserves work, costs the continuation slice.
- Removed layers: **auto-delete uniquely-owned files** (needs a per-layer file manifest in the lock; carries deletion risk) vs **migrations + safe-orphan (chosen)** — author-declared, no data-loss risk.

## Consequences

- The update CLI is `update`, rerun after a conflict (git/Copier idiom), with `--skip-answered` (Copier's name); `--dry-run` (preferred over Copier's `--pretend` where git and Copier idioms clash); `--prereleases` (Copier's name). Operationally-scoped flags may be set per-layer via an allowlisted params object; answers stay merged (the singular-template experience).
- Migrations are arbitrary code — fine for first-party templates (ADR-003), gated behind the trust model before untrusted templates run them.
- Authoring guidance (removed-layer cleanup migration, breaking-change migration) is owned by INT-009; `init-template` may scaffold a commented `_migrations` stub.

## Verification (2026-07-28)

Copier 9.15.0 on Windows, git 2.55. Fixtures: a single-template repo tagged v1/v2/v3, each tag changing a probe file whose content names its version, with version-gated `_migrations` entries whose commands append a JSON record of the migration id, stage, `VERSION_FROM`/`VERSION_TO`/`VERSION_CURRENT`, and the probe file's content as read at execution time — so the log proves which tree each migration saw. Two-layer variants added an overlay template overwriting a base-rendered file. An independent adversarial run repeated the two load-bearing claims with differently shaped fixtures and a marker distinguishing each tag's copy of a migration.

| Claim                                                                      | Result                                                                                                                                 |
| -------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Jump v1→v3 runs every crossed migration exactly once                       | Confirmed — both fired, ascending, one update                                                                                          |
| Intermediate migrations see the target tree, not an intermediate one       | Confirmed — `after`-stage probes read the v3 tree; `before`-stage probes read the pre-update tree; no v2 tree ever existed             |
| The migration list is read only from the target version's config           | Confirmed — a migration present only in v3's config still fired for a v1→v3 jump, and a stepped walk ran each tag's own copy           |
| A step-wise walk runs each migration once against a true intermediate tree | Confirmed — and re-running an already-current update is a no-op                                                                        |
| Migrations run despite unresolved merge conflicts                          | Confirmed — the `after`-stage migration read a file containing conflict markers; exit 0; the answers file advanced to the new tag      |
| A migration can silently overwrite another layer's file                    | Confirmed — a base-layer migration replaced overlay-owned content, and the overlay's own later update neither detected nor repaired it |

Read from Copier's source rather than exercised: `_migrations` executes in declaration order rather than sorted by version; `--skip-tasks` does not gate migrations (also stated in Copier's own configuration docs); trust is demanded only when a version-gated migration falls inside the crossed range. Measured incidentally: an update crossing a migration without `--trust` exits 4 and applies nothing at all.

## Relationship to other ADRs

- [ADR-006](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/adr-006-template-distribution/index.md) — supplies the per-template git history that update diffs against.
- [ADR-015](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/adr-015-idiomatic-artifacts/index.md) — the per-layer walk this ADR's update model executes; its verification records the companion per-layer run, while the migration evidence is recorded in [§Verification](#verification-2026-07-28) above.
- [ADR-003](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/adr-003-permissive-execution/index.md) — migrations share the task/extension trust surface.
- [Data models](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/02-data-models/index.md) and [Project lifecycle](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/06-project-lifecycle/index.md) — own the conflict model this ADR states: the update `conflict` state exits 4.

# ADR-008: Distribution name — publish as `boilerplate-cli`, keep `boilerplate` as the command and brand

**Status**: Pending — the default decision below stands *unless* the current PyPI `boilerplate` owner agrees to surrender the name. A voluntary-transfer request to the incumbent is outstanding; [PEP 541](https://peps.python.org/pep-0541/) is the fallback escalation. This ADR **must** resolve to Accepted before the **first PyPI publish**, because a PyPI distribution name is effectively immutable once published. It does **not** gate the git-URL-first launch (`uv tool install git+https://github.com/TheRealBillSiegler/boilerplate.git`) or the first public tag, which publish no wheel.

> **Scope note.** This is a packaging / go-public decision, not an architecture one. It gates INT-007 (PyPI installability) and INT-010 (publish pipeline), both in the [intentions register](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/intentions/index.md) — the PyPI path only; it does **not** gate the git-URL-first launch, which consumes no PyPI distribution name. It does not touch the import package, the CLI surface, or any persisted schema.

## Context

The PyPI distribution name `boilerplate` is **already taken** by an unrelated package — Kuba Janoszek's *"Easy to use tool for painless project layout templating"* (latest `1.2.4`, 6 releases). That is not a bare name collision: it is the **same niche** (project templating) and it is already at `1.x` while this project is at `0.2.0`. A `pip install`-ed wheel needs a unique PyPI name, so the project cannot publish under `boilerplate`.

Everything else in the project — the import package (`src/boilerplate/`), the CLI command (`boilerplate new`), the repository, the docs, and the brand — uses `boilerplate`, and the maintainer values the name: it is *self-referential* (a tool that emits boilerplate, named Boilerplate), a wink that fires on contact with no jargon. An exploration of replacement names (four rounds, ~220 candidate-evaluations) found **no free standalone name that reproduces that wink**: the wink-firing words (`plate`, `boil`, `boiler`, `chase`, `forme`, `stamp`) are all taken precisely because they are common, and the free survivors are either footnote-jokes (`potboiler`, `stetlock`) or flat descriptions (`roughcut`). Verified free as of 2026-06-20: `boilerplate-cli` on both PyPI and GitHub.

**Mis-install hazard (the load-bearing risk).** `pip install boilerplate` does not fail — it silently installs the *other, same-niche* package. A user who guesses the obvious command gets someone else's project. This is worse than a dead name; it is an active mis-install trap, and it is the primary reason to pursue acquiring the bare name.

## Decision

Conditional on the outstanding name-acquisition request:

- **Default (name not acquired):** the PyPI **distribution name is `boilerplate-cli`**. The import package, the `[project.scripts]` console command, the repository, and the brand **stay `boilerplate`**. In `pyproject.toml`: `name = "boilerplate-cli"`, with `[project.scripts] boilerplate = "..."` unchanged. This rename lands at/before the first PyPI publish, **not** for launch: `pyproject.toml` `name` currently remains `boilerplate` (with `get_version("boilerplate")` in `__init__.py`), and the git-URL install consumes no distribution name, so no rename is required to go public.
- **Contingency (name acquired):** if the current owner transfers `boilerplate` (voluntary surrender, or failing that a granted PEP 541 request), the distribution publishes as **`boilerplate`** and the `-cli` suffix is dropped. The distribution name lives in pyproject / wheel metadata and install docs, not in any persisted user file (the lock and the `EnvironmentProvisionRecord` store no distribution name), so a switch is a packaging change, not a user-data migration — but it **must** land before the first PyPI publish.

The primary install path is the bootstrap installer (`scripts/install.ps1` on Windows; see [Install](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/install/index.md)), which provides uv and installs boilerplate **from git** (`uv tool install git+https://github.com/TheRealBillSiegler/boilerplate.git`) — consuming no PyPI distribution name. *If/when published to PyPI*, the PyPI-specific install instructions MUST lead with the exact `pip install` line for the chosen distribution name and carry a one-line disambiguation note ("not the unrelated `boilerplate` package"). The OIDC trusted publisher binds to the chosen PyPI project name plus the release repo and workflow; if the name changes after acquisition, that binding changes with it.

## Options considered

- **`boilerplate-cli` distribution, `boilerplate` everything-else (chosen default)** — keeps the brand the maintainer values; cost is a permanent install-name ≠ command-name asymmetry and the mis-install trap, both mitigated only by documentation.
- **Acquire `boilerplate` (pursued in parallel)** — the best outcome: no papercut, no trap, brand intact. Rejected *as the plan of record* because it depends on a third party (and, as fallback, PyPI's discretion under PEP 541, where the incumbent's same-niche `1.x` package makes a forced claim weak). The launch cannot be gated on it; it is upside, not the baseline.
- **Real rename (e.g. `boilerkit`)** — a clean single-token brand with no papercut and no trap. Rejected because it discards the literal `boilerplate` brand and its printing-plate heritage, which the maintainer explicitly wanted to keep.
- **Fully-clean alternate token (e.g. `plateworks`)** — PyPI and GitHub both free, but the self-referential wink is weak (most developers do not bridge "plate" → boilerplate). Rejected.

## Consequences

- The default path ships an install-name/command-name asymmetry that surfaces only on PyPI. The primary install surfaces (README, quickstart, install docs) lead with the bootstrap installer / git-URL install and are unaffected by the distribution name; *if/when* published, the PyPI-specific instructions use `pip install boilerplate-cli` (or `uvx --from boilerplate-cli boilerplate`).
- This decision must be resolved (Accepted, under one branch or the other) **before the first PyPI publish** — not merely before the first public tag, since a git-URL-first public tag publishes no wheel. After the first PyPI publish the distribution name is fixed. See the release gate in [Build-out roadmap](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/roadmap/index.md).
- The OIDC trusted-publisher configuration is downstream of the final name and of the decision to publish to PyPI at all; it is **not** required for the git-URL-first launch. Do not configure it until this ADR is Accepted and a PyPI publish is imminent.

## Relationship to other ADRs and intentions

See the [intentions register](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/intentions/index.md) for the full definitions of both:

- INT-007 — org-independence / PyPI-installability gate; this decision is a prerequisite of "installable from PyPI."
- INT-010 — publish pipeline / OIDC trusted publisher; binds to the name chosen here.

# ADR-009: Environment provider protocol — proto is one provider, not the floor

**Status**: Accepted

> **Scope note.** The *shape* recorded here — proto as one provider behind an abstraction — is load-bearing for how the pillar grows, and it reconciles a coherence gap (see Context).

## Context

Environment Provisioning is specified around **proto** as the toolchain installer ([08-environment-provisioning.md](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/08-environment-provisioning/index.md), [ADR-001](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/adr-001-build-vs-adopt/index.md)) — `ProtoWorker` is the only provisioning interface. Two pressures push against that single-tool shape:

1. **Proto-optional provisioning.** The bootstrap script (`install.ps1`) provisions tools via `winget`, not proto. A user who wants a winget-based toolchain with **no proto at all** has no first-class way to express it; with `ProtoWorker` as the only interface, proto is a floor, not a choice.
1. **A "custom command" escape hatch with a promotion path.** The desire to run an ad-hoc provisioning step and *later* "roll it up into something managed."

Both collide with the project's non-negotiable **Reproducibility is mandatory** ([01-overview.md §Core Principles](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/01-overview/index.md)) and the fail-closed trust model: an arbitrary command is non-deterministic, non-pinnable arbitrary code.

A design exploration (prior art: mise backends, asdf plugins, devcontainer Features vs lifecycle hooks, Copier `_tasks`, proto/Nix; plus adversarial verification against this repo's own principles) converged on the model below. `install.ps1` invoking `winget` is **user-run bootstrap** — the *user* invokes the package manager, not Boilerplate. The orchestrated provider protocol (Boilerplate invoking a gated installer) is the only path by which Boilerplate installs a package, and the Trust paragraph below gates it.

## Decision

**Generalize `ProtoWorker` into a Provider Protocol; proto becomes one *kind*, not the interface.** A profile MAY contain zero proto. The abstraction is a **closed set of declarative provider kinds** dispatched by a registry — explicitly **not** an open arbitrary-command runner (an open runner is the exact thing that voids reproducibility and the fail-closed trust model).

**Every provider kind implements three methods:**

- `provision(spec)` — **idempotent**; converges to the pinned target. Idempotency is a precondition because "re-run `env apply`" is the only recovery contract ([02 §EnvironmentProvisionRecord](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/02-data-models/index.md)). Absent → install; present and satisfies the pin → **adopt** (record provenance + observed version, no reinstall); present but violates the pin → **fail closed** (`BP_ENV_ADOPT_PIN_CONFLICT`).
- `verify(spec)` — integrity + an **exact-version** post-condition probe (presence-only `command -v` checks are insufficient). Shared typed return carrying an integrity-strength tier so `env status` renders all kinds uniformly.
- `resolved_state(spec)` — a deterministic pinned-state record.

**Initial kinds (closed enum):**

- **`proto`** — declarative versioned tools; keeps its WASM-sandbox trust posture and `.protolock`. Its `resolved_state` delegates to (hashes) `.protolock` — **no competing `env.lock`**, so "orchestrate, don't replace" holds ([02 §Environment Lock Strategy](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/02-data-models/index.md)).
- **`pinned-artifact`** — *the disciplined form of "custom command"*: a content-pinned fetch-verify-run (exact version + per-platform `https` URL + **mandatory** per-platform `sha256` + a version-assertion probe). Byte-reproducible. This is genuinely **first-party** (nothing external to orchestrate), which ADR-001's two-pillar-orchestration framing must admit alongside orchestrated providers. Free-form shell, unpinned fetch, `curl | sh`, and host-mutating `sudo` are **prohibited** in this kind.
- **`system-package`** — `winget` / `apt` / `brew`. This is *"make the existing advisory [`packages` / `PackageRequirement`](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/02-data-models/index.md) field (already carrying `source` + optional `version`) actually provision, gated,"* not a new concept. Optional `version`: absent → latest today; exact/range later (plural-shape, additive). Records the **resolved** version into the lock. **Best-effort tier** (see Reproducibility).
- **`package-index`** — folds the duplicated `uv.toml` fetch/verify/seed out of `install.ps1` / `setup-wsl-env.sh`. (Note overlap with the plain-file `profile.toml` loader of [ADR-010](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/adr-010-profile/index.md) — see Consequences.)

**Raw arbitrary shell is CUT from this decision.** Its *effect* cannot be locked (you can hash the command string, not its side effects). If ever added, it needs its own ADR **and** an explicit amendment to the "Reproducibility is mandatory" principle — not a smuggled `reproducible:false` carve-out.

**"Roll up into managed" = promote a *definition*, not a snapshot.** Scaffold-not-snapshot (operator supplies version + URL + per-platform sha256 + verify-probe; a past side-effect's content hash and upstream URL cannot be auto-recovered on a fresh host), **operator-performed**, **out-of-band** (never self-declared in the file that ships the step — self-promotion through composition is privilege escalation). Identity / lock-key stays stable across rungs (inline → catalog-named → registered); only the locator changes, so promotion is a registration, not a rewrite.

**Lock & reproducibility.** No separate `env.lock`; per-provider resolved state lands in the `provider_states` map of the `EnvironmentProvisionRecord` ([.boilerplate/environment.yml](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/01-overview/index.md)). Integrity tiers, surfaced honestly (never hidden behind a uniform interface):

| Tier                         | Providers                                        | Guarantee                                                     |
| ---------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Checksum-locked              | `proto` (.protolock), `pinned-artifact` (sha256) | same bytes across time                                        |
| Version-pinned (best-effort) | `system-package`                                 | same *declared version*; bytes are the package manager's word |

Recorded version is a **floor** honored on re-apply: declaration > recorded floor > latest. `env status` reports drift floor-vs-latest **without** silently re-pinning; a deliberate relock advances it. This promotes `provider_states` from a "state, not audit" projection to a **resolution input** — [02 §EnvironmentProvisionRecord](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/02-data-models/index.md) must be amended to say so. Unpinned-latest is allowed (the declaration says "latest"; `env apply` records the resolved version) — state plainly that this **extends** the principle's scope-note logic to the provider domain. **An *explicit* pin that cannot be satisfied fails closed** (`BP_ENV_*`, record not written) — silently installing something else would reduce determinism.

**Trust.** Control is **allowlist-as-ceiling + mandatory pins** (parallel to the existing `allowed_proto_plugins` ceiling, [08 §`allowed_proto_plugins` Enforcement](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/08-environment-provisioning/index.md)): allowlisted + pinned providers need no per-apply consent; ad-hoc / un-allowlisted inline entries prompt interactively and **refuse in CI** until promoted. The new gate **extends** the WASM-sandbox trust *exemption* at [08 §`allowed_proto_plugins` Enforcement](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/08-environment-provisioning/index.md) to non-WASM providers — `pinned-artifact` fetches an https URL and `system-package` shells out, so the sandbox rationale that justified the exemption evaporates the moment a profile uses a non-proto kind.

**Signing.** Local executable-bearing profiles → note + filesystem-permission expectation (the same ADR-005 posture as `boilerplate.lock`); signing stays deferred (a writable-FS attacker who can edit the profile can edit PATH/binaries directly, and local verification is only as strong as a trust root the attacker can't touch). Remote/third-party provenance → signing belongs in the **catalog trust model** ([03 §Trust](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/03-template-system/index.md), [10-security.md](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/10-security/index.md)), not here.

**Naming.** The OS-host axis is **`platform`** (`windows`/`wsl2`/`linux`/`macos`, the existing `packages` key) — **not** `substrate`, which is locked to the enforcement-mode meaning (`enforced`/`preconfigured`, PROD-001, [glossary](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/01-overview/#term-substrate)).

## Options considered

- **Open arbitrary-command runner** — maximally flexible; rejected: voids reproducibility-mandatory and fail-closed trust. Convergent prior art (Copier `_tasks` default-deny, devcontainer Features-vs-hooks) draws the same managed-vs-escape-hatch line.
- **Closed declarative kind-set (chosen)** — every kind must implement `verify` with a real post-condition; a candidate that can't is, by construction, not a provider (the type-level test for escape-hatch abuse).
- **Separate Boilerplate `env.lock`** — rejected; duplicates `.protolock`, violates orchestrate-don't-replace. `provider_states` in the existing record instead.
- **Reuse the template trust gate as-is** — rejected; [08 §`allowed_proto_plugins` Enforcement](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/08-environment-provisioning/index.md) *exempts* profiles because proto runs in WASM. Non-proto providers have no sandbox, so the gate must be **extended**, not reused unchanged.
- **Capture as target (chosen) vs. keep the pillar thin in vision too** — a design review flagged Environment Provisioning as "a second product for users who don't exist yet." Capturing the protocol as *target* honors both that concern and "can't YAGNI a vision"; building it now was rejected as scope creep against the scripts-first decision.

## Consequences

- **Installation is gated.** Boilerplate installs a package only through an allowlisted, pinned provider, or through one the user consents to at the prompt, per the Trust paragraph above. The user-run `install.ps1` bootstrap invokes the package manager itself, so it sits outside this rule.
- **Design-doc changes this decision forces:** generalize `ProtoWorker` → Provider Protocol in [01](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/01-overview/index.md) and [08](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/08-environment-provisioning/index.md); admit first-party providers (`pinned-artifact`) in [ADR-001](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/adr-001-build-vs-adopt/index.md)'s pure-orchestrator framing; amend [02 §EnvironmentProvisionRecord](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/02-data-models/index.md) (`provider_states` is a resolution input, recorded-version-as-floor) and resolve the `tools`-map vs `provider_states` duplication (derive `tools`).
- **Naming hazards:** the plain-file `profile.toml` loader ([ADR-010](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/adr-010-profile/index.md), `settings/profile.py`) vs the `EnvironmentProfile` (`boilerplate-env.yml`) overload; "provider" also names catalog/template git-sources. The `package-index` kind overlaps the `profile.toml` loader — prefer *extending* that loader over reinventing it.
- **Build decomposition (target):** Unit 1 = Provider Protocol + `provider_states` + `pinned-artifact` (the proto-*less* tracer-bullet that proves the abstraction) → Unit 2a = proto refactored in + `system-package` + `package-index` → Unit 2b = active/named configs. Strictly sequential; 2a/2b depend on Unit 1's registry + schema. Substrate/`platform` becoming required on `boilerplate-env.yml` is a breaking change → major bump, spec the migration.

## Relationship to other ADRs

- [ADR-001](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/adr-001-build-vs-adopt/index.md) — "orchestrate, don't replace"; this widens Environment Provisioning to admit **first-party** providers (`pinned-artifact`) beside orchestrated ones (proto).
- [ADR-003](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/adr-003-permissive-execution/index.md) — the executable-bearing-provider trust gate shares the task/extension consent surface; full gating lands with the trust model.
- [ADR-005](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/adr-005-integrity-model/index.md) — signing stays deferred; local profiles inherit the filesystem-permission integrity posture.

# ADR-010: Profiles are plain default-answer files

**Status**: Accepted

## Context

An organization generating projects from shared templates needs to point those projects at its own private package index and container registry. Both are template answers: a value the template asks for, which the organization wants pre-filled on every run.

Default answers are the right shape for this need, for three reasons:

1. **Public by default.** The public product resolves packages from PyPI and GHCR. A default answer overrides that resolution for one user without any template or installer assuming an authenticated organization feed.
1. **Two values, not an apparatus.** The need is two values (`package_index.simple_url`, `container.registry`). A typed model, a layered resolution chain, and a CLI command group are a deep apparatus around a shallow need.
1. **Answers, not an interface.** Exposing a typed model as an interface invites more maintenance than the values earn, and "pluggable org profile" suggests an extension point the product does not offer.

## Decision

**A profile is a plain file of default answers to template questions.** A per-user `profile.toml` at the config root supplies **default answers to template questions**, merged into Copier as *overridable pre-fills* (`load_profile(template)` → `ExecutionContext.profile` → Copier's `user_defaults=` channel, not the forced `data=` channel). Templates declare ordinary Copier questions (`project.package_index_url`, `streamlit.container_registry`) and read them as ordinary answers.

Grammar: two reserved tables, `[defaults]` (any template) and `[templates.<name>]` (one template, overrides `[defaults]`). Keys are open: they are template question names, validated by nothing. A missing file yields `{}`; a malformed file raises `ProfileError`. Templates validate values, not the loader: a profile value's validation belongs in the declaring template's own Copier question (`copier.yml`), never in `load_profile`.

**The interface contract (how it stays coherent as the catalog grows):**

- `[defaults] X` is **best-effort**: it fills question `X` only in templates that declare it, and silently no-ops elsewhere. This is by design, not a gap.
- **Consistency comes from a canonical shared-question vocabulary owned by base templates and propagated by `extends`.** Declare a cross-cutting question once in a base (e.g. `package_index_url` on `project`); every descendant inherits the exact name/type; `[defaults]` then reaches the whole subtree. Verified: a `[defaults]` value reaches `streamlit` because it inherits the question from `project` (inherited questions reach every render of a descendant through its scoped view — [ADR-015](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/adr-015-idiomatic-artifacts/index.md)).
- **No per-template mandatory variable set.** Forcing every template to declare a fixed set is overexposure and couples unrelated templates. Authors declare only the few first-class variation points they intend.
- **No `[templates.<base>]` cascade.** The loader keys on the *invoked* template name; use `[defaults]` for family-wide values, `[templates.<name>]` for one-template overrides. Cascading would couple the settings loader to composition resolution.
- **Scope boundary.** A profile covers *declared questions only* — the customizations a template chose to make first-class. Structure the template didn't ship is a **layer** (`extends`); anything unanticipated is **your own script** after generation. A profile is one of three taps, deliberately the least powerful; it is **not** "the customization interface." (See [ADR-011](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/adr-011-structured-overlay-merge/index.md) for the structured-content gap this leaves.)

**Two answer channels, kept distinct** (`ExecutionContext`):

- `profile` → Copier `user_defaults=` — pre-fills the prompt, **overridable** interactively, taken as-is under `--non-interactive`. This is what a *default* means.
- `context_data` → Copier `data=` — a **forced** answer (prompt skipped); also holds answers threaded between composition layers. Merging profile values into this channel would make them non-overridable.

**Org configuration lives outside the product.** An organization layers its private config *after* the canonical public installer via an org-owned script that writes two plain files: `uv.toml` (machine package resolution + keyring/artifacts-keyring) and `%APPDATA%\boilerplate\profile.toml` (generation defaults). An organization keeps its real setup in its own repository; the public repo documents the generic pattern (fictional `acme`) in [Customization](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/customization/index.md).

## Options considered

- **Typed Profile model with a resolver chain and a `config` command group** — rejected: adds typed-model weight, a CLI surface, and a resolution chain for two values that are just answers.
- **Profile via the forced `data=` channel** — rejected: makes defaults non-overridable (skips the interactive prompt); contradicts "pre-fill, overridable."
- **Mandatory per-template variables** — rejected: overexposure; impossible to anticipate every downstream need anyway.
- **Env-var / CLI override layers on the loader** — rejected: per-invocation overrides already exist (the interactive prompt over the pre-fills, and Copier's forced `data=` channel for scripted runs), so new layers would duplicate channels. The loader stays a plain function, never a source-pluggable resolver; an environment layer returns only if a concrete second configuration source appears.
- **Profile as default answers (chosen)** — a thin merge over Copier's native `user_defaults`; orchestrate-don't-reimplement ([ADR-001](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/adr-001-build-vs-adopt/index.md)).

## Consequences

- `boilerplate.settings` exports `Settings`, `ProfileError`, and `load_profile`; the loader lives in `settings/profile.py`.
- [ADR-009](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/adr-009-environment-provider-protocol/index.md)'s `package-index` provider kind extends the plain-file profile.
- A missing `profile.toml` legitimately yields `{}`, so the loader has no *declared profile that fails to load* state to guard against silently falling back to the public index. The publish-safety concern belongs where publishing happens: a generated project's publish step should fail closed when no explicit target is configured. Boilerplate core stamps values and holds no publish opinion.
- **Deferred** (each with its own trigger):
  - *Named default sets*: one file per set plus an active pointer, switched by a `config` command; every render announces the active set — the loud toggle is part of the design, not polish (a silently stale org/personal switch is the failure mode). Build when a user actually juggles contexts.
  - *Warn-on-unknown-key lint + per-template key discoverability* — the best-effort model's safety net. Build when the catalog is large enough for key collisions and typos to bite.
  - *Profile-declared user tasks*: a `tasks = [...]` list appended to the composition engine's existing `_tasks` accumulation, run last after all template tasks. Interim answer: your own script after `boilerplate new`. Build when someone demonstrably re-runs the same script after every generation.
  - *Shareable-set trust*: profiles are trusted only because they are user-local files. If sets ever become distributable, fetching needs SHA-pinned verification — the trust boundary changes the moment the file crosses a machine boundary. Until then, distribution is the org script's business.

## Relationship to other ADRs

- [ADR-001](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/adr-001-build-vs-adopt/index.md) — orchestrate, don't reimplement: the profile is a merge over Copier's own channel, adding only the `profile.toml` grammar.
- [ADR-009](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/adr-009-environment-provider-protocol/index.md) — its `package-index` provider kind extends the plain-file profile.
- [ADR-011](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/adr-011-structured-overlay-merge/index.md) — the structured-content customization gap that the profile (values only) does not close.

# ADR-011: Structured overlay-merge for downstream customization

**Status**: Proposed (**deferred; not in the open-source release**). Captured because the customization design work surfaced it as the real developer-experience capability for arbitrary structured-file customization; deferred — the 0.x releases ship without it — the three taps of [ADR-010](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/adr-010-profile/index.md) plus the post-generation script escape hatch stand as the release story.

> **Scope note.** This records a *target* decision and changes nothing in the release. It is written now so the gap and the chosen direction are on the record before someone reaches for the wrong tool (post-generation `tomlkit` surgery) as if it were the pattern.

## Context

[ADR-010](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/adr-010-profile/index.md) gives three customization taps: **values** (the profile), **structure** (layers via `extends`), and **behavior** (your own post-gen script). A real gap sits between them: a downstream that wants an *arbitrary structured edit* to a generated file — e.g. change `requires-python` mid-`pyproject.toml` **and** append a `[tool.acme.audit]` section — has only poor options today:

- **Profile** — only reaches *declared* questions; an arbitrary mid-file edit is not a declared slot.
- **Own the file** — the layer ships its own `pyproject.toml.jinja`, duplicating the base's whole file and drifting when the base changes. Brittle for "add one block."
- **Post-generation script** — edit the rendered file with `tomlkit` (Python stdlib can *read* TOML but cannot *write* it), guarded for idempotency. Clunky, hand-rolled per edit. Unacceptable as the *standing* answer for a developer-experience tool.

Copier renders each layer independently with **no merge primitive**, so "reach into the base's output and change it" always bottoms out in one of the above.

Key insight: for a structured file, **"edit in the middle" and "append a section" are the same operation** — the file is a tree, not lines. Both are "set these nodes," expressible declaratively.

## Decision (proposed)

**Extend the composition engine to deep-merge structured-content overlays.** A layer ships `<file>.overlay.{toml,yaml,json}`; after all layers render, the engine deep-merges each overlay into its target file on disk (then removes the overlay marker). Position-independent by construction — one fragment expresses both a mid-file edit and a new section:

```toml
# pyproject.overlay.toml — shipped by an org layer
[project]
requires-python = ">=3.12"     # overwrites that leaf, wherever it sits
[tool.acme.audit]             # adds a new table
endpoint = "https://audit.example/..."
```

Scoped to **structured formats only** (TOML/YAML/JSON). Free-text patching of unstructured files is explicitly **out** — that stays "own the file or script it." Fits the composition engine's mandate (it already merges questions and tasks across layers; this is the same idea applied to file bodies) and fills a gap Copier leaves, so it is build-not-reinvent per [ADR-001](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/adr-001-build-vs-adopt/index.md).

## Open questions to resolve before building

- **List / array-of-tables merge semantics** — append vs replace vs merge-by-key. This is where every merge system lives or dies (kustomize strategic-merge, Helm values). Proposed default: deep-merge, overlay wins on scalar conflict; offer JSON-Patch-style ops (RFC 6902: `replace /project/requires-python`, `add /tool/acme`) for surgical array targeting when deep-merge is ambiguous.
- **Comment/formatting preservation** — a re-serialize is best-effort; acceptable for a generated file (semantic correctness over textual layout).
- **Residual not covered** — *transforming an existing value as a function of its current content* (append to a string, conditional rewrite) cannot be a static overlay; that stays a post-generation script. Rare tail; does not merit machinery.

## Consequences

- Turns "edit the middle + append a section" from a hand-rolled `tomlkit` script into a three-line declarative fragment — the developer-experience bar this tool is held to.
- Adds a post-render merge pass and per-format mergers to the composition engine; the list-semantics decision above is the central design cost.
- No release impact: deferred. If a specific structured edit proves common across the catalog first, the cheaper interim move is to give the *base* template a typed list question for that slot ([ADR-010](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/adr-010-profile/index.md) Tier-1), not to rush this.

## Relationship to other ADRs

- [ADR-010](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/adr-010-profile/index.md) — the profile handles *values*; this handles *structured content* the template did not parameterize. Complementary taps.
- [ADR-001](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/adr-001-build-vs-adopt/index.md) — build-not-reinvent: Copier has no structured merge; this is first-party composition of file content.

# ADR-012: Positioning relative to Copier

**Status**: Accepted; amended 2026-10-20 (one pitch on every surface)

> **Scope note.** This is a documentation-framing decision, not an architecture one. It governs how public-facing docs (README first screen, docs home, the [Why Boilerplate?](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/why/index.md) page) frame Boilerplate's relationship to Copier, and records the evidence that framing rests on. It does not change any behavioral contract.
>
> **Epistemic status.** Boilerplate has no public users yet. Nothing below is first-party data; it is public-signal research on adjacent ecosystems (issue trackers, adoption counts of proxy tools), and every conclusion drawn from it is an inference from proxies. Replace these inferences with first-party signals (issues, installs, feedback) as soon as any exist.

## Context

Boilerplate was extracted from an internal platform team's tooling and generalized for public release. Its public-facing story can be told two ways, and before this decision the repository told neither deliberately:

1. **The narrow pitch** — a composition engine for Copier templates (`extends`, merged questions, deterministic precedence). Concrete and verifiable, but it invites the immediate objection "Copier already documents applying multiple templates."
1. **The broad pitch** — an opinionated Python development system (curated toolchain, layered templates, planned lock/update lifecycle). Differentiated, but its value only fully demonstrates as the catalog and lifecycle features land.

Primary-source research (2026-07) resolved how to weigh these:

**Interest is documented, and upstream leaves it to the community.** Template composition/inheritance is Copier's longest-running unresolved feature request — 15+ distinct threads from 13+ authors, 2018–2025. The canonical thread, [copier-org/copier#934](https://github.com/copier-org/copier/issues/934) ("Updatable templates for template hierarchies and reuse", open since January 2023), sits in Copier's *Community contribution* milestone, whose own description is design-approved but not something the core team will build. Individual maintainer quotes need their context kept: yajo's "a different thing than copier" (2023) addressed a proposed fork/squash-merge update mode, and "with Copier, 1 template = 1 repo" a meta-template repo layout — neither is a blanket rejection of hierarchies, and yajo's first #934 response was a constructive meta-template prototype. The durable signal is the milestone itself. Copier's documented alternative, [applying multiple templates to one subproject](https://copier.readthedocs.io/en/stable/configuring/#applying-multiple-templates-to-the-same-subproject) with one answers file each, officially works only when templates touch **disjoint file sets**; merging shared files such as `pyproject.toml` across templates is the acknowledged unsolved gap ([discussion #1485](https://github.com/orgs/copier-org/discussions/1485), [issue #1738](https://github.com/copier-org/copier/issues/1738)).

**In the closest proxies, composition alone attracted few users; updatability attracted many.** The nearest prior art: [cookie-composer](https://github.com/callowayproject/cookie-composer) (declared multi-template layering for cookiecutter) drew ~21 stars and ~150 downloads/month over four years (as of 2026-07), while [cruft](https://github.com/cruft/cruft) — update-tracking only, same base ecosystem — has ~1,600 stars, and the highest-engagement thread in the space is cookiecutter's update request ([cookiecutter#784](https://github.com/cookiecutter/cookiecutter/issues/784), 43 reactions). This gap is suggestive, not conclusive — the tools differ in timing, marketing, and audience. Consistent with it: #934's own title asks for *updatable* hierarchies, and the users who articulate composition pain are platform teams whose stated motive is maintenance scaling, not initial scaffolding.

**Positioning norms among comparable tools are consistent.** Across uv, ruff, pnpm, pixi, biome, polars, and hatch: every tool that answers "why not X?" does so on the first screen or behind a first-screen link; none buries it; none uses an in-README feature table. The *form* splits by relationship — replacement tools (uv, ruff) lead with benchmarks and parity claims; tools built **on** an incumbent's ecosystem (pixi on conda; hatch on packaging standards) frame the incumbent as foundation, never attack, link outward to its docs, and defer extended comparison to a prose docs page.

**Honest caveats.** Per-thread engagement on composition asks is modest (single-digit reactions); Stack Overflow traffic on the topic is near zero; the one purpose-built predecessor flopped. The addressable market is thin and concentrated in platform teams. Separately, two competitive risks exist: upstream movement on #934 (a maintainer has sketched a "fork-like approach"), and uv absorbing scaffolding scope from below.

## Decision

Position Boilerplate as **a Python development environment paired with templates that build on one another, with Copier as their foundation — foundation framing, not replacement framing** (the pixi/hatch pattern):

- **Name Copier in the first paragraph as the foundation.** State the gap in one sentence: Copier applies multiple *independent* templates by hand; Boilerplate lets template authors *declare* composition, giving consumers one command, one merged question set, and deterministic precedence when layers overlap.
- **Cite the documented gap, respectfully.** The README and the [Why Boilerplate?](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/why/index.md) page may link Copier's own multi-template documentation and #934 — engaging prior art head-on, in the incumbent-as-foundation tone. No benchmarks, no feature-table combat.
- **Scope the compatibility claim to what ships.** Current-state docs say: templates remain standard Copier templates; composition metadata lives in a separate `boilerplate.yml`; `copier.yml` is never modified; a template becomes a layer by adding that one file. The stronger claim — vanilla Copier templates consumable with no added metadata — is not current behavior (the catalog requires `boilerplate.yml`) and MUST NOT appear in current-state docs unless that changes.
- **One pitch on every surface.** The README, the docs home, the package description and the CLI's help line lead with the same role line: a Python development environment, one tool for each job, paired with templates that build on one another. Copier stays the named foundation in the README's first paragraph. Extended "why not plain Copier?" prose lives on the [Why Boilerplate?](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/why/index.md) docs page, not in the README.

## Options considered

- **Foundation framing, first-screen gap statement (chosen)** — matches the norm for built-on-incumbent tools, preempts the predictable "just use `-a`" objection with the upstream's own words, and costs one paragraph.
- **Replacement framing (uv/ruff pattern)** — rejected: Boilerplate has no speed or drop-in-parity story against Copier, and it *depends* on Copier; attack framing would be both false and self-undermining.
- **Not naming Copier at all** — rejected: six of seven comparable tools name the incumbent, and Boilerplate's entire early audience consists of Copier users who will raise the comparison themselves if the docs don't.
- **Splitting the pitches by surface** (the narrow composition pitch in the README, the broad system pitch on the docs home) — chosen at first, then replaced on 2026-10-20: the model of what Boilerplate is gives the development environment the same weight as the templates, and one role line on every surface keeps the front door and the docs from describing two different products. The verifiability argument no longer decides the lead: the environment half is as checkable as the composition half (the installer and the configured picks ship), and Copier stays named as the foundation in the README's first paragraph.

## Consequences

- The proxy evidence (cruft vs. cookie-composer; #934's title) suggests the lock/update workstream (roadmap Phase 3, [adr-007](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/adr-007-update-model/index.md)) may matter more for adoption than composition alone. Weigh this when prioritizing; treat it as a hypothesis to test against first-party signals, not a settled fact.
- At public debut, the most directly reachable audience that has already expressed interest is the [copier-org/copier#934](https://github.com/copier-org/copier/issues/934) thread; a respectful pointer there is low-cost outreach. Caveat: the *Community contribution* milestone invites contributions **into Copier**, not external tools — the comment may present Boilerplate as one experiment toward the ask, never as "the" invited answer.
- Watch items: activity on #934 (upstream building or blessing an approach would change the gap statement), and uv's scaffolding scope. If either materializes, revisit this ADR.
- The mis-install hazard from [adr-008](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/adr-008-distribution-name/index.md) (bare `pip install boilerplate` installs an unrelated same-niche package) remains a positioning liability at every surface that names the package; install docs continue to lead with the git-URL path.

# ADR-013: The Interactivity Contract

**Status**: Accepted

## Context

`boilerplate new` renders in one of two modes: interactive (Copier prompts for unanswered questions) or non-interactive (`--non-interactive` / `--ci`, where every answer must come from a default, `profile.toml`, or a forced answer). Prompting has a failure mode with no natural backstop: when stdin cannot host a real terminal session, Copier's prompt layer (`questionary` / `prompt_toolkit`) does not always raise cleanly on EOF — it can retry-loop, growing memory without bound instead of exiting. This is not hypothetical: an equivalent failure was confirmed live on this project (Windows, stdin redirected from `NUL`, which `isatty()` misreports as a terminal) reaching the prompt layer and hanging before the guard was hardened. It is also a category-wide problem — see Evidence.

This ADR records the decision rationale for the interactivity contract of `boilerplate new` (`src/boilerplate/cli/commands/new.py`, `src/boilerplate/composition/rendering/engine.py`) and its error codes (design [Operational quality](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/07-operational-quality/index.md) §Error Code Registry; design [Data models](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/02-data-models/index.md) §Error Hierarchy), surveyed against primary sources across CLI standards and peer tools, July 2026.

## Decision

### 1. Prompt gating is a proactive stdin-TTY check

Immediately after flag composition (`--ci` / `--non-interactive` resolved to their effective values), and before the template catalog, resolver, composer, or render engine are touched, `new` checks whether stdin can host prompts. If interactive mode is in effect, stdin is not a real TTY, and `--dry-run` was not passed, the command fails closed with `BP_INPUT_TTY_REQUIRED` (exit 3) and a remediation naming the substitute flags (`--non-interactive`, the global `--ci`).

Rationale: Copier's prompt layer can retry-loop on EOF instead of raising. A proactive check refuses the render before that failure mode can occur, rather than relying on the reactive layer (Clause 2) to catch it after the fact.

### 2. A reactive second layer stays

`isatty()` alone can lie. On Windows, `NUL` is a character device and `isatty()` reports `True` for it — confirmed live to pass a naive TTY check and hang in the prompt layer. The proactive guard closes that specific gap with a `GetConsoleMode` probe on the stdin handle: `GetConsoleMode` succeeds only on a genuine console input handle, the same discriminator the prompt layer itself depends on.

Hardening the proactive check does not retire the reactive one. A terminal can pass both the TTY and console-handle checks and still be unable to host `prompt_toolkit`'s rendering (Git Bash pseudo-TTYs, editor-embedded shells, some CI-provided pseudo-consoles). Prompt-layer failures that occur during rendering are still caught and translated to `BP_RENDER_PROMPT_FAILED` (exit 1). The translator additionally recognizes Copier's own `copier.errors.InteractiveSessionError`: Copier wraps EOF-during-prompt in this type with a `builtins` exception as its cause, which would otherwise evade a plain module-prefix match against `prompt_toolkit` / `questionary`. Neither layer subsumes the other — the proactive gate is cheap and catches the common case before any work starts; the reactive layer is the backstop for prompt-layer failures the proactive gate cannot anticipate.

### 3. No input-mode switching on CI environment variables

`CI=true` and vendor equivalents (`GITHUB_ACTIONS`, `TF_BUILD`, and similar) never flip `new` into a defaults-accepting mode. The only mode switches are explicit flags (`--non-interactive`, `--ci`) and their env-var equivalents, `BOILERPLATE_NON_INTERACTIVE` and `BOILERPLATE_CI`, which are tool-scoped opt-ins following the `PIP_NO_INPUT` pattern (an environment variable defined and documented by the tool it controls) — not a heuristic read of ambient CI-identity variables.

Rationale: a CI environment variable answers "am I running in CI?", not "should this tool skip prompting?" Those questions happen to have the same answer on the major CI providers today, but that is not a contract any of them make. A scaffold silently built with wrong defaults propagates through every rendered layer and is discovered late, if at all; a failed pipeline step is discovered immediately, at the point of cause, with a named fix.

### 4. Every prompt has a non-interactive substitute

No template question is reachable only through a prompt:

- **Defaults** (`--non-interactive`) — accept the template's declared `default:` for every question.
- **Persistent pre-fills** (`profile.toml`) — per-user `[defaults]` and `[templates.<name>]` tables that ride Copier's `user_defaults` channel; an interactive answer, or a forced answer, overrides them.
- **A per-invocation answers channel** (`--data` / `--data-file`) — forced answers for a single invocation, on Copier's `data` channel.

`--non-interactive` (and `BOILERPLATE_NON_INTERACTIVE`) is the only defaults-accepting mode for questions; `--yes` governs confirmation prompts only ([CLI reference](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/05-cli-reference/index.md)).

### 5. Read-only operations are exempt

`--dry-run` never prompts. It is checked ahead of the TTY guard (Clause 1) and short-circuits it, so a piped `--dry-run` invocation stays legal — there is nothing to answer and no render to protect.

## Options considered

- **Reactive-only enforcement (no proactive TTY gate)** — rejected: relies entirely on Copier's own EOF handling, which is insufficient on its own (see Evidence — `copier-org/copier#2436`) and leaves the unbounded-retry-loop risk live for every non-TTY interactive invocation, not just the Windows `NUL` edge case.
- **Sniff `CI=true` (or vendor equivalents) to auto-switch to non-interactive** — rejected: binds correctness to an environment-identity contract no CI provider makes; the counterexamples (pnpm, uv) show that even narrowly-scoped CI heuristics are treated by their own maintainers as provisional or safety-only, never as a general "assume defaults" switch.
- **Silently substitute defaults on non-TTY stdin (the create-vite model)** — rejected for this category: workable when output is a single-shot starter reviewed immediately after generation; wrong for a composition engine whose answers propagate through every layer a template extends.
- **Collapse to a single enforcement point** — rejected: the proactive gate cannot see prompt-layer failures that only manifest mid-render (Git Bash pseudo-TTY, editor-embedded shells); the reactive translator cannot prevent Copier's retry-loop from starting in the first place. Each covers a failure mode the other cannot.

## Evidence

Verified against primary sources, July 2026.

**The pattern this decision follows:**

- [clig.dev §Interactivity](https://clig.dev/#interactivity): "Only use prompts or interactive elements if stdin is an interactive terminal (a TTY)... you should throw an error telling the user what flag to pass." §Arguments and flags: "Never require a prompt."
- [gh (cli/cli)](https://github.com/cli/cli): `CanPrompt()` requires both stdin and stdout to be a TTY (`pkg/iostreams`); commands fail closed with named-flag errors when not interactive, e.g. `pkg/cmd/pr/merge`: "`--merge`, `--rebase`, or `--squash` required when not running interactively." No `CI` (or vendor-equivalent) detection anywhere in its environment-variable surface.
- [az (microsoft/knack)](https://github.com/microsoft/knack): a stdin-only TTY check gates prompting; failure message: "Unable to prompt for confirmation as no tty available. Use --yes."
- [rustup-init.sh (rust-lang/rustup)](https://github.com/rust-lang/rustup): `[ ! -t 0 ]` gates the install prompt; failure message: "Unable to run interactively. Run with -y to accept defaults."

**Category peers get this wrong** — the proactive guard (Clause 1) is ahead of the category, not behind it:

- Copier itself reacts to `EOFError` only and still waits indefinitely on stdin that is open but never fed ([copier-org/copier#2436](https://github.com/copier-org/copier/issues/2436)).
- cookiecutter has no EOF handling; a non-TTY prompt surfaces as a raw traceback.
- Yeoman acknowledged the same gap in 2018 and closed the issue stale without a fix ([yeoman/generator#694](https://github.com/yeoman/generator/issues/694)).

**CI-detection counterexamples cut toward fail-closed, not toward auto-switching** (Clause 3):

- pnpm auto-enables `--frozen-lockfile` in CI specifically to *prevent* silent lockfile drift, not to relax behavior ([pnpm/pnpm#1994](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/1994)).
- `uv venv` silently deleting an existing venv when non-interactive is acknowledged by its own maintainers as provisional backwards-compatibility behavior, likely to change ([astral-sh/uv#14309](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/issues/14309)).

**The alternative model exists, and is rejected for this category** (Clause 3 / Clause 4):

- create-vite silently substitutes defaults for non-destructive choices in non-TTY mode (`argInteractive ?? process.stdin.isTTY`), failing closed only on the overwrite prompt ([vitejs/vite, `packages/create-vite`](https://github.com/vitejs/vite/tree/main/packages/create-vite)). Workable for a lightweight, single-shot starter whose output is reviewed immediately; wrong for a composition engine whose answers propagate through every rendered layer.

## Consequences

- `new` refuses to start an interactive render against non-TTY stdin instead of hanging or silently defaulting; the failure is immediate, attributed, and names the fix.
- CI pipelines and other non-interactive callers must pass an explicit flag (`--non-interactive` or `--ci`). Ambient `CI=true` has no effect on `boilerplate`'s behavior, by design; the tool-scoped env-var equivalents (`BOILERPLATE_NON_INTERACTIVE`, `BOILERPLATE_CI`) do not change this — they are explicit opt-ins, not a CI-identity heuristic.
- The TTY check and the prompt-layer translator are two independent code paths (`new.py` and `engine.py`) with different failure signatures and different exit codes (`BP_INPUT_TTY_REQUIRED` is 3; `BP_RENDER_PROMPT_FAILED` is 1). A future refactor MUST NOT collapse them into a single check without re-verifying both failure modes — `isatty()` lying, and prompt-layer failures the proactive gate cannot anticipate — stay covered.
- Clause 4's substitute set is complete: defaults via `--non-interactive`, persistent pre-fills via `profile.toml`, and per-invocation forced answers via `--data` / `--data-file`, plus the env-var equivalents (`BOILERPLATE_NON_INTERACTIVE`, `BOILERPLATE_CI`) for the flags themselves.

## Sources

- [clig.dev — Command Line Interface Guidelines, §Interactivity](https://clig.dev/#interactivity)
- [cli/cli — GitHub CLI](https://github.com/cli/cli)
- [microsoft/knack](https://github.com/microsoft/knack)
- [rust-lang/rustup](https://github.com/rust-lang/rustup)
- [copier-org/copier#2436](https://github.com/copier-org/copier/issues/2436)
- [yeoman/generator#694](https://github.com/yeoman/generator/issues/694)
- [pnpm/pnpm#1994](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/1994)
- [astral-sh/uv#14309](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/issues/14309)
- [vitejs/vite — create-vite](https://github.com/vitejs/vite/tree/main/packages/create-vite)

# ADR-014: Deferred task execution — accumulate per layer, run once on the final layer

**Status**: Accepted

## Context

Copier's contract runs `_tasks` after generating a project, in the destination directory. Under composition, "the project" is the composed whole: layers render sequentially into one destination, and a layer's tasks (dependency installation, `git init`) generally assume the finished project, not that layer's partial contribution. Copier's own multi-template guidance — sequential independent applications — runs each template's tasks at its own apply time, against a project the later templates have not written yet. The closest prior art fails in the other direction: cookie-composer executes each layer's cookiecutter hooks inside a throwaway temp render, so environment side effects never reach the real project, and its documented mitigation is disabling hooks per layer.

## Decision

- **Merge**: `_tasks` accumulates across layers by ordered concatenation — topological order across layers (dependencies first, target last), declaration order within a layer, no deduplication. Tasks are effects; repetition and order are meaningful, so the append-only strategy is deliberate even though files use last-layer-wins.
- **Execution**: every non-final layer renders with `skip_tasks=True` (a public Copier flag); the final layer executes the full accumulated list exactly once, after all layers' files exist. Conditions are evaluated by the final layer's worker against the merged answers.
- **Update**: the update walk renders with `skip_tasks=True` in every render Copier makes during a layer's update (the old copy, the in-place render and the new copy), and the accumulated list runs exactly once against the finished project after the last layer's update, through the same `Worker` subclass under Copier's `update` operation, so a task's `when:` sees `_copier_operation == "update"` ([design 04 §Safe Update](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/04-composition-engine/#safe-update)). Copier would otherwise run each updated layer's own `_tasks` three times per update, twice in temporary directories, and never the merged list.
- **Shapes**: task entries keep Copier's native forms end-to-end — plain string (shell execution), argv list (no shell), mapping with `command` and optional `when`/`working_directory` — so Copier, not Boilerplate, interprets execution semantics. Entries that match none of these shapes are dropped with a warning.

## Options considered

- **Per-layer execution (Copier-native timing)** — rejected: runs a base layer's tasks against an incomplete project (e.g. dependency installation against a `pyproject.toml` a later layer still overrides); the sequential-application precedent inherits exactly this flaw.
- **Deferred single execution (chosen)** — matches the pattern Yeoman institutionalized in its `composeWith` run loop (all composed generators' writing phases complete before any install/end phase runs) and preserves the object of Copier's contract: the completed project.

## Consequences

- A child layer cannot remove or reorder an inherited task; the idiomatic gate is a `when:` condition on the task, which shape pass-through preserves.
- Task provenance (which layer contributed an entry) is not yet carried through the merge. The trust-tier consent and audit design ([03 §Task Execution Safety](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/03-template-system/#task-execution-safety), [Security model](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/10-security/index.md)) requires per-layer attribution and selective execution; that needs a provenance-carrying merge and is deferred work this ADR explicitly does not cover.
- Mid-list failure leaves rendered files with partially applied post-processing — Copier's own no-rollback property, inherited unchanged. Task authors SHOULD keep tasks idempotent.
- `{{ _copier_conf.src_path }}` and `_copier_operation` inside task templates resolve against the final layer's worker, not the declaring layer's.

## Relationship to other ADRs

- [ADR-003](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/adr-003-permissive-execution/index.md) governs the permissive `unsafe` trust posture the deferred execution runs under.
- [ADR-002](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/adr-002-copier-internals-shim/index.md) localizes the `Template`/`Worker` coupling this mechanism drives; `skip_tasks` itself is public Copier API.
- [ADR-015](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/adr-015-idiomatic-artifacts/index.md) — the update walk whose renders skip tasks; its [Verification (2026-10-06)](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/adr-015-idiomatic-artifacts/#verification-2026-10-06) records where Copier runs a layer's tasks during an update.

# ADR-015: Idiomatic artifacts, orchestrated engine — a composed project is plain Copier on disk

**Status**: Accepted

> **Scope note.** This ADR names the paradigm the composition and update designs assume, so later decisions can cite an invariant instead of re-deriving it. For what exists in code today, see [status.md](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/status/index.md).

## Context

The composition goal ([ADR-001](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/adr-001-build-vs-adopt/index.md)) is the experience of a singular template built from many variants. Copier's own idiom for multiple templates in one project is N independent applications, each with its own answers file, each independently updatable — and Copier's update algorithm defines "user changes" as any difference between its own pristine re-render of one template and the actual working tree, which means it has no concept of, and no need for, cross-template awareness. Two pressures meet here: being true to Copier's interfaces and idioms (so users keep every guarantee Copier gives them), and the unified experience that is the product's reason to exist (one question flow, one compose, one update). A single canonical `.copier-answers.yml` written by Boilerplate itself resolves that tension the wrong way: it forfeits per-layer updates and Copier's ownership of its own file.

## Decision

**A composed project MUST carry the same file set and the same file ownership as a project built by running Copier N times by hand, and every git-backed layer MUST stay updatable through the escape hatch of point 1, within the limits that point states** — one measured exception, stated in point 4: each per-layer answers file records its own layer's and its ancestors' answers, which the update walk reads. Idiom governs what persists; product governs what it feels like.

**Composition is Boilerplate's process, not a template property.** A template's `copier.yml` declares its own questions and the parent questions it overrides or extends, and MUST NOT declare a parent question unchanged; a template does not join its own `extends` chain. Boilerplate joins every layer's questions into the full merged schema, which the questionnaire asks once, and joins each layer with its ancestors, every layer its `extends` chain reaches, into that layer's scoped view ([design 04 §Scoped view](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/04-composition-engine/#scoped-view)); it hands the scoped view to every render of the layer, at compose and at update, each render receiving the join of the versions it renders. Copier does all rendering, answers-file writing and three-way merging, and Boilerplate implements none of them.

Composition therefore answers to two reference points at once, and each owns a different half of the result: **rendering** matches, for each layer, the single flattened template that layer and its ancestors would make if merged by hand (one question schema and one extension set per layer, tasks running once against the finished project), under one questionnaire that covers the whole composition, while **artifact structure** matches N independent Copier applications (one answers file per layer, each independently updatable where its source is git-backed). Where a mechanism looks un-idiomatic against one reference point, check it against the other before calling it a deviation. Concretely:

1. **Artifacts are Copier's.** Each first-party template declares `_answers_file: .copier-answers.<layer>.yml` **and ships the answers-file stub** (`{{ _copier_conf.answers_file }}.jinja`) that causes Copier to write it — the directive alone is inert (the [design 04 contract](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/04-composition-engine/#render-behavior)); Copier writes every answers file, and Boilerplate MUST NOT write or rewrite them. The escape hatch is a hand-run vanilla `copier update -a .copier-answers.<layer>.yml` for one **git-backed** layer, with its ancestors' answers passed as data, for example `--data-file .copier-answers.project.yml`; a base layer needs nothing passed, and a layer sourced from a plain directory is copy-only, per point 5. A child layer's answers file records its ancestors' answers, but a vanilla update sees only the layer's own `copier.yml`, and Copier keeps in the answers file only answers to questions the layer's template declares ([Copier: the answers file](https://copier.readthedocs.io/en/stable/configuring/#the-copier-answersyml-file)), so the first hand-run update trims the file to the layer's own keys and the passed data is what supplies the ancestors' answers from then on; an undeclared answer left in an answers file survived one update and rendered empty on the next ([Verification (2026-09-30)](#verification-2026-09-30)). The hatch updates one layer and does not compose, which bounds it twice, and it checks no recorded answer: where a target version retypes a question or tightens its validator, Copier drops an answer it reads from the layer's own answers file and records the new default with no warning. Copier renders the old copy from the layer's own answers file and never from passed data, so once the file is trimmed, a template edit on or beside a line that renders an ancestor's answer conflicts on every run. The next `boilerplate update` refills the file: the walk fills a trimmed file's keys for the old copy from the declaring layer's record, and the in-place render records the full scoped view's answers again. The stop applies only when no layer records a key, before any layer runs, naming the layer and the keys ([design 04 §Safe Update](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/04-composition-engine/#safe-update)). A child layer's derived answers are recomputed only by its scoped view, so the hand-run path pauses on the files that render them, visibly and with conflict markers, and never loses content silently. A layer whose `_jinja_extensions` import from the `boilerplate` package needs that package importable in Copier's environment; the first-party templates do.
1. **Update is orchestration of Copier's update through each layer's scoped view.** `boilerplate update` runs Copier's `update` once per layer, always in composition order (lower layers first, so overrides are re-asserted against an already-updated base and a migration that renames a question rewrites the ancestor's answers file before a descendant's update reads it), and each render of that update sees the layer's scoped view at the versions it renders: the old copy of a layer renders the layer's own template at its own `_commit` and its ancestors at the versions `boilerplate.lock` records, under its scoped view joined at those versions, and the in-place render and the new copy render under its scoped view joined at the target versions, which matches Copier's own rule that the old copy renders exactly as it did. Copier performs the three-way merge, writes the conflict markers, reads each layer's own answers from that layer's answers file and prompts as it does for a vanilla update; Boilerplate passes each declaring ancestor's answers as data for the in-place render and the new copy, fills for the old copy the keys the layer's own file lacks from the declaring layer's record at the start of the walk, stops on a recorded answer the target view rejects, and runs the composition's accumulated task list once against the finished project after the walk, as at compose ([design 04 §Safe Update](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/04-composition-engine/#safe-update) owns these rules; [ADR-014](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/adr-014-deferred-task-execution/index.md)). The scoped view reaches those renders through the same `Worker` subclass compose renders every layer through ([ADR-002](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/adr-002-copier-internals-shim/#decision)). The order is recorded in a project artifact, so replaying the walk by hand does not require guessing it: `boilerplate.lock` lists `layers` in execution order ([design 02](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/02-data-models/#lock-file-model)), and it is plain YAML, so a user replaying the walk reads the order without running Boilerplate. The per-layer answers files do not carry the order; they record `_src_path` and `_commit` per layer and nothing about sequence. A project with no lock — never managed by Boilerplate, or `eject`ed since — therefore has no on-disk order, and reconstructing it by hand means reading the templates' own `extends` chains.
1. **Layer stacking rides Copier's own merge model.** During any one layer's update, every other layer's contribution is user-space by construction — Copier diffs its old pristine render against the working tree, so other layers' files and overwrites are preserved when disjoint from the update and surface as ordinary three-way conflicts when they collide. Composition never needs an all-layers-at-once operation.
1. **The unified prompt experience at compose is deliberate and stays.** Prompting is ephemeral — no artifact records how questions were asked, and the rendered tree a unified compose produces is the tree N sequential Copier runs would produce from the same answers. The [ADR-002](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/adr-002-copier-internals-shim/index.md) shim serves compose and update alike, and one artifact-level deviation follows from it and is deliberate: because every layer's Worker exposes the layer's scoped view, each per-layer answers file records the layer's *own and its ancestors' answers* rather than only that layer's own questions, and nothing of a sibling or a descendant. Copier's `Worker._answers_to_remember` keeps an answer only if the worker's template declares it as a question, and never keeps a hidden or secret one, so a worker that exposes the scoped view records the answers to that view's questions, and the update walk reads each declaring ancestor's recorded answers from that ancestor's file and passes them as data. Compose keeps its single unified pass over the full merged schema, because nothing is recorded and no migration runs at compose. Answers of `when: false` questions such as `project_slug` and `package_name` are derived: each render recomputes them and no answers file records them. A layer's files MAY use only questions its own layer or an ancestor declares; the single-owner pattern [design 04](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/04-composition-engine/#managing-shared-files-across-layers) recommends for shared files applies this to a file assembled from several layers' answers. The view stops at the ancestors because a descendant's context hook or same-named filter would otherwise change an ancestor's files, and an update step takes each question's definition and default from the full merged schema because, without it, a descendant's override of a question its ancestor adds is lost ([Verification (2026-10-06)](#verification-2026-10-06)). The bounded fallback for compose, should the internals coupling ever become untenable, is sequential per-layer `run_copy` with accumulated answers threaded through `data=` — shared questions still ask once, at the cost of grouped-by-layer ordering; for update, it is Copier's public `run_update` per layer with its ancestors' answers passed as data, with the limits of point 1.
1. **The source model is inherited from Copier wholesale, and updateability is a per-layer property.** Remote git sources yield portable artifacts; a local git repository is a full source (tags, update) scoped to machines where the path exists, with rehoming a documented one-line `_src_path` edit; a plain directory is copy-only because Copier records no `_commit` for it — `commit: null` in the lock is the honest no-version-stream marker, not a placeholder. A mixed composition degrades per layer, not per project: `update` walks the git-backed layers and skips non-git layers with a prominent warning.

## Options considered

- **Boilerplate-owned composite answers file** — rejected: wrong author and wrong shape; it forfeits per-layer update, Copier's file ownership, and the escape hatch.
- **Boilerplate-implemented cross-layer merge or update metadata** — rejected: reimplements what Copier already provides per layer, contradicting [ADR-001](https://therealbillsiegler.github.io/boilerplate/0.4/design/adr-001-build-vs-adopt/index.md).
- **Fully idiomatic compose (sequential per-layer prompting)** — rejected as the default experience: it forfeits the singular-template question flow, which is the product thesis at the moment of first contact; retained as the named fallback in point 4.
- **Idiomatic artifacts, orchestrated engine (chosen)** — the invariant above.
